352.text: This occurrence matches the term's usual adverbial sense of zealous/earnest effort, consistent with its ordinary classical and NT usage; no divergence.

353.text: Earnestly is not itself the operation word but a manner-qualifier of zēteō; it modifies how Onesiphorus's search toward Paul was conducted, not a separate initiated action.

354.text: From earnestness's own vantage: it qualifies zēteō's (searching) manner/intensity; same party (Onesiphorus), same act — an intensifying, not causal, relation, as already recorded.

605.text: G4709 (spoudaiōs) and G4710 (spoudē) share the same root (spoudē/speudō, 'to hasten') and the same core semantic arc from physical haste/speed to earnest, zealous, energetic effort. Across the subgroup's combined occurrences, both terms are used to intensify acts of seeking or caring for another person (G4709: pleading for the centurion in Luke 7:4, searching for Paul in 2Tim 1:17; G4710: haste to Elizabeth in Luke 1:39, care for the Corinthians placed in Titus's heart in 2Cor 8:16) -- the two members converge tightly on relational/interpersonal earnestness as a shared core sense.

607.text: The subgroup's two members diverge sharply in grammatical range: G4709 is exclusively adverbial (ADV) across all three of its occurrences, always modifying a verb of action (pleaded, searched, do your best/speed) and never functioning as a nameable, possessable quality. This confirms and extends the prior char_subgroup_observation that G4709 is 'exclusively adverbial' -- across its FULL occurrence list this holds without exception, unlike G4710 which is uniformly nominal.

610.text: G4709 never occurs paired in the same verse with G4710 anywhere in the NT corpus given -- the two subgroup members are never co-present in a single verse, so any synergy between them must be established at the strong-comparison level (as done in these observations) rather than observed as direct verse-level combination.

790.text: The relational scope is broad: it includes fellow believers (2Cor 8:16, Titus's care for Corinthians), ministry partners and traveling workers (Titus 3:13, 2Tim 1:17), kin (Luke 1:39), and even those outside the community of faith or covenant (Luke 7:4, elders for a Gentile centurion). No occurrence shows the characteristic explicitly excluding any category of person; where it is withheld, it is due to personal sloth/idleness rather than the exclusion of a class of people.

2458.text: Neh.12.27 'thanksgivings' (plural, amid musical instruments) sits within the base liturgical-song sense of H8426, consistent with its other choir/procession-related occurrences; no notable divergence.

2460.text: In Neh.12.27 H8426 (thanksgivings) co-occurs with M22 (singing) and M04 (gladness); together these three M-codes constitute the compound celebration -- gladness as the emotional state, singing and thanksgivings as its joint musical/verbal expression at the dedication.

2972.text: Across its full occurrence list H8426 clusters into three recurring realizations of one lexeme: (1) the concrete thank-offering sacrifice (Lev.7.12 x2, Lev.7.13, Lev.7.15, Lev.22.29, Ps.50.14, Ps.50.23, Ps.107.22, Ps.116.17, Amos.4.5, Jonah.2.9, 2Chr.29.31 x2, 2Chr.33.16, Jer.17.26, Jer.33.11), (2) the vocal/manner accompaniment of praise, 'with/in thanksgiving' (Ps.69.30, Ps.26.7, Ps.95.2, Ps.100.4, Ps.147.7, Isa.51.3), and (3) the institutional thanksgiving choir/procession/company (Neh.12.27, Neh.12.31, Neh.12.38, Neh.12.40, Ps.42.4). A fourth, rarer sense realizes it as verbal confession (Josh.7.19, Ezra.10.11). This is a single strong showing internally the full sense-range attributed to the subgroup label (hymn, choir, offering) without needing a second member strong to supply any of these senses.

2973.text: Since H8426 is the sole member strong of this subgroup, there is no second lexeme to compare it against directly; the meaningful cross-comparison available is internal -- between H8426's own sacrificial/cultic-object occurrences (e.g. Lev.7.12-15, Lev.22.29, 2Chr.29.31, 2Chr.33.16, Jer.17.26, Jer.33.11, Amos.4.5) versus its choir/procession-as-institution occurrences (Neh.12.27-40, Ps.42.4) versus its purely adverbial/manner occurrences ('with thanksgiving', e.g. Ps.69.30, Ps.95.2, Ps.100.4, Ps.147.7, Ps.26.7). These three groupings do not overlap grammatically: the sacrificial sense is always the head noun or a construct-genitive qualifier of an offering-word (zebach, shelamim), the choir sense functions as a collective-body noun (subject or object of appointment/movement verbs), and the manner sense is marked by a preposition (b-) modifying a separate main verb of praise. No morphological distinction (all occurrences are the same feminine noun stem, singular or plural absolute/construct) drives this three-way split -- it is purely syntactic/contextual, meaning the noun's referent is disambiguated entirely by its syntactic role in each verse rather than by any inflectional change.

3277.text: In Ps.38.12 and 2Sam.4.8 and Prov.29.10 the surface sense diverges from the neutral base gloss 'seek' because it participates in the idiom 'seek my life/his life' -- meaning to seek to kill, not merely to search for or desire. This idiomatic shift carries lethal hostile intent, contrasting against occurrences like 1Kgs.22.8 where the same root (H1875, related seeking root) denotes benign consultation of the Lord.

3278.text: In Ps.38.12 those hostile to the psalmist (the party 'those who seek') initiate the seeking-operation, directed toward the psalmist's life/hurt -- an adversarial party seeking harm against the sole party present as target.

3279.text: In 2Sam.4.8 Saul (as party) is described as having initiated seeking of David's life; the operation is directed by Saul toward David, now reported after the fact by the assassins to David.

3280.text: In Prov.29.10 bloodthirsty men (party) initiate the seeking-operation directed toward the life of the upright (the other party), an adversarial pursuit paralleling the Ps.38.12 pattern.

3281.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Ps.38.12 alongside H1245 seeking; the other tagged words in the verse are role-T or non-cluster tags plus M47 (life), M24/M58 (hurt), M18 (ruin), M84 (meditate), M14 (treachery) -- checking against cluster scope, no additional M-code home-cluster overlap applies to H1245's own vantage beyond noting these are present but distinct; treat as no other M83-relevant relation to build on.

3282.text: In 2Sam.4.8 M-codes M24/M72 (head/king), M47 (life), M06 (enemy), M26 (avenged) co-occur with H1245's seeking; the seeking of David's life by Saul stands as the hostile backdrop that M26 vengeance later answers -- these M-codes describe surrounding persons/status/emotion but are not themselves modified by or dependent on the seeking-operation itself.

3283.text: In Prov.29.10 M06 (hate) and M34 (blameless) and M12 (upright) co-occur with the seeking; the seeking of the upright's life is the outworking of the bloodthirsty men's hatred (M06), showing seeking here as the operational expression of a prior hateful disposition rather than an independent characteristic.

3335.text: In Luke.2.48 the parents (father and mother, the party) initiate the searching-operation, directed toward the child Jesus (the other party) who had gone missing -- a relational, anxious seeking of a person.

3337.text: In Luke.2.48 M48 (astonished) and M24 (great distress/anguish) co-occur; the parents' searching (G2212) is the cause producing their distress (M24) upon finding him, while the astonishment (M48) belongs to the crowd's reaction to the child rather than to the search itself -- related in narrative sequence but not characteristics of the seeking-act itself.

3376.text: In Zeph.2.3 all three occurrences of baqash sit squarely within the base gloss 'seek' (the Lord, righteousness, humility) with no surface divergence -- straightforward imperative use.

3378.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Zeph.2.3 alongside baqash (the co-occurring M12 righteousness and M05 humility terms are the OBJECTS sought, not separate characteristics of the seeker in this verse's role tagging) -- baqash stands as the operative seeking-act relating to those pursued qualities.

3379.text: In Ezra.8.22 other M-codes are present (M07 shame, M23 power, M02 wrath) but none bears a direct dependency relation to the seeking-act itself within this verse's syntax; baqash names the condition under which God's hand is described as good.

3381.text: In 1Kgs.1.2 no other M-code characteristic is present in the verse's role tags apart from the seeking-act itself (M83); the surrounding vocabulary is untagged narrative detail.

3382.text: In Ezra.8.22, seeking (baqash) is directed by 'all who seek him' (worshippers, generic party) toward God (party H0430G), contrasted with those who forsake him -- the operation runs from human party toward the divine party as its object.

3383.text: In Zeph.2.3, the seeking operation is initiated by 'the humble of the land' (addressed party) and directed toward the Lord, and secondarily toward righteousness and humility as sought qualities.

3385.text: In 1Kgs.1.2, the seeking operation is initiated by the servants (party) directed toward finding a young woman for the king (party, the lord/king), i.e. an instrumental search on the king's behalf.

3401.text: In 2Chr.25.15, other M-codes present (M02 anger, M43 prophet, M45 deliver) frame the narrative context (the Lord's anger, sending a prophet) but do not structurally modify the seeking-act itself; darash here names Amaziah's culpable act of seeking foreign gods, the object of divine anger.

3402.text: In Ps.10.4 darash (negated: 'does not seek') occupies the negative pole of the cluster's dual seeking-motif, paired with M08 pride and M58 wickedness in the same verse -- the wicked's pride is what suppresses the seeking-act, making darash's absence diagnostic of the wicked disposition.

3406.text: In 2Chr.25.15, the seeking operation is initiated by Amaziah (party) directed toward foreign gods (party/object), the very act that provokes the Lord's anger.

3409.text: In Ps.10.4, the seeking operation (negated) is attributed to 'the wicked' (party) with God as its withheld object -- the wicked initiates no such act toward God.

3460.text: In Lev.10.16 the doubled construction ('diligently inquired') intensifies the base sense of investigation but does not shift its meaning beyond the term's ordinary procedural-inquiry sense; in Ps.77.2 the term sits within its standard devotional-seeking sense (seeking the Lord in trouble). Neither occurrence diverges from the base gloss.

3462.text: In Ps.77.2, other M-codes present are M24 (trouble/distress), M73 (wearying), M30 (refuses), M11/M45 (comforted) -- H1875's seeking of the Lord is set within a context of unresolved distress and refusal of comfort; the seeking is the psalmist's persistent response amid these other conditions, but does not resolve them within this verse.

3476.text: In Esth.2.21, 1Sam.24.9, Num.35.23, and 1Kgs.20.7 the surface sense shifts from the base gloss 'seek/desire' toward a conspiratorial/hostile sense 'to plot against, seek to harm/kill' -- a marked negative-valence divergence from the neutral-to-positive base gloss. By contrast in 2Chr.15.4 the surface sense aligns with the base devotional gloss (seeking God). This shows the same lexeme's stepGloss splits sharply by direction of the object across these occurrences.

3477.text: In Jer.19.9 and Ezek.7.25 the sense stays within the base gloss range (seeking life to destroy it; seeking peace that will not be found) without further nuance shift beyond what the object noun already conveys.

3478.text: Esth.2.21: the operation-tagged word 'lay' (H7971K, role-T3) co-occurs with party-tagged 'hands' (H3027G) and 'King' (H4428G); the conspirators (Bigthan and Teresh, having 'sought'/H1245) initiate the operation of laying hands, directed at King Ahasuerus.

3479.text: Num.35.23: the operation word 'dropped' (H5307G, role-T3, tagged M02) is directed by the unwitting agent ('he') toward the victim ('him'), resulting in death; H1245's seeking (of harm) is explicitly negated in this verse ('did not seek his harm'), clarifying the dropping was accidental, not an intentional operation flowing from a hostile seeking.

3480.text: 1Kgs.20.7: the operation word 'sent' (H7971G, role-T3) is initiated by Ben-hadad (implied 'he') and directed 'to me' (the king of Israel), demanding wives, children, silver and gold; this sending is the concrete operation behind the accusation that he is 'seeking trouble' (H1245).

3481.text: In Esth.2.21, M02 (angry) precedes and motivates H1245's plotting-seeking; the anger of the eunuchs is the disposition, the seeking is the resultant hostile operation directed at the king -- H1245 supplies the active pursuit-phase that M02's anger sets in motion.

3482.text: In Jer.19.9, M47 (flesh/soul) and M06 (enemies) and M24 (distress) surround H1245's seeking; here the seeking is the enemies' predatory pursuit of 'their life' (M47), set within a broader scene of siege-distress (M24) -- H1245 names the active hostile pursuit that converts the surrounding distress into mortal danger.

3483.text: In 2Chr.15.4, M06/M23/M24 (distress) precedes and M11/M81 (turned) accompanies H1245's seeking of the Lord; the sequence shows distress prompting a turning which is enacted as seeking -- H1245 is the devotional-pursuit phase of the turning-in-distress pattern, distinct from the turning (M11/M81) itself.

3484.text: In Ezek.7.25, M24 (anguish) precedes and M33 (peace) is the object of H1245's seeking; the verse shows seeking-in-anguish for peace that will not be found -- H1245 is the futile pursuit-response to the anguish, with M33 naming its unattainable object.

3485.text: In Num.35.23, M02 ('dropped', tagged as an anger-related code) co-occurs with H1245's negated seeking ('did not seek his harm'); the verse explicitly denies hostile intent (H1245 negated) even though the fatal act (tagged M02) occurred, distinguishing accidental action from malicious pursuit.

3486.text: In 1Sam.24.9 and 1Kgs.20.7 the only other M-code present is M58/M24 ('harm'/'trouble', the object sought); H1245 names the act of pursuit whose object is itself named by the M24/M58 term -- the two are tightly bound as verb-and-object within the same accusation.

3500.text: The occurrence in Hos.5.15 sits within the base gloss of 'seek earnestly/early' with no further contextual shift; the surrounding language (acknowledging guilt, distress) intensifies the scene but does not alter the word's own core sense.

3501.text: In Hos.5.15, M56 (guilt, 'acknowledge their guilt') and M02/M50 (face) and M06/M23/M24 (distress) co-occur with H7836; the verse's sequence shows guilt-acknowledgment (M56) and distress (M24) as the preconditions that provoke the earnest seeking (H7836) of God's face (M02/M50) -- H7836 is the culminating penitential response to the preceding conditions named by the other M-codes, paired alongside H1245 ('seek my face') as a doublet of seeking-verbs in the same verse.

3536.text: In Esth.9.2 'sought' (participle, construct with 'their harm') sits within the base sense of seeking-to-find/secure applied to a hostile object; no divergence from the general gloss.

3537.text: In Ps.40.14, Ps.70.2, Ps.71.13, and Ps.71.24 'seek' functions in the stock formulaic phrase 'those who seek my life/hurt' -- fully within the base gloss's hostile-pursuit sense, consistent across all four occurrences with no unique nuance.

3538.text: In Jer.45.5, 'seek great things for yourself' shifts the sense toward ambition/self-aggrandizement rather than search or hostile pursuit -- a distinct nuance (worldly ambition) compared to the hostile-pursuit sense dominant in the Psalms occurrences and the neutral/malicious sense in Esth.9.2 and Jer.38.4.

3539.text: M23/M72 (hand/king-authority) and M01 (fear) are present in this verse but relate to the narrative's power dynamics, not to the seeking itself; H1245 here characterizes the enemy's hostile intent (seeking harm) which is thwarted, distinct from and unconnected to those authority/fear M-codes.

3540.text: M07 (shame/disappointment, via H0954/H2659/H3637) is the fate wished upon those who 'seek' (H1245) the psalmist's life; the seeking (this cluster) is the malicious cause, and M07 is the desired consequence -- a cause-effect relational pairing across the verse.

3541.text: As in Ps.40.14, the seeking (H1245) of the psalmist's life is paired with M07 (shame/confusion) as the desired reversal -- same relational pattern repeated in this near-duplicate psalm.

3542.text: H1245 (seek my hurt) again pairs with M07 (shame, scorn, disgrace) as the imprecated consequence on the seekers; M06 (accusers) additionally identifies the agent-class doing the seeking, tightening the relational web around the hostile-pursuit sense.

3543.text: Here the seeking (H1245, 'sought to do me hurt') is reported as already having resulted in the seekers' shame (M07) -- the causal pairing seen in Ps.40/70/71.13 is now narrated as fulfilled, and M12 (righteousness, H6666) is introduced as the psalmist's own vindicating quality contrasted against the failed seekers, adding a new relational thread beyond the shame-pairing.

3544.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in Jer.45.5 that meaningfully relates to H1245's ambition-sense here beyond the general narrative; the verse's other tagged items (Lord, life, disaster) are not M-coded characteristics.

3558.text: In 2Cor.13.3, 'seek proof' shifts zeteo toward a forensic/evidentiary sense (demanding demonstration) rather than the general 'look for/desire' gloss -- a demand-nuance distinct from Gal.1.10's approval-seeking and Gal.2.17's endeavor-sense.

3561.text: The operation 'speaking' (G2980, T3, Christ speaking in Paul) co-occurs with the party Christ and the seeking-party 'you' who seek proof (G2212); the seeking is directed AT Christ/Paul as its object, demanding evidence of Christ's speaking-operation.

3562.text: M35 (proof, G1382) and M73 (weak, G0770G) co-occur but relate to Christ's demonstrated power, not directly to the seeking itself beyond being its object; no direct characteristic-to-characteristic relation beyond object-of-seeking.

3578.text: In Jer.38.4, darash is used not in its more common cultic/oracular-inquiry sense but in the 'care for, seek with application' sense applied to political/social welfare ('seeking the welfare of this people') -- a civic-care nuance distinct from the term's more frequent devotional usage elsewhere in the OT.

3579.text: The operation 'weakening' (H7503, T3/M24) is what the officials (party) accuse the man of doing to the soldiers' hands; H1875 (seeking) is embedded in the officials' claim that he is NOT seeking the people's welfare -- the negated seeking-operation stands opposed to the weakening-operation as the officials' charge against him.

3580.text: M33 (welfare, H7965I) and M24/M58 (harm, H7451C) are the direct antithetical objects governed by H1875's negated seeking in this verse -- the officials frame the accused as failing to seek M33 and instead effectively producing M24, making H1875 the pivotal verb linking these two opposed M-codes as alternatives.

3614.text: Phil.2.21 uses zeteo in its base 'seek/pursue interests' sense with no notable divergence from the general stepGloss -- self-interest-seeking is a standard application of the verb.

3615.text: Col.3.1 uses zeteo as an imperative command to seek heavenly/spiritual realities -- this sits within the verb's attested 'seek, strive for' sense (cf. Mt.6.33) with no unusual surface divergence, though it carries elevated theological weight via its object 'things above'.

3616.text: 1Thess.2.6 uses zeteo in the standard 'seek glory/honor from people' sense, matching the base gloss's 'desire, strive for' -- no unusual nuance beyond ordinary application to social honor-seeking.

3617.text: In Phil.2.21, other role tags present (T7/T8 on Jesus/Christ) are person-tags, not other M-code characteristics; no other M-code characteristic co-occurs, so seeking stands as the sole characteristic-word.

3618.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in Col.3.1 alongside seeking; the verse's other tagged words are T-role/party tags (Christ, God) not M-code characteristics.

3619.text: 1Thess.2.6 co-occurs seeking (M83) with 'glory' (M22) and 'made demands/burden' (M78, not this cluster's own). From seeking's vantage: the negated seeking-of-glory here functions to set up a contrast pole, denying that the apostles' pursuit was oriented toward self-honor or burdening others -- seeking's absence of a self-interested object is the point, distinguishing it from the M22 glory-term it is paired with by negation.

3620.text: Phil.2.21: zeteo itself is not tagged role-T3 (Operation) in this verse's role list -- it carries only the M83 cluster tag, so no D7.7.1 operation-relation applies to this word here.

3621.text: Col.3.1: zeteo is not itself role-T3 tagged (only M83); the verse's operation words are 'raised' and 'seated' (both T3), directed at the addressee/Christ respectively, but these are not the home strong -- no D7.7.1 relation recorded for zeteo itself.

3622.text: 1Thess.2.6: zeteo carries no role-T3 tag in this verse's role list (only M83), so no operation-relation is recorded for this home strong here.

3639.text: Ps.22.26 'those who seek him' uses darash in its worshipful/devotional sense (seeking God in praise and satisfaction) rather than the oracular-inquiry sense dominant in the Kings narratives -- here the nuance is communal, joyful seeking tied to being satisfied and praising, showing the term's range extending to worship-postures beyond formal consultation.

3643.text: Ps.22.26 co-occurs darash (seek) with M09 (afflicted), M45 (satisfied), M08/M16/M22 (praise), M47 (hearts), M34 (forever). From inquiring's vantage: seeking the Lord here is the PRECONDITION for the sequence of affliction being resolved into satisfaction and praise -- seeking initiates the chain that other M-codes in this verse then complete (satisfaction, praise, enduring life), rather than being a mere co-occurring quality.

3647.text: Ps.22.26: the seeking is initiated by 'those who seek him' (the afflicted worshippers, generic party) and directed toward the Lord (T7/T10 party), the object of both seeking and subsequent praise.

3661.text: 2Sam.5.17 'search for David' carries a hostile-pursuit nuance beyond neutral 'seeking to find' -- the Philistines seek David militarily, intending to capture or kill him, paralleling the NT Hebraism 'seek the soul' noted for zeteo; this military-hostile sense is a notable narrowing from the base 'seek' gloss, and recurs identically in the parallel 1Chr.14.8 account.

3662.text: 1Chr.14.8 parallels 2Sam.5.17 exactly: baqash 'search for David' retains the same hostile-military nuance (Philistines seeking David to attack), consistent across both accounts of the same event -- no additional divergence beyond what is noted at 2Sam.5.17.

3663.text: 1Sam.10.2 'went to seek' the donkeys sits squarely within baqash's ordinary practical-search sense (seeking a lost object) -- no notable divergence from the base gloss, contrasting with the hostile-pursuit nuance seen in 2Sam.5.17/1Chr.14.8.

3664.text: 2Sam.5.17 co-occurs baqash (search) with M41 (heard) and M72 (king/anointed). From seeking's vantage: the Philistines' searching is triggered directly by their HEARING of David's anointing as king -- seeking here is the response-action to news of a rival's elevated status, showing search-behaviour causally chained to the hearing/kingship complex rather than standing independently.

3665.text: 1Chr.14.8 co-occurs baqash (search) with M41 (heard) and M72 (king/anointed), identical structure to 2Sam.5.17. From seeking's vantage: the same causal chain holds (hearing of David's kingship triggers the search), reinforcing that in the Chronicles parallel, seeking is again reactive rather than independently initiated.

3666.text: 1Sam.10.2 co-occurs baqash (seek, of the donkeys) with M59 (ceased/H5203, front-loaded), M65 (care/H1697I, front-loaded), M20 (anxious/H1672, front-loaded). From seeking's vantage: the son's original errand of SEEKING donkeys is now supplanted in the father's mind by anxious care for the SON himself -- seeking here functions as the narrative pretext that ironically gives way to a father's relational anxiety, though seeking itself is not modified by the other M-codes present.

3667.text: 2Sam.5.17: baqash (search, role-T3-adjacent operation) is initiated by the Philistines (T10/T11 party) and directed toward David (T8 party) as the object of the search -- a hostile pursuit operation.

3668.text: 1Chr.14.8: identical structure to 2Sam.5.17 -- baqash is initiated by the Philistines (T10/T11 party) and directed toward David (T8 party) as the sought target.

3669.text: 1Sam.10.2: baqash (seek) is initiated by the addressee ('you' -- Saul, in the reported speech) and directed toward the donkeys (an object, not a party) -- a mundane recovery-operation rather than an interpersonal one.

3694.text: Used here in the negated imperative 'do not be alarmed' addressed to the women at the tomb, matching its standard sense of amazement/distress at a supernatural sight; no divergence from base gloss.

3706.text: Used substantivally as the object of 'seek' contrasted with evil; matches base gloss of moral good with no special nuance shift.

3710.text: In each of these three narrative verses yare' carries its plain sense of ordinary fear of danger/threat (David's men, Jehoshaphat, Uriah), not the reverential-awe sense; no notable shift from base gloss across the set.

3714.text: Used of fire 'breaking out' as judgment imagery in the conditional warning tied to not seeking the Lord; matches base sense of sudden rushing.

3732.text: The women's 'seeking Jesus' at the tomb is a literal physical search for a person, sitting squarely within the base sense of zeteo (look for/search after) with no unusual idiomatic shift.

3733.text: No prior context recorded for this verse. G1568 (alarm/amazement, M01) co-occurs but names an emotional reaction unrelated to the act of seeking itself; the women's seeking of Jesus is a separate action from their fear-response, so no direct relational tie between the two M-codes here.

3734.text: The operation-word 'seek' (role-T3-tagged in some contexts, here the verse's action word) is initiated by the women (implied subject, addressed 'you') and directed toward Jesus of Nazareth (party-tagged, T7/T8), the object of their search.

3749.text: In 1Sam.22.23 and Jer.26.21 baqash carries the idiomatic hostile sense 'seek the life/put to death' rather than neutral searching -- a lethal-intent nuance markedly different from ordinary seeking, consistent across both occurrences.

3751.text: No prior context recorded. In 1Sam.22.23 baqash (seeks life) co-occurs with M01 (afraid) and M47 (life/soul) and M26 (safekeeping); this characteristic's vantage adds that the seeking is the THREAT-action which explains why fear (M01) is raised and why safekeeping (M26) is offered as its counter-response.

3752.text: No prior context recorded. In Jer.26.21 baqash (sought to kill) co-occurs with M41 (heard) and M01 (afraid); this characteristic's vantage adds that the king's seeking is the causal trigger producing Uriah's fear and flight, sequencing the other M-codes around this one active pursuit.

3754.text: The operation 'seeks' is initiated by an unnamed hostile party (implied Saul) and directed toward David's/Abiathar's life, the party under threat.

3755.text: The operation 'sought' is initiated by King Jehoiakim and directed toward Jeremiah (implied 'him'), whom the king seeks to put to death.

3769.text: In Ps.69.32 'you who seek God' matches the base devotional-seeking gloss directly, naming worshippers whose hearts are to revive; no divergent nuance.

3770.text: In Amos 5:4,6,14 the repeated imperative 'Seek [the Lord/good] and live' sits squarely within the devotional/covenantal base sense, with 'live' making explicit the life-outcome inherent to darash's promise-register; consistent across all three occurrences.

3772.text: In 2Chr.20.3 'set his face to seek the Lord' combines darash with the idiom 'set the face,' intensifying but not diverging from the devotional-seeking base sense; standard usage.

3773.text: No prior context recorded. In Ps.69.32 darash (seek God) co-occurs with M09 (humble), M04 (glad), M47 (heart), M25 (revive); this characteristic's vantage adds that seeking God is the ACT that produces the gladness and heart-revival named by the other M-codes -- the causal center of the verse's chain.

3774.text: No prior context recorded. In Amos.5.4 darash co-occurs with M25 (live); this characteristic's vantage adds that seeking functions as the CONDITION for the life named by M25, a conditional-covenantal pairing.

3775.text: No prior context recorded. In Amos.5.6 darash co-occurs with M25 (live) and M46 (break out/fire); this characteristic's vantage adds that failure implied by not-seeking triggers the destructive outbreak (M46), making seeking the preventive counter-action to judgment.

3776.text: No prior context recorded. In Amos.5.14 darash co-occurs with M05/M18 (good), M24/M58 (evil), M25 (live); this characteristic's vantage adds that seeking is the verb governing the moral choice between the two named opposites (good vs evil), making it the pivot-action of the verse.

3778.text: No prior context recorded. In 2Chr.20.3 darash co-occurs with M01 (afraid), M02/M50 (face), M42 (proclaimed); this characteristic's vantage adds that seeking the Lord is Jehoshaphat's active RESPONSE to fear, converting the fear-state into a directed devotional action.

3779.text: Ps.69.32 has no separate role-T3 operation word distinct from the seeking act itself co-occurring with a clear party tag beyond 'God'; the seeking verb functions as its own operation here with God as the party sought (initiator: the humble worshippers; directed toward: God).

3780.text: The operation 'Seek' is initiated by the addressed house of Israel (2nd person plural imperative) and directed toward the Lord/God, the party to be sought.

3781.text: The operation 'Seek' is initiated by the addressed people and directed toward the Lord, with the alternative consequence (fire breaking out) directed toward the house of Joseph if unheeded.

3782.text: The operation 'Seek' is initiated by the addressed people and directed toward 'good' (the moral object), with the Lord of hosts as the responding party who will be with them.

3784.text: The operation 'seek' is initiated by Jehoshaphat and directed toward the Lord, prompted by his fear.

3799.text: In Hos.3.5 bāqaš is used in its central sense of seeking God/covenant restoration, squarely within the base gloss; no notable divergence from ordinary usage.

3800.text: In Prov.17.11 bāqaš is used of an evil man's habitual pursuit of rebellion; this sits within the base gloss's 'desire, demand' sense (a negative object rather than a divergent form), so no surface-form shift is present -- the negativity comes from the object 'rebellion', not from the verb's own nuance.

3801.text: In Hos.3.5, bāqaš (seek) co-occurs with H6342 (fear) and other M-coded terms (H1732 David/king M72, H0430 God/Lord T10/T7) but these are role-classification tags (T-codes) not M-codes with home membership here; among genuine M-code characteristics present, seeking the Lord functions as the initiating disposition that precedes and enables the subsequent 'fear/awe' response toward the Lord and his goodness -- the two are sequential rather than overlapping in this verse's own action.

3802.text: In Prov.17.11, bāqaš (seek) co-occurs with M24/M58 (evil man) and M30 (rebellion) and M10 (cruel messenger); the seeking here is the operative link between the evil disposition (M24/M58) and its object (rebellion, M30) -- the evil man's character finds active expression through the act of seeking, while the cruel messenger (M10) is the resulting consequence, not something seeking itself connects to directly.

3803.text: H1245 (seek) is not tagged role-T3 in either Hos.3.5 or Prov.17.11 in the role list provided (it carries only M83); the role-T3 operation tags in these verses belong to other strongs (H7725 return, H7971 sent), so D7.7.1 does not apply to this home strong directly in these verses.

3816.text: In Matt.2.20 'sought the child's life' the surface sense of zēteō diverges from its base gloss 'seek/look for' into the Hebraic idiom meaning 'sought to kill'; the nuance here carries lethal hostile intent, not neutral searching, and is distinct from the term's other occurrences in this batch (e.g. Mark.1.37 crowds simply looking for Jesus, or Luke.11.9's positive spiritual-seeking imperative).

3817.text: In Matt.2.13 'search for the child, to destroy him' zēteō carries its plain physical-search sense reinforced by the following purpose infinitive apolesai (destroy); no divergence within the verb itself beyond its ordinary range.

3819.text: In Luke.11.9 zēteō is a direct imperative parallel to ask/knock, within its ordinary volitional-seeking sense; no divergence.

3820.text: In Luke.11.24 the unclean spirit 'seeking rest' personifies zēteō as a restless drive toward a place of habitation; the nuance shifts from ordinary human searching to a figurative, almost compulsive wandering-need, distinct from the deliberate demand-sense in the sign-seeking occurrences (Mark.8.12, Matt.12.39, Luke.11.29).

3821.text: In Matt.2.13, zēteō (search) co-occurs with M10 (destroy/apollymi); the search here functions as the preparatory operation whose completion enables the destructive act -- zēteō names the investigative means, M10 names the intended lethal end.

3822.text: In Matt.2.20, M47 (life/psychē) is present but functions purely as the grammatical object of zēteō within the fixed idiom 'seek the life,' not as an independent characteristic in tension or cooperation with seeking; no other M-code characteristic operates alongside seeking here.

3824.text: In Luke.11.9, zēteō (seek) co-occurs with M21 (ask); both are commanded parallel spiritual postures (ask/seek/knock) toward God, complementary rather than one modifying the other -- seeking adds the dimension of active pursuit alongside asking's dimension of verbal request.

3825.text: In Luke.11.24, zēteō (seeking) co-occurs with M10c (unclean), M47 (spirit), and M33 (rest); the unclean spirit's seeking is directed at obtaining rest -- seeking functions as the operative link between the spirit's unclean nature and its unmet goal of rest, showing restlessness as consequence of uncleanness rather than seeking itself carrying the moral valence.

3826.text: In Matt.2.13, zēteō is tagged role-T3 (operation) with Herod as the initiating party, directed toward the child (party present as object); the angel's prior command to flee frames this search as a hostile pursuit to be evaded.

3827.text: In Matt.2.20, zēteō (sought) is role-T3, initiated by 'those who sought the child's life' (unnamed hostile party, successors of Herod) and directed at the child -- now resolved as they are dead, permitting return.

3829.text: In Luke.11.9, zēteō (seek) is role-T3, an imperative from Jesus to 'you' (disciples/hearers) directing them to seek, with the implicit divine addressee as the one from whom finding results.

3830.text: In Luke.11.24, zēteō (seeking) is role-T3, initiated by the unclean spirit and directed toward 'rest' as its sought object, in the waterless places it passes through.

3881.text: In Luke.13.6 the vineyard owner (party) is both initiator and subject of 'came seeking' (zēteō) fruit on the fig tree; the operation is directed toward the tree/fruit as object, expressing an expectation of the tree bearing produce for its owner.

3882.text: In Luke.13.24 'many' (party) are the initiators of 'will seek' (zēteō) to enter the narrow door, directed toward the goal of entry itself; the operation fails because ability (ischyō) is lacking.

3883.text: In John.1.38 Jesus (party) initiates the question 'What are you seeking?' addressed to the disciples following him, making them the target party whose zēteō-activity is being probed; the operation is verbal inquiry directed at the followers' own seeking.

3884.text: In John.6.26 the crowd (party) is the subject of 'you are seeking me' with Jesus as the object sought, though Jesus reframes the true motive as bread rather than signs; the operation is directed from the crowd toward Jesus' person.

3886.text: In John.7.25 'they' (unnamed hostile party, implicitly the authorities) are the initiators of 'seek to kill' directed at 'this man' (Jesus) as target, zēteō here carrying lethal intent paired with apokteinō.

3887.text: In John.11.8 the Jews (party) are named as initiators of 'seeking' directed toward 'you' (Jesus) with intent to stone him, reported by the disciples as reason for caution.

3889.text: In John.13.33 Jesus (party, speaker) predicts 'you will seek me' -- the disciples become future initiators of zēteō directed toward Jesus' person after his departure, paralleling what he earlier said to the Jews.

3910.text: In Luke.13.6 'seeking' fruit sits squarely within zēteō's base gloss of ordinary physical searching -- no notable divergence from the general stepGloss.

3911.text: In Luke.13.24 'will seek to enter' matches the base gloss of striving/attempting -- straightforward volitional-effort sense with no special divergence.

3912.text: In John.1.38 'What are you seeking?' is a direct, literal use of zēteō asking about the disciples' immediate purpose -- within the base gloss, no shift.

3913.text: In John.6.26 zēteō carries an ironic nuance: the crowd's 'seeking' Jesus is exposed by him as motivated by physical satisfaction (bread) rather than genuine pursuit of his person/signs -- a divergence toward self-interested seeking rather than devoted seeking, distinct from its more earnest uses elsewhere (e.g. Jn 1:38).

3915.text: In John.7.25 zēteō pairs with apokteinō ('seek to kill') giving the term a lethal-intent nuance well beyond its neutral 'search for' base gloss -- an idiomatic hostile extension paralleling the Hebraic 'seek the life of' construction, distinguishing this occurrence from the more neutral seeking in John.1.38 or Luke.13.6.

3916.text: In John.11.8 zēteō again carries the lethal-intent nuance ('seeking to stone you'), matching John.7.25's hostile extension rather than the neutral base sense of searching.

3918.text: In John.13.33 'You will seek me' echoes Jesus' earlier words to the Jews (Jn 7:34) about seeking him after his departure -- a future, longing-for-presence sense within the base gloss, no unusual divergence beyond its established Johannine usage pattern.

3927.text: In Luke.13.6 the only M-code present is M83 (zēteō, 'seeking'); other tagged items are T-coded roles (parable, fig tree, vineyard, fruit), so zēteō is the sole characteristic here.

3928.text: In Luke.13.24 M23 (ischyō, 'able') co-occurs alongside M83 (zēteō, 'seek'). From M83's vantage, the seeking-to-enter precedes and is distinct from the capacity question raised by M23 -- many will seek entry but the text separates the act of seeking from the outcome of ability, so the two characteristics describe sequential but not overlapping aspects of the same event.

3929.text: In John.1.38 M63 (hermēneuō, 'means/interpret') co-occurs with M83 (zēteō, 'seeking') but the two operate in separate clauses -- M83 governs Jesus' question to the followers, M63 explains the term 'Rabbi'; from M83's vantage the seeking-inquiry is unrelated to the interpretive gloss on the title.

3930.text: In John.6.26 M41 (apokrinomai, 'answered') and M15 (eidon/'saw', cognitive perception) and M43 (sēmeion, 'signs') co-occur with M83 (zēteō). From M83's vantage, the crowd's seeking is the topic Jesus' answering (M41) addresses and corrects, contrasting their seeking-motive against what they actually 'saw' (M15) -- the seeking is shown to be misdirected toward bread rather than the signs.

3931.text: In John.13.33 the only M-code present is M83 (zēteō, 'seek'); no other M-code characteristic co-occurs in this verse.

3932.text: In John.11.8 M83 (zēteō, 'seeking') co-occurs with no other M-code tag among the role list here (the disciples/Jews/stoning-verb are T-coded); confirmed sole M-code presence.

3947.text: In Luke.13.24 'Strive' uses agōnizomai's general 'exert oneself/struggle' sense with an infinitive, matching its base gloss with no unusual divergence.

3975.text: In John.1.38 hermēneuō is used in its standard translation-gloss sense ('which means Teacher'), matching the base gloss with no notable divergence.

3989.text: In Luke.13.24 'will not be able' uses ischyō's standard modal-capacity sense ('to have power/be able'), matching the base gloss with no notable divergence.

4003.text: Pilate's seeking to release Jesus sits squarely within the base gloss of zeteo as volitional pursuit/effort — no notable divergence from the ordinary sense of 'seeking to accomplish' an action.

4004.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in this verse (only role-T tags on other words besides M83 itself; M59/M42/M05/M63 tags appear but M-code cluster words here are role-marked as non-home, not co-present home M-codes for relational linkage purposes at this pass). Recording as no-direct-connection since M59, M42, M05, M63 tags are visible on other words in the verse though not this cluster's own concern.

4005.text: The operation-word 'sought' (zeteo) is initiated by Pilate (the party-tagged subject) and directed toward releasing 'him' (Jesus, the accusative object) — Pilate seeks Jesus' release, positioning Pilate as agent and Jesus as the object of the operation's aim.

4006.text: In John 20:15 Jesus asks Mary 'whom are you seeking' (zeteo) — plain literal search for a missing person, squarely within the base gloss, no divergence.

4007.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in this verse's role list at the home-cluster level; M03, M15, M72 appear on other words but are not this cluster's own home strongs, and no prior relational context exists to build on.

4008.text: The operation 'seeking' is initiated by Mary (addressed as 'you') and directed toward the missing body of Jesus ('whom') — Jesus as questioner surfaces the operation, but the seeker-party is Mary, the sought object is Jesus/his body.

4022.text: In Acts 15:17 (quoting Amos 9:12 LXX) ekzeteo carries the nuance of the Gentiles' eschatological, corporate turning to seek the Lord — a diligent/earnest theological seeking rather than casual search, its impact here universalizing the seek-motif beyond Israel; this contrasts with other occurrences where ekzeteo denotes legal demand (Luke 11:50f) or personal supplication (Heb 12:17).

4023.text: Other M-code tags present in this verse (M72, M42) belong to other clusters (Lord-title, calling/naming) and are not directly related to the seeking-action from this cluster's vantage point; ekzeteo names the approach toward the Lord while the M42/M72 words name the Lord's own identity and calling of the Gentiles — parallel but distinct functions.

4024.text: The operation 'seek' is initiated by the remnant of mankind and all the Gentiles (party-tagged group), directed toward 'the Lord' as the sought object — establishing a movement from the human party toward the divine party.

4025.text: In Rom 10:20 (quoting Isa 65:1) zeteo appears negated ('those who did not seek me') describing Gentiles who had NOT been actively pursuing God, yet God was found by them anyway — the nuance here is that the normal expectation of seeking-precedes-finding is inverted; God's self-disclosure precedes and exceeds human seeking, a theologically loaded divergence from the ordinary active-pursuit sense, contrasting with Acts 15:17 where the nations DO seek the Lord.

4026.text: Other M-code words present (M23 'bold') belong to a different cluster (boldness of Isaiah's speech) and are not directly related to the seeking-motif itself; the two operate on separate planes (Isaiah's boldness vs. the Gentiles' non-seeking).

4027.text: The operation 'seek' (negated) here is attributed to 'those who did not seek me' — the human party (Gentiles) as would-be initiators, directed toward God ('me') as object, but the negation itself marks the reversal: God is the one who acts (found, shown) despite the absence of seeking by the human party.

4041.text: In Heb 11:14 epizeteo describes the patriarchs' collective, ongoing seeking of a 'homeland' — a figurative, eschatological longing (for the heavenly city) rather than a literal search for a lost object; the nuance shifts the term toward a theological pilgrim-motif, contrasting with its use for demanding a sign (Matt 12:39) or anxious daily care (Matt 6:32) elsewhere.

4042.text: The co-occurring M-code M05 (clear/manifest, from emphanizo) describes the outward evidence of the patriarchs' confession, while this cluster's epizeteo names the inward longing itself — related in the verse's logic (confession reveals seeking) but distinct functions, not duplicative.

4043.text: The operation 'seeking' is initiated by 'people who speak thus' (the patriarchs/faithful, party-tagged) and directed toward 'a homeland' as the sought object — establishing a movement from the human party toward an as-yet-unattained goal.

4057.text: In Ps 40:16 'all who seek you' sits within the base religious-seeking sense (worshippers seeking God), matching baqash's well-attested devotional idiom without further nuance-shift.

4058.text: Other M-code words present (M04 rejoice/glad, M51 love, M45 salvation, M22 great) describe the worshippers' emotional and devotional responses that flow FROM seeking God but are not themselves the seeking-act; this cluster's vantage adds that baqash names the initiating approach which these other characteristics presuppose as their occasion.

4059.text: The operation 'seek' is initiated by 'all who' (the worshipping party) and directed toward 'you' (God, the second party) — establishing the human-to-divine approach that grounds the psalm's praise.

4060.text: Ps 70:4 duplicates Ps 40:16's phrase 'all who seek you' with baqash in the identical devotional idiom — no divergence from the base gloss.

4061.text: As in the parallel Ps 40:16, other M-codes present (M04 rejoice/glad, M51 love, M79 salvation, M22 great) name responses flowing from the act of seeking God rather than the seeking-act itself; this cluster's vantage adds that baqash marks the initiating approach that occasions the joy and praise named by those other characteristics.

4062.text: The operation 'seek' is initiated by 'all who' (worshippers, human party) and directed toward 'you' (God, divine party) — the same human-to-divine directional pattern as in Ps 40:16.

4122.text: In Song 5.6, 1Chr 16.10, Ps 105.3, and Isa 45.19 the surface gloss 'sought/seek/Seek' sits squarely within the base sense of active searching/desiring with no notable divergence.

4123.text: No other M-code characteristic is tagged in Song.5.6 alongside H1245's seeking.

4124.text: No other M-code characteristic is tagged in Isa.45.19 alongside H1245's seeking (the vain-seeking of oracles from Jacob's offspring stands alone as the M-code element).

4126.text: No other M-code characteristic is tagged in Ps.105.3 alongside H1245's seeking of the Lord.

4128.text: In Song.5.6, H1245 (sought) is an operation initiated by the female speaker ('I sought him'), directed toward her absent beloved -- a party present by reference though physically gone; the operation fails ('found him not').

4129.text: In Isa.45.19, H1245 (Seek) is an imperative operation attributed by the Lord to the offspring of Jacob, directed toward himself ('Seek me') -- but the Lord denies having commanded it 'in vain', so the operation's directedness is negated/contrasted rather than affirmed.

4131.text: In 1Chr.16.10 and Ps.105.3, H1245 (seek) is an operation initiated by worshippers ('those who seek'), directed toward the Lord as its object.

4146.text: In Esth 10.3 'sought the welfare of his people' diverges markedly from the base cultic/oracular gloss 'inquire of a deity' -- here darash carries a benevolent-pastoral nuance of actively promoting another's good, with clear impact: it frames Mordecai's greatness in terms of care for his people rather than religious consultation, distinguishing this occurrence from the 2Kgs and Ezekiel occurrences where the oracular sense dominates.

4150.text: No other M-code characteristic is tagged in Esth.10.3 alongside H1875's seeking of the people's welfare; the adjacent 'welfare' term (H2896B) carries other M-codes but is not this cluster's home strong.

4154.text: In Esth.10.3, H1875 (sought) is an operation initiated by Mordecai, directed toward the welfare of his people -- a benevolent operation aimed at a collective party's good rather than at a deity.

4181.text: In 1Chr.16.11/Ps.105.4 'Seek [the Lord]...seek his presence' sits squarely within the devotional-consultative base sense; no divergence.

4182.text: In 1Sam.28.7 'inquire' of darash refers specifically to necromantic consultation of a medium/the dead -- a divergence from the general devotional-seeking sense elsewhere in this word's occurrences (e.g. seeking the Lord), carrying a strongly negative, forbidden-practice nuance in this context.

4184.text: In 1Chr.16.11/Ps.105.4, darash ('seek') co-occurs with M83's own H1245 (baqash, also 'seek') and M23 (H5797, strength). The two seeking-verbs together intensify the plea: seeking the Lord's strength AND presence are portrayed as parallel, mutually reinforcing acts of devotion rather than distinct characteristics competing for attention.

4185.text: In 1Sam.28.7, darash ('inquire') co-occurs with no other M-code besides M83's own H1245 ('seek out' a medium); the two M83 members describe successive steps of the same illicit act (fetch, then consult) rather than distinct characteristics interacting.

4199.text: In Deut.13.10 'sought' carries the specific hostile nuance of seeking to seduce/draw Israel away from the Lord (idolatrous incitement), diverging from the neutral 'seek to find/procure' sense seen in 1Sam.16.16 -- here the impact is that seeking becomes an act of religious subversion warranting capital punishment.

4200.text: In 1Sam.23.10 and 2Sam.16.11, 'seeks' collocates with 'life/city' to mean hostile pursuit intending harm or death, a marked narrowing from the neutral base gloss 'seek/require' -- the impact intensifies stakes to mortal danger, distinct from 1Sam.16.16's benign 'seek out a skilled man.'

4201.text: In 1Sam.16.16 ('seek out a man') and 1Sam.28.7 ('Seek out...a woman') and 2Sam.17.20 ('sought and could not find'), the surface sense of procurement/search sits squarely within the base gloss with no notable shift.

4202.text: In Deut.13.10, the operation 'sought' (baqash, role-T3-tagged 'away'/draw-away action paired with it) is initiated by the false enticer (implicit 3ms subject) and directed toward 'you' (the Israelite addressee), aiming to draw them away from the Lord -- an operation of subversive persuasion targeting the covenant party.

4204.text: In 1Sam.23.10, the seeking is initiated by Saul and directed toward David (via the city of Keilah he intends to enter and destroy) -- an operation of hostile pursuit against David as the target party.

4205.text: In 1Sam.28.7, the seeking operation is initiated by Saul (via his servants) and directed toward locating 'a woman who is a medium' -- the medium is the target party of the search.

4206.text: In 2Sam.16.11, the seeking operation is initiated by Absalom (David's son) and directed toward David's own 'life' -- David the speaker is the target party of this hostile pursuit.

4207.text: In 2Sam.17.20, the seeking operation is initiated by Absalom's servants and directed toward finding Ahimaaz and Jonathan, the two fleeing messengers -- an unsuccessful search operation targeting these two parties.

4208.text: In Deut.13.10, M36 (H5650, slavery/servants) is also present but describes Israel's prior condition in Egypt, not the seeking act itself -- the two M-codes co-occur without direct interaction; baqash's own contribution is the depiction of active subversive enticement warranting the death penalty.

4210.text: In 1Sam.23.10, M41 (surely heard) and M55 (destroy) co-occur; baqash's own contribution is that Saul's 'seeking' names the intent/motive behind the reported hearing and the destructive action -- it is the connective verb of hostile purpose linking perception (heard) to intended destruction.

4211.text: In 1Sam.28.7, aside from M83's own two members (baqash and darash), no other M-code characteristic is present.

4212.text: In 2Sam.16.11, M33 (alone/leave) and M47 (life/nephesh) co-occur; baqash's own vantage is that the 'seeking' names the hostile intent against David's life, while M33 describes David's resigned response (leave him alone) -- the two are causally linked but distinct in what each names.

4213.text: In 2Sam.17.20, M02/M08/M56 (crossed over) and M11/M81 (returned) co-occur; baqash's own contribution is that the failed 'sought' names the unsuccessful search operation bracketed between the crossing and the returning, marking the narrative turning point rather than overlapping in meaning with the movement terms.

4227.text: In John.7.4, zeteo takes the sense 'seeks/desires [to be known]' rather than 'seeks [an object/person]' -- a shift toward desiring a state of public recognition. The impact is ironic: the brothers frame Jesus's avoidance of public display as inconsistent with someone truly wanting fame, contrasting with more object-directed occurrences like seeking the kingdom or seeking a lost item.

4228.text: In John.7.4, M23 (G3954, openness/boldness of speech) co-occurs; zeteo's own contribution is that the desire 'to be known' is the motivating cause for which openness/boldness would be the fitting expression -- the brothers argue Jesus's secretive action undercuts the seeking he is presumed to have.

4242.text: In John.7.4 'openly' sits within the base gloss's plain adverbial sense of 'publicly, before all,' matching Mounce/tree's stated Johannine usage; no notable divergence.

4284.text: In 1Sam.23.10 'destroy' sits within the base Hiphil gloss 'to spoil, ruin, destroy' with no notable divergence -- straightforward military destruction sense.

4296.text: In 1Kgs.2.40 'seek his servants' sits squarely within the base gloss of physical searching-to-find; no divergence from the general stepGloss.

4297.text: 2Kgs.2.16 'seek your master' uses the plain search-for-a-missing-person sense, matching the base gloss with no notable shift.

4299.text: Neh.2.10 'come to seek the welfare of the people' uses the benevolent-pursuit sense (seeking good/welfare for others), a well-attested idiomatic extension already covered in the base range; no unusual shift beyond the expected idiom.

4300.text: Ps.119.176 'seek your servant' (imperative addressed to God, following the lost-sheep metaphor) sits within the base search-for-what-is-lost sense; the psalmist casts himself as the sought object, a natural extension with no unusual divergence.

4301.text: Jer.21.7 and Jer.46.26 both use the idiom 'those who seek their life/lives' -- here the base sense of seeking shifts to a lethal-intent nuance (seeking in order to kill), the Hebraism explicitly noted in the meaning tree as carried over into Greek zeteo; this is a marked intensification compared to the neutral or benevolent seeking senses elsewhere in the batch, showing the same root can denote mortal hostility when combined with 'life/soul' as object.

4302.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in 1Kgs.2.40 alongside seeking (servants M36 tag is present but M36 is not flagged as a co-occurring characteristic here in role list); seeking stands as the operative characteristic driving the narrative action.

4303.text: M23/M46 (strength, H2428G) and M47 (spirit, H7307G) co-occur in 2Kgs.2.16 but relate to the Spirit's power lifting Elijah, not to the act of seeking itself; seeking here is the sons-of-prophets' proposed search-action, functionally unrelated to the strength/spirit vocabulary describing the miraculous translation.

4305.text: M58 (displeasure, H7489A/H7451I) co-occurs in Neh.2.10 as the enemies' reaction to Nehemiah's seeking-welfare mission; seeking here is the positive motivating act while displeasure is the hostile response it provokes -- adjacent but distinct characteristics.

4306.text: M76 (going astray, H8582) and M81 (forgetting, H7911) co-occur in Ps.119.176 as the psalmist's confessed condition contrasted with his request that God seek him; seeking functions as the remedy sought FOR the wandering/forgetting condition, an inverse relational pairing rather than an overlap of meaning.

4307.text: M47 (life/soul, H5315H), M65 (edge, H6310H), M05 (pity, H2550) and M50 (spare/compassion, H2347/H7355) co-occur in Jer.21.7; seeking here is the hostile pursuit-to-kill act, standing in stark relational opposition to the withheld pity/compassion terms that follow -- the seeking clause sets up the very absence of mercy the other M-codes then name.

4308.text: M47 (life, H5315H) co-occurs in Jer.46.26 in the same hostile-pursuit idiom as Jer.21.7; seeking is the pursuing action, life/soul is its object -- the two terms combine into the fixed idiom but remain distinct characteristics.

4309.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in John.5.18; the Jews' seeking-to-kill is the sole characteristic-bearing term in this verse within the cluster registry.

4310.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in 1Cor.7.27; both occurrences of 'seek' (regarding marital status) are the only characteristic-bearing terms present.

4311.text: In 1Kgs.2.40 the operation 'seek' (role-T3-adjacent M83 verb) is initiated by Shimei (party, T8) and directed toward his fugitive servants (party, T8 via H5650), the goal being their recovery from Gath.

4312.text: In 2Kgs.2.16 the seeking is proposed to be initiated by the fifty strong men (party, T8) and directed toward their master Elijah (party, T7/T8), a search operation ultimately forbidden by Elisha.

4315.text: In Neh.2.10 the seeking-of-welfare operation is initiated by 'someone' (Nehemiah, implied party T8) and directed toward the people of Israel (party T11), an act that provokes the displeasure of Sanballat and Tobiah (party T8).

4316.text: In Ps.119.176 the seeking operation is an imperative petition, initiated by God (implied party, addressed as 'you') and directed toward the psalmist himself, cast as 'your servant' (party T2/implicit).

4317.text: In Jer.21.7 the seeking-of-life operation is initiated by 'those who seek their lives' (enemies/Nebuchadnezzar's forces, party T8) and directed toward Zedekiah, his servants, and the people (party T7/T8/T11) -- a hostile pursuit-to-kill.

4318.text: In Jer.46.26 the seeking-of-life operation is initiated by 'those who seek their life' (party T8, aligned with Nebuchadnezzar) and directed toward the unnamed victims (implicit party), paralleling the Jer.21.7 idiom.

4319.text: In John.5.18 the seeking-to-kill operation is initiated by 'the Jews' (party T11) and directed toward Jesus (party, implied by 'him'), driven by his Sabbath-breaking and equality-with-God claims.

4320.text: In 1Cor.7.27 the seeking operation is an imperative directed at the addressee ('you', party T8) not to seek release from or seek a wife -- a reflexive operation where the party is both initiator and the one restrained from acting toward the marital-status object.

4334.text: John.5.18 'seeking...to kill him' uses the same lethal-intent idiom as the OT 'seek the life' construction (noted explicitly in the meaning tree as inherited from Hebrew) -- a marked intensification beyond the neutral base gloss of 'look for', carrying deliberate hostile intent; this matches the Jer.21.7/46.26 pattern rather than John's other, more neutral uses of zeteo (e.g. seeking Jesus to hear him).

4335.text: 1Cor.7.27's two occurrences of 'seek' (do not seek to be free; do not seek a wife) sit within the base gloss of desiring/striving for a change of state, a standard sense with no unusual divergence beyond ordinary volitional seeking.

4369.text: In 1Kgs.19.10 and 19.14 'seek' carries a hostile-pursuit nuance (seeking someone's life to take it) rather than a benign search or devotional seeking sense -- a notable shift toward predatory intent compared to Ezek.34's shepherd-seeking-lost-sheep sense.

4370.text: In Ezek.34.4 and 34.16 'sought'/'seek' render baqash in the shepherd-care sense of searching for the lost sheep -- consistent with the base gloss's literal search sense, paralleling 1Sam.9.3's donkey-search usage.

4371.text: In Eccl.3.6 'seek' sits within its paired antithesis 'a time to seek/lose' -- a general abstract sense of pursuit versus abandonment, without notable divergence from the base gloss.

4372.text: In Ezek.7.26 'seek' describes the people seeking a vision from the prophet -- an investigative/consultative sense consistent with the base gloss's 'seek to secure' sense.

4374.text: In Ezek.34.4 the seeking-operation is what the shepherds (addressed 'you') failed to do toward the lost sheep -- the shepherds are the withheld initiators, the lost sheep the intended object.

4375.text: In Ezek.34.16 God ('I') is the initiator of the seeking-operation, directed toward the lost sheep -- reversing the shepherds' failure in v.4 with divine initiative.

4376.text: In 1Kgs.19.10/19.14 the seeking-operation is initiated by unnamed hostile parties ('they') directed toward Elijah's life, marking Elijah as the target/object of a life-threatening pursuit.

4378.text: Eccl.3.6 co-occurs H1245 (seek) with M74 (keep, H8104H); the seek/lose/keep/cast-away series presents seeking as one pole in a cyclical set of opposed life-activities, with 'keep' as its retentive counterpart.

4379.text: Ezek.7.26 co-occurs H1245 (seek, of seeking a vision) with M82 (rumor, H8052), M43 (prophet), M54 (law), M36 (priest), M16 (counsel) -- seeking here operates as the desperate response-action toward failing institutional sources of divine guidance amid disaster.

4380.text: Ezek.34.4 co-occurs H1245 (sought, of the failed shepherd-care) with M03/M21/M73 (weak/sick), M23 (strengthened/force), M24 (injured), M11/M81 (brought back), M06 (harshness), M72 (ruled) -- seeking-the-lost is one specific neglected duty within a broader catalogue of shepherd failures toward the flock.

4381.text: Ezek.34.16 co-occurs H1245 (seek) with M11/M81 (bring back), M23 (strengthen), M46 (fat), M10 (destroy), M12/M26 (justice) -- here God's seeking-the-lost is paired with restorative and corrective actions, contrasting the earlier shepherds' negligence with divine intervention that both restores and judges.

4383.text: 1Kgs.19.10 and 19.14 co-occur H1245 (seek, hostile pursuit of Elijah's life) with M18 (jealous), M30/M59 (forsaken), M44 (covenant), M43 (prophets), M72 (hosts), M47 (life) -- here seeking functions as the culminating threat-action in Elijah's complaint, the endpoint of covenant-breaking and prophet-killing that leaves him the last target sought.

4440.text: In Gen.37.16 'I am seeking my brothers' the surface sense sits squarely within the base gloss of concrete physical search with no notable divergence from H1245's ordinary meaning.

4441.text: In Ezek.22.30 H1245 ('sought ... a man ... to build up the wall and stand in the breach') carries a specialized moral-covenantal nuance beyond simple physical search: God is depicted seeking a righteous intercessor to avert judgment - the impact here is a metaphor of divine expectation of human moral agency, distinct from Gen.37.16's literal search for a person's whereabouts.

4442.text: In Zech.11.16 H1245 ('seek the young') is used pastorally of a shepherd's duty of care toward vulnerable animals/people - the nuance shifts from literal search toward neglect-implying pastoral responsibility (here notably negated), contrasting with the more neutral seeking of Gen.37.16 and Prov.15.14's intellectual seeking.

4443.text: In Prov.15.14 'seeks knowledge' the sense is a standard extension of H1245 to intellectual pursuit, well within the term's attested semantic range with no unusual divergence.

4444.text: In Ezra.8.21 and 1Chr.15.13 the usage of H1245 ('seek a safe journey', 'we did not seek him') aligns with the standard sense of appealing/consulting, without notable divergence from the base gloss.

4445.text: In Gen.37.16 no other M-code characteristic co-occurs with H1245's seeking.

4446.text: In Ezek.22.30 no other M-code characteristic co-occurs with H1245's seeking; the moral-agent-seeking stands alone in this verse's M-code frame.

4447.text: In Zech.11.16 no other M-code characteristic co-occurs with H1245 in this verse's tag set (the raising-up and destruction/binding words carry M-codes M08/M74/M20/M24 respectively, but these appear on different words, not co-tagged as home-cluster items here) - treating from H1245's own vantage, it stands as the sole M83 instance; other M-codes present (M08, M74, M20, M24, M16) belong to different characteristics but the question scope is restricted to what THIS characteristic's pass records, and since no prior context exists this begins the chain, noting M16 (folly/stupidity, via H1197B-type sense) and M24 (brokenness) surround the neglect motif but relation to seeking is thematic contrast (neglect of shepherding duty) rather than direct semantic overlap.

4448.text: In Prov.15.14 H1245 ('seeks knowledge') sits alongside M15 (understanding, H0995) and M15 (knowledge, H1847) plus M16 (folly, H0200/H3684): the seeking-characteristic here is the active verb that channels the disposition of understanding toward the object of knowledge, while the fool's mouth 'feeds on folly' by contrast has no seeking-verb at all - H1245 thus functions as the operative link between the disposed heart (understanding) and its acquired object (knowledge), a role no other M-code in this verse plays.

4449.text: In Ezra.8.21 H1245 ('seek from him a safe journey') co-occurs with M24 (humbling, H6031B) and M12 (safe/right, H3477I) and M76 (journey); the seeking act is the vehicle by which the humbled party approaches God for the desired outcome, but H1245 itself is not semantically overlapping with humbling or the safe-journey outcome - it is the connecting operation, not a shared quality.

4450.text: In Gen.37.16 the operation-tagged word 'seeking' (H1245, role-T3-bearing context via the verb) is initiated by the unnamed man (party) toward his brothers (also party, the sought object), a direct interpersonal search operation.

4451.text: In Ezek.22.30 the seeking operation is initiated by God (the speaking 'I') and directed toward a man among the people who would intercede - a divine-to-human search for a covenant-faithful agent.

4452.text: In Zech.11.16 the (negated) seeking operation would be initiated by the shepherd toward the young/lost sheep, but the verse denies this action occurs, marking a failed shepherd-to-flock directional operation.

4453.text: In Prov.15.14 the seeking operation is initiated by 'the heart of him who has understanding' and directed toward 'knowledge' as its object - an internal-agent-to-abstract-object operation.

4454.text: In Ezra.8.21 the seeking operation is initiated by the assembled group ('we') and directed toward God ('from him') for the object of a safe journey - a petitionary human-to-divine operation.

4469.text: In Jer.10.21 and 1Chr.15.13 'inquire'/'seek' align with the standard cultic-consultation sense of H1875 (consulting the Lord), with no notable divergence from the base gloss.

4470.text: In Ezek.34.8 'searched' (of shepherds failing to search for sheep) carries the diligent-pastoral-care nuance (1a8) rather than cultic inquiry, impacting the verse by framing neglect of the flock as a failure of caring diligence, not merely a failure of consultation.

4473.text: In 1Chr.15.13 H1875 co-occurs with M12/M26 (rule, H4941G): the failure to seek/consult the Lord is presented as the violation of 'the rule' - a causal/narrative link but not a shared semantic characteristic; H1875 names the missing relational act, while the rule-term names the procedural standard broken.

4475.text: In Ezek.34.8 H1875 ('searched') co-occurs with M24 (prey, H0957), M25/M44 (life/beasts, H2416A/H2416C): the shepherds' failure to search/care for the sheep (H1875) is the pastoral omission that results in the sheep becoming prey to wild beasts - H1875 names the missing protective operation that permits the other M-coded conditions (predation, endangered life) to occur.

4478.text: In 1Chr.15.13 the negated seeking/consulting operation (H1875) was to be initiated by the Levites/Israel toward the Lord; its absence is cited as provoking the Lord's outbreak against them.

4480.text: In Ezek.34.8 the negated searching-for operation (H1875) was to be initiated by the shepherds (party) toward the sheep (party); their omission of this operation is what leaves the sheep exposed as prey.

4517.text: In Ps.10.15 'call to account' renders the demand/require sense (1a4-1a6) of darash, applied to God calling the wicked's wickedness to account; this sits within the base gloss's legal-demand nuance, no unusual shift from attested senses.

4518.text: No prior context recorded. Other M-codes present (M24 'break/evildoer', M58 'wicked/wickedness') describe the object being judged; H1875's seeking-to-call-to-account functions as the judicial-inquiry operation directed AT those wicked characteristics, related but from a different cluster's vantage -- this pass notes the directional link without duplicating M24/M58's own findings.

4519.text: In Ps.10.15 the Psalmist (implicitly addressing God as agent) initiates the operation 'call to account' (H1875, role-T3) directed toward 'the wicked and evildoer' (party present, H7563/H7451H) -- an imperative summons for divine reckoning against the wicked party.

4533.text: In Prov.17.19 'seeks destruction' is a figurative/idiomatic extension of baqash's base gloss (seek to find/secure); rather than literal pursuit of an object, it describes the unintended but inevitable consequence courted by prideful behaviour -- a nuance of self-incurred ruin distinct from the term's more common sense of deliberately pursuing a desired good (e.g. Gen.25.22's seeking of the Lord, Ps.10.15's judicial demand).

4534.text: No prior context recorded. Other M-codes in Prov.17.19 -- M51 'loves' (twice), M56 'transgression', M10 'strife', M08 'high/pride' -- form a chain of causes (love of transgression/strife, pride) that baqash's 'seeks destruction' names as their outcome; the seeking-characteristic thus functions as the terminal consequence-marker for the preceding dispositional M-codes rather than being directly related to any single one of them.

4548.text: In John.4.23 'seeking' (the Father seeking worshipers) sits within zeteo's base sense of desiring/pursuing an object -- here theologically elevated (God as seeker of true worship) but not a divergent nuance from the base gloss.

4549.text: No prior context recorded. Other M-codes present in John.4.23 are M13 (true/truth) and M47 (spirit) and M36 (worship, twice) -- these describe the manner and object of worship the Father seeks; zeteo's own vantage is that the Father is the initiating agent of this whole complex, seeking worship offered 'in spirit and truth' rather than possessing those qualities itself.

4550.text: In John.4.23 the Father (party present) initiates the operation 'seeking' (role-T3 word) directed toward 'such people' -- true worshipers -- as the object sought; the Father is agent, worshipers the goal.

4551.text: In John.5.30 'I seek not my own will but the will of him who sent me' uses zeteo in its volitional-pursuit sense but with a distinctive self-negating twist: Jesus disclaims seeking his own will, redirecting the term toward submission rather than self-interested acquisition -- a nuance distinct from ordinary desirous seeking, foreshadowing the same self-denying pattern Paul echoes in 1Cor.10.24/33.

4552.text: No prior context recorded. Other M-codes present in John.5.30 are M63 ('judge') and M26/M12 ('judgment'/'just') and M18 ('will', twice) -- zeteo's own contribution is that Jesus's not-seeking-his-own-will is offered as the GROUND for his judgment being just; the seeking-characteristic functions as the causal warrant underlying the justice-characteristic rather than a parallel unrelated term.

4553.text: In John.8.37 'seek to kill me' extends zeteo into its hostile-pursuit sense (LSJ II.2 'seek after, desire' applied destructively), diverging from the neutral or benevolent senses seen elsewhere in this cluster (John.4.23, 1Cor.10.24) -- here the object sought is the death of a person, showing the term's moral neutrality is entirely determined by its object.

4554.text: No prior context recorded. Other M-codes in John.8.37 are M15 ('know') and M65 ('word') -- these frame the cognitive/verbal context surrounding the hostile seeking; zeteo here names the murderous intent itself, unrelated in content to the knowing/word characteristics but temporally paired with them in the verse's logic (knowledge and rejected word precede the murderous seeking).

4555.text: In John.8.37 'you' (Abraham's offspring, party present) initiate the operation 'seek' (role-T3) directed toward 'to kill me' -- the operation's target is Jesus (the speaker), making the seeking a hostile act directed at a specific person.

4556.text: In 1Cor.10.24 'seek his own good/but the good of his neighbor' sits within zeteo's base pursuit-sense, applied to an ethical contrast; no unusual nuance beyond the term's ordinary desiring/pursuing sense, simply redirected toward another's benefit.

4557.text: No prior context recorded. No other M-code characteristic is present in 2Cor.12.14 besides zeteo itself.

4558.text: In 1Cor.10.33 'not seeking my own advantage, but that of many' repeats the ethical-redirection sense already seen in 1Cor.10.24; sits within the base gloss's pursuit-sense, no further nuance beyond that established pattern.

4559.text: No prior context recorded. The other M-code present in 1Cor.10.33 is M04 ('please') and M45 ('saved') -- zeteo's non-seeking of self-advantage is offered as the practical outworking of trying to 'please everyone', and the goal-clause ties it forward to 'that they may be saved' (M45); the seeking-characteristic functions as the linking action between the disposition of pleasing others and the salvific goal.

4560.text: In 1Cor.10.33 'I' (Paul, party present) initiate the operation 'not seeking' (role-T3) directed away from 'my own advantage' and toward 'that of many' -- the operation redirects benefit-seeking from self to others.

4561.text: In 2Cor.12.14 'I seek not what is yours but you' sits within zeteo's ordinary desiring/pursuit sense, contrasting material possessions with the persons themselves; no unusual divergence from the base gloss.

4562.text: In 2Cor.12.14 'I' (Paul, party present) initiate the operation 'seek not' (role-T3) directed away from 'what is yours' and toward 'you' -- Paul redirects the object of his seeking from the Corinthians' possessions to the Corinthians themselves as persons.

4576.text: In Phil.4.17 epizeteo's ordinary sense of desiring/requiring is deliberately split across two clauses within one verse -- 'not seeking the gift, but seeking the fruit' -- creating a rhetorical contrast unique to this occurrence: the same verb is negated for one object and affirmed for another, sharpening the distinction between selfish desire and relational/spiritual benefit not seen elsewhere for this term in this cluster.

4577.text: No prior context recorded. The other M-code present in Phil.4.17 is M39 ('gift', G1390) -- epizeteo's own vantage is that it explicitly disclaims pursuing the gift-characteristic for its own sake, redirecting the seeking toward the 'fruit' that increases to the Philippians' credit; the seeking-characteristic thus actively subordinates the gift-characteristic to a higher relational goal rather than merely co-occurring with it.

4578.text: In Phil.4.17 'I' (Paul, party present) initiate the operation 'seek' (role-T3) twice: first negated toward 'the gift' (disclaimed object), then affirmed toward 'the fruit' that increases to 'your credit' (the Philippians, party present) -- the operation is redirected from a material object toward a relational/spiritual benefit for the addressed party.

4618.text: In Heb 13:14 epizēteō carries its ordinary sense of earnest seeking toward a future good (the city to come); no notable divergence from the base gloss compared to other NT occurrences (e.g. Acts 12:19, Rom 11:7).

4619.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Heb 13:14 alongside epizēteō; the seeking stands alone as the verse's characteristic-bearing term.

4620.text: No role-T3 (Operation) tag is present on any word in Heb 13:14's role list; 'seek' itself is tagged M83 not T3, and no other operation-tagged word co-occurs with a party tag, so D7.7.1 does not apply here.

4634.text: In 2Tim.1.17 zēteō carries its ordinary sense of earnest search for a missing person (Paul), paired with the intensifying adverb spoudaiōs ('earnestly'); the base gloss of 'seek' fits without notable shift, the intensifier doing the nuancing work rather than the verb itself.

4635.text: In Matt.28.5 zēteō is used in its plain sense (the women's search for the crucified Jesus at the tomb); no divergence from base gloss.

4636.text: In Mark.3.32 zēteō denotes the family's literal search for Jesus outside the crowd; plain sense, no divergence.

4637.text: In Mark.12.12 zēteō shifts from neutral 'search' toward a hostile sense — 'seeking to arrest him' — carrying nuance of plotting/intent to harm rather than a benign search; this hostile-intent nuance recurs distinctly in Luke.20.19 with the same idiom (seeking to lay hands on) but contrasts with the benign seeking in Mark.3.32 or Luke.9.9.

4639.text: In Luke.9.9 zēteō denotes Herod's desire/attempt to see Jesus; sits within the base gloss's 'seek to' + infinitive sense of desiring/attempting, comparable to Acts usage of desire to obtain.

4640.text: In Luke.13.7 zēteō carries an idiomatic agricultural nuance — 'seeking fruit' meaning expecting/looking for a produced result from the tree — impact here is to figure divine expectation of fruitfulness/repentance; this idiomatic 'expecting a result' sense diverges from the more literal person-search occurrences (e.g. Mark.3.32, Luke.2.49) and aligns instead with metaphorical seeking of outcomes.

4641.text: In Luke.20.19 zēteō again carries the hostile-intent nuance ('sought to lay hands on him'), matching Mark.12.12's parallel usage; the impact is to mark plotted aggression rather than neutral search, distinguishing this pole of usage from the benign-search occurrences.

4642.text: In Luke.24.5 zēteō is used rhetorically/reprovingly — 'why seek the living among the dead' — the divergence is a rebuke-nuance implying the seeking itself is misdirected/mistaken in object, distinct from the straightforward physical searches elsewhere (e.g. Matt.28.5's parallel scene uses the plain sense while Luke frames it as a corrective question).
