4644.text: In Matt.28.5, M01 (fear, 'be not afraid') and M15 (knowledge, 'I know') co-occur with zēteō but are not directly tied to the seeking itself; the angel contrasts fear and knowledge against the women's search for Jesus, but zēteō's own role is simply to name what the women are doing, not to modify or be modified by the fear/knowledge terms.

4645.text: In Mark.3.32, M14 (brothers/kinship) is present as a party descriptor but not directly related to the act of seeking; the seeking targets Jesus while the kinship term merely identifies who is doing the seeking.

4646.text: In Mark.12.12, M01 (fear, 'feared the people') and M15 (perception, 'perceived') co-occur; the seeking-to-arrest is checked by fear of the crowd, but from zēteō's own vantage the seeking itself remains a distinct hostile-intent operation not merged with the fear/perception terms — it is thwarted by them rather than qualified by them.

4648.text: In Luke.9.9, M15 (seeing, 'sought to see him') co-occurs, functioning as the seeking's own object/complement (seeking-to-see) rather than as an independent characteristic in relation; the seeking and the seeing verb form a single desiring-to-perceive construction.

4649.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Luke.13.7 alongside zēteō (fruit-seeking); the term stands as the verse's sole characteristic-bearing word.

4650.text: In Luke.20.19, M01 (fear, 'feared the people') and M15 (perception, 'perceived') co-occur; as in Mark.12.12's parallel, the hostile seeking is restrained by the fear-term rather than combined with it — zēteō's own vantage is that the seeking-to-arrest remains the driving intent, checked externally by fear of the people.

4651.text: In Luke.24.5, M01 (fear, 'frightened') and M25 (life, 'the living') co-occur; the men's rebuking question uses zēteō to pointedly contrast the women's fearful state with the misdirected object of their search (the living among the dead) — the seeking-term itself supplies the corrective frame around which the fear and life-terms are set, but does not merge with either.

4653.text: In Matt.28.5, the operation-tagged word 'crucified' (role-T3) relates to the party Jesus (T7/T8) as the one who underwent it, initiated by unnamed crucifiers (implicit); this operation is distinct from but adjacent to the seeking-operation (zēteō) which the women (T2/T8 women) direct toward Jesus.

4654.text: In Mark.3.32, the operation-tagged word 'sitting' (role-T3) is performed by the crowd around Jesus (party T2), while zēteō's own seeking-operation is initiated by the mother/brothers (party T8) directed toward Jesus (party T2) who is 'outside'.

4669.text: In John.4.27 ('What do you seek?') the surface form sits within the base gloss of literal/conversational inquiry -- the disciples' unspoken question about Jesus's purpose in speaking with the woman. No notable divergence from the base sense of seeking/inquiring.

4670.text: In John.7.20 zeteo is used in the idiomatic hostile sense 'seeking to kill' (zeteo + apokteinai), diverging from the neutral base gloss 'seek/look for' toward a specifically lethal intent -- a Hebraistic idiom ('seek the life/soul') absorbed into Greek. This nuance intensifies the term into a marker of murderous plotting, distinct from its more common neutral or relational uses elsewhere in the same Gospel (e.g. John.4.27, John.7.36).

4671.text: In John.7.36 and John.8.21, zeteo describes seeking Jesus himself after his departure -- a relational/existential seeking (searching for the person of the departed Messiah) rather than a concrete physical search for a lost object. This carries theological weight (failure to find him, dying in sin) beyond the base 'look for' gloss, marking these as paradigmatic instances of futile or too-late seeking, contrasted with the successful, benign seeking in Acts.10.19/21.

4673.text: In John.18.4, John.18.7, and John.18.8, zeteo is used in its plain concrete sense 'whom do you seek/look for' -- the arresting party's search for Jesus by name/identity. This sits squarely within the base gloss of literal seeking with no notable divergence, though dramatic irony (Jesus knowingly presents himself to those seeking him) colors the narrative context without altering the word's own sense.

4675.text: M48 (marveled/thaumazo) is present in John.4.27 describing the disciples' astonishment at Jesus speaking with the woman, but this is unrelated to the unspoken seeking-question ('what do you seek') the disciples withhold; the marveling and the (unasked) seeking are separate reactions in the same moment, not causally linked.

4676.text: M41 (answered/apokrinomai) is present in John.7.20 as the crowd's response, and M15 (front-loaded, not in this verse) is absent; the crowd's hostile 'seeking to kill' accusation-denial follows their answering, but the two M-codes describe sequential speech-acts rather than one characteristic acting upon the other.

4677.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in John.7.36 alongside seeking; M65 (mean/logos) tagged 'mean' is a different word-sense not a parallel characteristic in the same relational frame.

4678.text: M56 (sin/hamartia) is present in John.8.21 ('you will die in your sin'), forming a consequence-clause parallel to seeking-and-not-finding Jesus, but sin is not itself acted upon or modified by the seeking; the two stand as parallel outcomes of the disciples'/opponents' unbelief rather than one characteristic operating through the other.

4680.text: M15 (knowing/ginosko) is present in John.18.4 describing Jesus's foreknowledge of what would happen to him, which sets up his voluntary self-presentation to those seeking him; the seeking (M83) is the opponents' activity while the knowing is Jesus's own -- parallel but distinct vantage points, not one characteristic modifying the other.

4681.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Acts.27.30 alongside seeking.

4682.text: M41 (answered/apokrinomai), M59/M60 (let/aphiemi, permit-release) co-occur with seeking in John.18.8: Jesus's answer names himself as the object of their seeking, and his subsequent request to release the disciples (aphiemi) is a distinct act of protective intercession contingent on, but not modifying, the seeking itself -- the seeking identifies the target, the release-request follows as a separate transaction.

4685.text: In John.4.27 the operation 'seek' (implied unasked question, role-T3 context via surrounding verbs) is directed from the disciples (party, T8) toward Jesus, though the question itself is left unspoken -- the verse records the withheld inquiry rather than an executed seeking-act.

4686.text: In John.7.20 the seeking-to-kill operation is initiated by an unnamed 'who' (implicitly Jesus's opponents) and directed toward 'you' (Jesus), voiced rhetorically by the crowd (party, T11) who deny such intent exists.

4687.text: In John.7.36 the seeking operation is initiated by the addressed 'you' (the Jews Jesus spoke to) and directed toward Jesus ('me') -- a future seeking that will fail to find him.

4688.text: In John.8.21 the seeking operation is initiated by 'you' (his hearers) and directed toward Jesus ('me'), paralleling John.7.36 but now paired with dying in sin as the consequence of that unfulfilled seeking.

4690.text: In John.18.4 the seeking operation is initiated by the arresting party (soldiers/officers, unnamed but implied party) and directed toward 'whom' -- ultimately Jesus, who himself initiates the exchange by asking the question back to them.

4691.text: In John.18.7 the seeking operation is initiated by the same arresting party and directed toward 'whom,' answered explicitly this time as 'Jesus of Nazareth' (party, T7/T8).

4692.text: In John.18.8 the seeking operation, initiated by the arresting party, is directed toward Jesus ('me'), who confirms himself as its object and leverages that confirmed seeking to request release of his companions.

4720.text: In John.18.8 aphiemi is used in its plain permissive sense 'let/allow to go' -- sitting within the base gloss ('to permit, suffer, allow... let') with no notable divergence.

4759.text: In John.4.27 thaumazo is used in its plain base sense 'marveled/were amazed' at an unexpected social scene -- sitting within the base gloss with no notable divergence.

4771.text: In Acts.13.8 'seeking' (present participle, Elymas seeking to turn the proconsul from the faith) sits within the base sense of striving/endeavoring toward a goal; no unusual divergence, though the goal is malicious.

4772.text: In Acts.16.10 'sought' (aorist, 'we sought to go on into Macedonia') carries the ordinary sense of striving/endeavoring to act; falls within base gloss with no notable shift.

4786.text: In Acts.13.7 'sought' describing the proconsul's desire to hear God's word sits within the base sense of earnest/intensified seeking; no unusual divergence from the general gloss.

4787.text: No other M-code characteristic is tagged in Acts.13.7 alongside epizeteo's sought-to-hear action; M4908 (intelligence) and M42 (summoned) are present as roles but M4908/M65 are the only other M-codes and this is the first pass — epizeteo relates to M63 (intelligence) as the disposition motivating the seeking act, and to M65 (word/message) as its object; no prior context exists to build on.

4788.text: The operation-tagged verb 'sought' (epizeteo, role-T3 not explicitly marked here as T3 but functioning operationally) is initiated by Sergius Paulus (the proconsul, tagged T2/party) and directed toward hearing 'the word of God' — the operation moves from the human party toward the divine message as its object.

4802.text: In Gen.37.15 'seeking' (Joseph seeking his brothers) sits within the base gloss of ordinary physical searching; no notable divergence.

4803.text: In Exod.4.19 'seeking your life' carries the idiomatic hostile sense (seeking to kill), diverging from the neutral base gloss of 'search for'; the impact here is to mark mortal danger rather than benign inquiry, matching a recurring pattern with 'life' as object across other occurrences (e.g. Judg.4.22 context of Sisera's pursuit).

4804.text: In Judg.4.22 'the man you are seeking' is Jael's use of the verb in its straightforward searching sense (though the wider narrative is one of pursuit-to-kill by Barak, the verb itself here denotes simple identification/searching); no distinguishing nuance beyond the base gloss for this particular occurrence.

4805.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Gen.37.15 alongside baqash's seeking action; M76 (wandering) applies to a different word ('wandering' H8582) not co-tagged with baqash in a relational sense here — treated as sole M-code focus for this characteristic's own pass.

4806.text: In Exod.4.19, M47 (life/nephesh) co-occurs as the object of the seeking; from baqash's own vantage, the seeking-characteristic is what activates the life-term into a target of hostile pursuit — no prior cluster pass exists for this verse, so this begins the relational chain.

4807.text: In Judg.4.22, no other M-code characteristic besides baqash's own seeking-tag is present (M02 'lay' applies to a different word not co-relational with baqash here); this is the first pass over this verse.

4808.text: In Exod.4.19 the seeking-operation is initiated by unnamed 'men' (party) and directed hostilely toward Moses' life, reported by the Lord to Moses as the reason it is now safe to return.

4859.text: In Judg.6.29 'inquired' (with H1875) sits within the ordinary investigative sense of baqash -- searching out who did the deed -- no notable divergence from the base gloss.

4860.text: Ruth.3.1 'seek rest' uses baqash in its ordinary sense of Naomi seeking/arranging security for Ruth -- no divergence from base gloss, though the object 'rest' (H4494) gives it a caregiving nuance.

4861.text: In 1Sam.10.14 'seek' refers concretely to searching for lost donkeys -- a mundane, non-relational object, contrasting with the more common interpersonal/hostile senses ('seek my life') seen in 1Sam.19.2, 1Sam.20.1, 1Sam.27.1, 2Sam.3.17. This occurrence sits at the plain literal end of the range.

4862.text: 1Sam.19.2 'seeks to kill' carries a hostile, lethal nuance -- baqash here means pursuing to destroy, a sharper and more menacing sense than the neutral 'search/request' gloss, matched by the same idiom in 1Sam.20.1.

4863.text: 1Sam.20.1 repeats the hostile 'seeks my life' idiom (parallel to 1Sam.19.2), reinforcing that baqash here denotes lethal pursuit rather than neutral inquiry.

4864.text: 1Sam.27.1 'seeking me' continues the hostile-pursuit sense (Saul's manhunt for David), paired with despair (H2976), showing the seeking here is adversarial rather than devotional or investigative.

4865.text: 2Sam.3.17 'seeking David as king' shows baqash extended to a political/social desire -- the people's wish to enthrone David -- a positive, corporate-desire nuance distinct from the hostile pursuit sense elsewhere in this cluster's occurrences.

4866.text: 2Sam.21.1 'sought the face of the LORD' uses the idiomatic devotional sense -- seeking divine favor/guidance through inquiry -- distinct from the hostile or mundane senses seen elsewhere, aligning instead with worship-register usage.

4867.text: In Judg.6.29 the seeking (H1245, paired with H1875) is initiated by 'they' (the townsmen) directed toward discovering who committed the act -- an investigative operation among the community party, not toward a named individual object yet.

4868.text: In Ruth.3.1 the operation is initiated by Naomi, directed toward securing 'rest' (H4494) for Ruth -- an act of care directed from one party (mother-in-law) to another (daughter-in-law).

4869.text: In 1Sam.19.2 the seeking is initiated by Saul, directed toward killing David -- an operation of hostile pursuit from one named party toward another.

4870.text: In 1Sam.20.1 the seeking is again Saul's, directed toward David's life, reported by David himself in dialogue with Jonathan.

4871.text: In 1Sam.27.1 Saul is again the initiator of the seeking, directed toward David, within David's own internal reasoning about escape.

4872.text: In 2Sam.3.17 the initiators are the elders/people of Israel, directed toward David as the desired king -- a corporate party seeking to install another party in kingship.

4873.text: In 2Sam.21.1 David initiates the seeking, directed toward the LORD's face -- a human party petitioning the divine party for guidance.

4874.text: In Judg.6.29 the only other M-code present is M65 (thing/word), tagged on the noun 'thing' being investigated, not a characteristic-word in its own right; H1245/H1875's seeking here has no other characteristic-M-code to relate to.

4875.text: In Ruth.3.1 H1245 (seek) governs M33 (rest, H4494) as its direct object and stands near M05 (well/good, H3190) as the desired outcome -- Naomi's seeking is the operative means toward the state of rest and wellbeing for Ruth; this is the first pass over this verse.

4877.text: In 1Sam.19.2 other M-codes present are M65 (told), M74 (guard), M20 (hide) -- these describe Jonathan's warning and David's evasive response, not the content or object of Saul's seeking itself; H1245 relates to the danger these words respond to but is not semantically merged with them.

4878.text: In 1Sam.20.1 M56 (guilt) and M56 (sin) and M47 (life) appear alongside H1245 (seeks) -- David's guilt/sin question is the reason he suspects Saul's life-seeking, but the terms name distinct concepts (moral standing vs. pursuit) rather than being synonyms or direct modifiers of each other.

4879.text: In 1Sam.27.1 H1245 (seeking) is directly paired with M24 (despair, H2976) -- Saul's despairing of the seeking is the narrative pivot; the seeking-characteristic here is the very object of the despair, a tight semantic pairing.

4880.text: In 2Sam.3.17 H1245 (seeking) governs M72 (king) as its object -- the people's seeking is directly of David's kingship, a tight operation-object relation between the two M-codes.

4882.text: In 2Sam.21.1 H1245 (sought the LORD's face) co-occurs with M02/M50 (face-idiom on H6440H); the face-term is the grammatical object of the seeking rather than an independent characteristic, so no separate characteristic-level M-code stands apart from H1245 here.

4896.text: In Judg.6.29 'searched' (H1875) paired with 'inquired' (H1245) sits within the ordinary investigative sense -- no notable divergence from the base gloss.

4899.text: In Judg.6.29 the search/inquiry (H1875) is initiated by 'they' (the townsmen), directed toward discovering the identity of the altar's destroyer -- a collective investigative operation.

4934.text: In 2Sam.21.2 (Saul's zeal to strike down the Gibeonites), the surface sense 'sought [to strike down]' sits within the base gloss of intent/desire (1a4) with no notable divergence.

4935.text: In 1Kgs.11.22 Hadad's 'seeking to go' to his own country sits within the base gloss of desire/intent (1a4), no notable divergence from general usage.

4936.text: In 1Kgs.18.10 'sent to seek you' uses the base sense of physical search for a fugitive person (1a1), squarely within the gloss.

4937.text: In 2Kgs.2.17 'sought him' (the sons of the prophets searching for Elijah) is the base physical-search sense (1a1), no divergence.

4938.text: In 2Kgs.6.19 'the man whom you seek' (the Syrians seeking Elisha) is again the base physical-search sense (1a1), no divergence.

4942.text: In 2Chr.14.4 'commanded Judah to seek the Lord' shifts from a single-occasion consultative act toward the devotional/covenantal sense of ongoing worship and obedience (1a3a), a broader whole-life orientation compared with the punctual prophetic-enquiry occurrences in 1Kgs.22.5/7 and 2Kgs.22.18.

4943.text: In 2Chr.14.7 'we have sought the Lord our God... he has given us peace' extends the devotional sense (1a3a) into a covenant-causation frame -- seeking is presented as the ground of national security/peace, a nuance beyond the punctual consultation sense seen elsewhere and matching 2Chr.14.4's devotional register.

4952.text: In 2Sam.21.2, Saul (party, T8) is the initiator of the seeking-operation, directed toward striking down the Gibeonites (T11 party) -- the seeking is hostile/lethal in intent, aimed at a specific ethnic group.

4953.text: In 1Kgs.11.22, the unnamed subject (Hadad, implied party) initiates the seeking, directed toward departure/going to his own country -- self-directed movement-intent rather than toward another party.

4954.text: In 1Kgs.18.10, Pharaoh/'my lord' (T8 party) is depicted as the initiator sending agents to seek Elijah -- the operation is directed toward locating a specific fugitive person.

4955.text: In 2Kgs.2.17, the sons of the prophets (T8 party, 'fifty men') initiate the seeking, directed toward finding Elijah -- a search operation toward a specific missing person.

4956.text: In 2Kgs.6.19, the Syrian soldiers (T8 party, addressed as 'you') are the ones seeking, directed toward 'the man' (Elisha) -- Elisha's own speech frames their search-operation toward himself as object.

4960.text: In 2Chr.14.4, Judah (T11/T8 party, as commanded people) is the one directed to seek, initiated by the king's command, toward the Lord the God of their fathers (T7 party) -- a covenantal/devotional operation.

4961.text: In 2Chr.14.7, 'we' (Judah, T8/T11 party) is the initiator of the seeking, directed toward the Lord our God (T7 party) -- the operation is presented as the cause of the peace subsequently given, a covenant-causal relation between party and party.

4962.text: In 2Sam.21.2, M83 (sought) co-occurs with M03 (remnant/H3499A) and M18 (zeal/H7065), but the seeking-operation itself targets the Gibeonites' destruction and is not functionally tied to the remnant-status or zeal terms beyond sharing the verse; no prior relational context exists for this verse.

4963.text: In 1Kgs.11.22, M83 (seeking, Hadad's intent to leave) co-occurs with M18 (lacked, H2638, Pharaoh's rhetorical question about deficiency), but the seeking is not caused by or dependent on the lack-term; the two characteristics run in parallel within the exchange rather than interlocking.

4964.text: In 1Kgs.18.10, M83 (seek) co-occurs with M25/M44 (lives, H2416A) and M72 (kingdom, H4467), but the seeking-operation (Pharaoh's search for Elijah) is independent of the divine-life-oath formula and the political-kingdom terms, which frame the oath's scope rather than interact with the seeking itself.

4965.text: In 2Kgs.2.17, M83 (sought) is the only M-code characteristic present in the verse.

4966.text: In 2Kgs.6.19, M83 (seek) co-occurs with M76 (way, H1870K), but the 'way' term functions as Elisha's denial ('this is not the way') rather than interacting with the seeking-operation directed at himself; the two characteristics are unrelated in function here.

4970.text: In 2Chr.14.4, M83 (seek) co-occurs with M54 (law/commandment, H8451/H4687); seeking the Lord and keeping the law are presented as parallel royal commands rather than one characteristic acting upon the other -- both flow from the same command but remain distinct disciplines.

4971.text: In 2Chr.14.7, M83 (sought) co-occurs with M02/M50 (still ours, H6440G, land/presence) and M33 (given us peace, H5117) and M46 (prospered, H6743B); here the seeking-of-the-Lord is presented as the causal ground for the peace and prosperity that follow, making M83 the operative characteristic upon which the other outcomes depend within this verse.

4985.text: In 2Chr.22.9 'searched' sits within H1245's base sense of active pursuit (manhunt for Ahaziah); no notable divergence from the general gloss.

4989.text: In 2Chr.22.9 the search operation is initiated by unspecified pursuers (party) directed at Ahaziah (the hidden fugitive), leading to his capture -- H1245 marks the operation's onset before capture and execution.

4993.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with H1245 in Prov.21.6.

5010.text: In 2Chr.15.2 'seek' sits within the base covenantal-seeking gloss (seek the Lord), no notable divergence.

5013.text: In 2Chr.22.9 'sought' sits within the base devotional sense (sought the Lord with all his heart), no notable divergence.

5017.text: In 2Chr.15.2 the operation 'seek' is directed by Asa/Judah/Benjamin (addressed party) toward the Lord, with the promise that the Lord's own response ('found') reciprocates the initiating party's action.

5020.text: In 2Chr.22.9 Jehoshaphat's grandson (Ahaziah, referenced party) is described as the one who sought the Lord, operation directed toward the Lord with wholehearted devotion.

5024.text: Other M-codes present in 2Chr.15.2 (M02/M50 'meet', M41 'hear') do not directly interact with H1875's seek-operation; they belong to separate action threads (approach, hearing) in the same speech act rather than modifying or being modified by the seeking.

5027.text: In 2Chr.22.9 H1875 (sought the Lord) co-occurs with H1245 (searched, for Ahaziah) and M47 (heart) and M20 (hiding); from H1875's vantage, the wholehearted seeking of the Lord (righteous devotion) stands in ironic contrast to the search-and-capture of the fleeing, ungodly Ahaziah in the same verse -- the devotional seeking frames his grandfather's contrasting fate.

5044.text: In 2Chr.22.9 'able' narrows the general strength/power gloss to specifically administrative/political capacity to rule a kingdom, rather than physical or martial strength -- the impact is to underscore the total collapse of Ahaziah's dynasty, lacking any qualified successor.

5058.text: In Jer.11.21, 38.16, and 44.30 'seek' carries the idiomatic hostile sense 'seek [someone's] life' = to seek to kill, a marked divergence from the neutral 'search for' gloss; the impact is that the verb's ordinarily benign pursuit sense is inverted into murderous intent, contrasting sharply with its devotional use in Ps.27.8/Isa.65.1 where seeking is oriented toward God for blessing.

5059.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in this verse alongside the seeking of the priesthood.

5061.text: M16 (wise, H2450) and M15 (know, H3045) and M23 (cannot, H3201) co-occur but describe the futility of human search for wisdom, not a direct functional relation to seeking itself; seeking here is the frustrated activity, wisdom/knowing are its unattained objects.

5062.text: M47 (life/soul, H5315H) is present as the object of hostile seeking; the two are directly linked as verb-object (seeking a life to destroy) rather than independent co-occurring characteristics, so no separate relational role beyond being the seeking's target.

5063.text: M25/M44 (living, H2416A) and M47 (life/soul, H5315H) co-occur; seeking here targets the life (M47) of the one under threat, while 'living' describes God's own vital nature invoked in the oath -- the two M-codes are unrelated to each other beyond both attaching to different parties in the same oath-verse.

5064.text: M06 (enemy, H0341) and M47 (life, H5315H) co-occur; enmity and seeking-of-life together form the composite idiom of mortal threat, but as separate M-codes they are complementary rather than one modifying the other.

5066.text: Seeking here is initiated by the psalmist ('my heart') and directed toward the Lord's face -- the party seeking is human, the party/target sought is God.

5067.text: The toiling man initiates the seeking, directed toward the hidden 'work of God' as its object, but the verse asserts the pursuit fails to reach its target.

5068.text: God is the initiator here ('by those who did not seek me' being sought BY God), an inversion where God is subject seeking out a nation that itself did not seek him -- the direction is God toward the unresponsive nation.

5069.text: The men of Anathoth initiate the seeking, directed hostilely toward Jeremiah's life -- a party-to-party threat operation.

5070.text: 'These men' initiate the seeking, directed toward Jeremiah's life, within Zedekiah's oath promising protection against them.

5071.text: Two parallel seeking operations: unnamed 'those' initiate seeking directed at Pharaoh Hophra's life, and Nebuchadnezzar (as enemy) initiated seeking directed at Zedekiah's life -- both hostile pursuits between ruler-parties.

5085.text: In Ezek.34.11 'search' (darash) diverges from the typical cultic-consultative gloss ('inquire of' a deity/oracle) to a pastoral-shepherding sense: God searching for lost sheep. The nuance carried is active rescue-seeking rather than formal consultation; its impact is to cast God as shepherd actively pursuing the scattered flock, contrasting with the more formulaic inquiry sense in Isa.8.19 and Jer.37.7.

5088.text: M42 (called, H7121H) co-occurs describing the nation not being 'called by God's name'; it characterizes the unresponsive nation's identity, distinct from the inquiring/seeking dynamic itself which here is enacted by God, not the nation.

5090.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in this verse alongside searching/seeking.

5093.text: God ('I, I myself') initiates the search operation, directed toward his own scattered sheep -- a shepherd-to-flock operation of active pursuit and care.

5113.text: In Hos.2.7 the wife 'seeks' her lovers but does not find them -- this sits squarely within the base gloss of seeking-to-find with no unusual nuance; the futility is supplied by context (not found), not by the verb's own semantic shift.

5114.text: The seeking operation is initiated by the estranged wife (subject) and directed toward her lovers (object), paralleling the pursue/overtake verbs earlier in the verse; all describe her futile search before she resolves to return to her first husband.

5115.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with H1245 in Hos.2.7; the only M-code roles here belong to different words carrying no cluster tags of that kind (lovers, husband, better are tagged with other M-codes not present as home-cluster markers in this verse's role list for M83's counterparts). Treated as the sole M-code present from this cluster's vantage.

5116.text: In Nah.3.7 'Where shall I seek comforters for you?' uses H1245 in its ordinary sense of actively looking for/procuring a person to perform a function (comfort); no divergence from the base gloss of seeking-to-find/secure.

5117.text: The seeking operation in Nah.3.7 is initiated by the speaker (rhetorical 'I') and directed toward finding 'comforters' for ruined Nineveh -- an operation revealing the impossibility of consolation for the devastated city.

5118.text: Other M-code words are present in this verse (M76 shrink/grieve, M55 wasted, M11/M45 comforters) but they describe Nineveh's devastation and mourning rather than interacting with the act of seeking itself; the seeking here is rhetorical and unconnected to those states.

5122.text: In Zech.8.21 'seek the Lord of hosts' uses H1245 in its well-attested sense of seeking deity in prayer and worship (1a3a); this sits squarely within the base gloss with no unusual shift.

5123.text: The seeking operation is initiated by the inhabitants of the cities (parties) and directed toward the Lord of hosts, paired with entreating his favor -- a collective, mutually reinforcing movement toward divine engagement.

5124.text: H1245's seeking of the Lord in this verse is directly paired with entreating his favor (M02/M50/M73-adjacent) -- the seeking characteristic supplies the goal-directed motion toward the deity, while the entreaty term supplies the mode of approach (pleading); together they form one worship-act.

5125.text: In Mal.3.1 'the Lord whom you seek' uses H1245 in the sense of seeking/desiring an anticipated coming figure -- within the base gloss of seeking-to-find/desire, no distinct shift from ordinary usage.

5126.text: The seeking operation is initiated by 'you' (the addressed people/party) and directed toward the Lord who is about to come to his temple; the seeking anticipates and is answered by the messenger's arrival operation.

5127.text: H1245 (seeking the Lord) co-occurs with M18 delight and M44 covenant in this verse; the seeking-characteristic frames the people's anticipatory posture toward the Lord's coming, while delight (M18) names their emotional stance toward the covenant messenger -- seeking is the active pursuit that delight colors affectively.

5144.text: In Isa.1.17 'seek justice' uses H1875 in its sense of diligent pursuit/demand applied to an abstract object (mishpat, justice) rather than a person; this is within the attested semantic range (1a4 demand/require) and carries no unusual shift.

5145.text: The imperative 'seek' is directed at an unnamed addressee (the people/leaders being exhorted) toward the object 'justice', paired with correcting oppression, bringing justice to the fatherless, and pleading the widow's cause -- a chain of moral operations all initiated by the addressed party toward the vulnerable.

5146.text: H1875 (seek justice) sits amid a cluster of M-coded moral-action terms in this verse (M12/M26 justice, M80 correct oppression, M63 bring justice, M24 fatherless, M44 plead) -- seeking here functions as the initiating verb of a whole justice-program, supplying the active pursuit that the other terms specify as object, method, or beneficiary.

5150.text: In Ps.34.4 'I sought the Lord' uses H1875 in its central worship-sense (1a3a, seeking deity in prayer), matching the base gloss with no divergence -- a paradigmatic devotional use of the term.

5151.text: The psalmist (party, 'I') initiates the seeking operation directed toward the Lord; the Lord in turn answers and delivers, forming a reciprocal operation-chain of seek-answer-deliver.

5152.text: M45 (delivered) is also present but names the Lord's responsive action after seeking, not an interaction with the seeking-characteristic's own nature; the two are sequential (seek then deliver) rather than mutually defining.

5166.text: In Prov.1.28 'seek me diligently' uses H7836 in its ordinary earnest-seeking sense (personified Wisdom as object); this sits squarely within the base gloss, though the futility (seeking too late, after refusing to listen earlier) is supplied by narrative context, not the verb's own shift.

5167.text: The seeking operation is initiated by 'they' (those who earlier refused wisdom's call) and directed toward personified Wisdom ('me'), paired with 'call upon me' and answered by refusal ('I will not answer') -- an operation of belated, futile pursuit.

5168.text: M42 (call) and M22 (answer) are also present, describing the paired invocation and refusal; H7836's diligent seeking supplies the futile intensified pursuit that follows the call, but the M-codes describe distinct acts (calling vs seeking) rather than one shaping the other's meaning.

5232.text: In Isa.41.17 'seek' (participle, ongoing) sits squarely within H1245's base gloss of active pursuit of water; no divergent nuance beyond the standard sense of seeking a needed resource.

5233.text: In Hos.7.10 'seek' is negated ('nor seek him') -- the surface form carries the nuance of covenantal failure-to-seek rather than seeking itself; the impact is indictment of Israel's pride overriding any turn to God, contrasting with the positive seeking of 2Chr.7.14 and Exod.33.7.

5234.text: In Exod.33.7 'sought' describes habitual cultic practice (everyone who sought the LORD would go to the tent of meeting) -- a straightforward instance of the base gloss with no unusual nuance.

5235.text: In Lam.1.19 'sought' takes food as its object rather than God or a person -- a literal survival-seeking sense; the impact here is pathos (priests/elders seeking mere sustenance while starving), a physical-need nuance distinct from the cultic/relational seeking seen in Exod.33.7 and 2Chr.7.14.

5236.text: In 2Chr.7.14 'seek my face' is the classic idiomatic combination (seek + face) meaning seeking God's favor/presence in penitence -- squarely within the base gloss's known idiomatic use, no further divergence.

5237.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Isa.41.17 (other tags present are M09/M24/M18/M22/M30/M59/M69-type role tags on non-home strongs, but the verse's only cluster-anchored M-code term besides H1245 itself among home-cluster strongs is absent); seeking here stands alone as the relational-characteristic anchor of the verse.

5238.text: Other M-codes present in Hos.7.10 (M08 pride, M02/M50 face, M22 testify, M11/M81 return) are not directly connected to seeking from this vantage: the verse's structure sets pride as the OBSTACLE that displaces seeking, rather than seeking relating positively to any co-present characteristic -- seeking's own role is as the negated/absent act that pride's presence crowds out.

5239.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in Exod.33.7 among home-cluster terms; seeking the LORD here stands as the verse's sole relational-characteristic focus, establishing the tent-of-meeting practice.

5240.text: M-code terms present in Lam.1.19 (M51 lovers, M14 deceived, M36 priests, M11/M81 revive) surround seeking but are not directly tied to it relationally: the lovers' deception and the priests' death are the CAUSE of the desperate seeking, not a characteristic seeking itself relates to -- seeking's own contribution is marking the community's reduced state, food-seeking as last resort after betrayal and death.

5241.text: In 2Chr.7.14, seeking (H1245, seek my face) sits within a tightly-related chain with M09 (humble themselves) and M60 (forgive): seeking is the middle act -- following humbling and preceding turning -- that directs the humbled disposition specifically toward God's face/presence, making it the pivot that connects self-abasement to the divine forgiving response.

5242.text: In Exod.33.7, H1245 is the role-T3 operation: 'everyone' (the party) initiates the seeking, directed toward 'the LORD' (party), the action performed by going out to the tent of meeting.

5243.text: In 2Chr.7.14, H1245 is the role-T3 operation: 'my people' (party) initiate the seeking, directed toward God's 'face' (representing the divine party) as part of the penitential sequence.

5244.text: In Lam.1.19, H1245 is role-T3: the speaker's priests and elders (party) initiate the seeking, directed toward 'food' (an object, not a party) to revive their strength -- so the operation is party-to-object rather than party-to-party.

5259.text: In Isa.55.6 'Seek the LORD' is the paradigm sincere imperative use of darash, squarely within the base gloss of urgent covenantal seeking; no divergent nuance.

5261.text: In Isa.34.16 'Seek' takes 'the book' as its object -- a textual-inquiry nuance (seek/investigate a written record) distinct from the deity-directed sense elsewhere; the impact is to frame prophetic fulfillment as verifiable through diligent inquiry into the text itself.

5262.text: In 2Chr.1.5 'sought it out' describes Solomon and the assembly locating/visiting the bronze altar -- a concrete-object-directed use close to the base gloss's 'resort to, frequent a place' sense, no notable further divergence.

5264.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in Isa.55.6 among the tagged roles; seeking the LORD stands as the verse's sole relational-characteristic focus, paired only with the imperative to call on him.

5266.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in Isa.34.16 among tagged roles; seeking/reading the LORD's book stands alone as this verse's relational-characteristic focus.

5267.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in 2Chr.1.5 among tagged roles; Solomon and the assembly's seeking-out of the altar is the verse's sole relational-characteristic focus.

5269.text: In 2Chr.1.5, H1875 is not itself tagged role-T3 in the role list (it carries only M83); the co-occurring operation words (e.g. made/T3 on H6213H) belong to Bezalel, not to Solomon's seeking-out act, so no operation-tagged instance of H1875 itself is present to report under D7.7.1 for this verse.

5283.text: In Ps.54.3 'seek my life' is a standard idiomatic hostile use (seeking to find/secure = seeking to kill), squarely within the base gloss's 'seek to secure' sense; no unusual divergence.

5284.text: Ps.86.14 repeats the identical idiom 'seeks my life' with no shift from the base gloss.

5286.text: 1Sam.14.4 'sought to go over' uses the ordinary 'seek to secure/attempt' sense (an intended course of action), sitting within the base gloss with no special nuance.

5287.text: Ps.83.16 'seek your name' reflects the devotional 'seek the face' sense (1a3), a standard extension of the base gloss with no unusual divergence in this occurrence.

5288.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with baqash in Ps.54.3; the surrounding roles (rising up, being ruthless) are role-tagged but not this cluster's own home M-code, so relationally H1245 stands alone as the only characteristic-bearing term relevant here.

5289.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with baqash in Ps.86.14 within this cluster's home scope; H1245 is the sole characteristic-relevant term.

5291.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with baqash in 1Sam.14.4 within this cluster's home scope.

5292.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with baqash in Ps.83.16 within this cluster's home scope; shame (M07) is present but that is a different cluster and no prior relational finding is recorded to build on.

5293.text: In Ps.54.3, baqash (seek) is an operation directed by the 'ruthless men/strangers' party toward 'my life' -- the hostile subjects initiate the seeking-action aimed at the psalmist's life.

5294.text: In Ps.86.14, baqash is initiated by the 'band of ruthless men' toward the psalmist's life -- same hostile-seeking structure as Ps.54.3.

5296.text: In 1Sam.14.4, baqash is initiated by Jonathan, directed toward crossing over to the Philistine garrison -- the operation targets a place/objective rather than a person.

5297.text: In Ps.83.16, baqash is initiated by the shamed enemies (implied subject 'they') directed toward the Lord's name -- the operation moves the humiliated party toward seeking God, per the psalmist's imprecation.

5312.text: Deut.12.5 'seek the place' draws on the 'resort to, frequent' sense (1a1) combined with devotional pursuit of the divinely chosen worship-site; a standard extension within the base gloss, no notable divergence.

5313.text: 1Chr.22.19 'seek the Lord' is the classic devotional sense (1a3a), squarely within the base gloss.

5315.text: Ps.9.10 'those who seek you' is the devotional trust-sense (1a3a), squarely within the base gloss.

5317.text: In Deut.12.5, M15 (choose, of God choosing the place) is present but functions as God's own prior action, not something darash (Israel's seeking) directly modifies; the two characteristics operate on different agents (God chooses; the people seek) within the same verse without direct interaction.

5318.text: In 1Chr.22.19, darash (seek the Lord) sits alongside M47 (heart/mind, 'set your mind and heart to seek') and M44 (covenant, the ark of the covenant) -- the seeking here is explicitly heart-directed, showing darash functions as the outward enactment of an inward disposition (heart/mind) toward covenant faithfulness.

5320.text: In Ps.9.10, M19 (trust) and M30/M59 (forsaken) co-occur with darash (seek); the verse structurally pairs 'trust' and 'seek' as two aspects of the same faithful posture, with 'not forsaken' as God's covenantal guarantee answering those who trust/seek -- darash here supplies the active-pursuit half of a trust-relationship whose passive/receiving half is trust itself.

5352.text: In Acts 13:11 zeteo is used in its base literal sense — Paul, now blind, seeks people to lead him by the hand. This sits squarely within the ordinary physical 'look for/seek' gloss with no metaphorical or idiomatic shift.

5353.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in this verse alongside G2212's seeking; the nearby M73 (blindness) tag belongs to a role list entry but is not otherwise flagged as a co-present M-code needing relational comment beyond noting the narrative link: blindness precipitates the seeking.

5354.text: The seeking (role-T3 not tagged for this word directly, but the verb functions operationally) is initiated by Paul (the blinded man, party) and directed toward unnamed people ('some to lead him by the hand') — a party-directed search operation following his sudden blindness.

5370.text: Eccl 7:25's 'seek' (wisdom) is the standard intellectual-pursuit sense of baqash, well within its base gloss; no notable divergence.

5371.text: Song 3:2's repeated 'seek'/'sought' for the beloved is the literal physical-search sense of baqash and matches the base gloss with emotional intensification from repetition, but no shift in core meaning.

5372.text: 2Chr 15:15's 'sought him' (God) with 'whole desire' reflects baqash's ordinary covenantal-seeking sense; no divergence from base gloss beyond the intensifying qualifier phrase.

5374.text: In Eccl 7:25, baqash (seeking wisdom) co-occurs with M16 (wisdom/folly terms), M43 (scheme/devices), M58 (wickedness), M66 (madness) and M15 (knowing). This characteristic's vantage: seeking is the METHOD by which the Preacher pursues and tests wisdom and folly — it is the investigative operation binding the other M-codes together as objects of inquiry rather than being one of them itself.

5375.text: In Song 3:2, no other M-code characteristic besides M83 (seeking, appearing twice) and M47 (soul) is present as a distinct virtue/vice; M47 names the faculty (soul) doing the loving, not a separate characteristic in tension with seeking. Seeking here functions relationally as devoted pursuit of the beloved.

5376.text: In 2Chr 15:15, baqash (sought God) co-occurs with M04 (rejoiced), M47 (heart), M18 (desire), M33 (gave rest). This characteristic's vantage: seeking-with-whole-heart is presented as the covenantal precondition that results in God being found and rest (M33) being granted — seeking functions as the causal/relational hinge between the people's disposition (heart, desire) and the divine outcome (rest).

5378.text: In Song 3:2, the seeking operation is initiated by the speaker (the woman) and directed toward her beloved ('him whom my soul loves') — a party-to-party pursuit through the city streets.

5379.text: In 2Chr 15:15, the seeking operation is initiated by all Judah (party, M08/T11) and directed toward the Lord (party, T7) — covenantal seeking resulting in the Lord being found.

5393.text: Isa 16:5's 'seeks justice' sits within the base gloss of darash as habitual pursuit/exercise of a quality by a ruler; no unusual divergence.

5394.text: Hos 10:12's 'seek the Lord' and 1Chr 10:14's negated 'did not seek the Lord' both sit within darash's standard covenantal-seeking sense; no notable divergence beyond polarity (positive command vs. negative narrative report).

5395.text: In Isa 16:5, darash ('seeks justice') co-occurs with M72 (throne), M23 (established), M07/M50 (steadfast love), M13 (faithfulness), M63 (judges), M12 (justice/righteousness). This characteristic's vantage: seeking-justice functions as the active verb binding the throne's establishment (M23) to the moral qualities (M07 love, M13 faithfulness) that legitimate it — the ideal ruler's seeking is what operationalizes the other static virtue-nouns into royal practice.

5396.text: In Hos 10:12, darash ('seek the Lord') co-occurs with M12 (righteousness x2), M07/M50 (steadfast love), M05 (rain — a co-occurring but unrelated M-code here tagged to a different sense). This characteristic's vantage: seeking the Lord is presented as the temporal hinge-action ('it is time to seek') that must accompany sowing righteousness and reaping steadfast love — seeking is the posture that opens the way for God's response.

5398.text: In 1Chr 10:14, no other M-code characteristic besides M83 (seeking, negated) is present; the verse reports Saul's failure to seek the Lord as the sole characterized quality driving the narrative consequence (death, transfer of kingdom).

5399.text: In Isa 16:5, the seeking-justice operation is initiated by the enthroned Davidic ruler (party) and directed toward 'justice' as its object/goal — the ruler's judicial seeking benefits the people under judgment.

5400.text: In Hos 10:12, the seeking operation is initiated by Israel (addressed 'yourselves', party) and directed toward the Lord (party, T7) as the one to be sought before he comes to rain righteousness.

5402.text: In 1Chr 10:14, the (negated) seeking operation would have been initiated by Saul (party) toward the Lord (party, T7); its absence is the operative narrative fact leading to his death.

5416.text: Job 8:5's use of shachar ('seek God') sits within its base sense of diligent seeking directed at the deity, matching its typical usage; no unusual divergence.

5417.text: In Job 8:5, shachar ('seek God') co-occurs with M50 (plead/favor, H2603A). This characteristic's vantage: shachar supplies the diligent-pursuit half of the appeal while M50 (plead for favor/grace) supplies the tone of the appeal — together they form Bildad's conditional formula for Job's restoration, with seeking as the initiating action and pleading as its accompanying posture.

5418.text: In Job 8:5, the seeking operation is initiated by Job (addressed 'you', party) and directed toward God/the Almighty (party, T7) — a conditional appeal urging Job toward divine favor.

5447.text: In John 8:50 zeteo is used in its ordinary sense of seeking/pursuing (glory), matching the base gloss 'to look for, seek, strive for' with no special nuance shift; the theological weight comes from the object (glory) and the contrast of subjects, not from divergence in the verb's own sense.

5448.text: M22 (glory) is the object of the seeking in this verse -- G2212 (seeking) supplies the operative verb that directs attention either toward self (declined) or toward the Father, while M22 names what is sought; the two M-codes are bound as verb-and-object of the same clause, seeking being the vehicle that establishes to whom glory properly belongs.

5449.text: The judging (krino, T3 operation) is directed by 'the One who seeks' (the Father, implied party) toward the party of Jesus/the disputants; the seeking (G2212) itself, though not tagged role-T3 here for 'seeks' at the second occurrence, functions relationally as the ground for the judging operation -- the seeker is also cast as the judge, uniting seeking and judgment in one party.

5461.text: In Gen 43:30 baqash is used in its ordinary literal sense of seeking a place, matching the base gloss with no special divergence.

5463.text: In Exod 4:24, 1 Kgs 11:40, 2 Sam 20:19, and Ps 37:32 baqash is used in the well-attested idiomatic sense 'seek to kill/destroy' -- this is a recognized extension already covered by the base gloss's own range (seek, desire, exact), not a fresh divergence peculiar to a single occurrence.

5464.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Gen 43:30 alongside the seeking (of a place to weep); the surrounding compassion/weeping terms are annotated only with role tags in this list, not with M-codes distinct from M83 itself in a way requiring cross-reference (H7356B/M50 and H1058/M03 are present but belong to other clusters -- see below).

5465.text: M50 (compassion, H7356B) is present in this verse but relates to the earlier clause (Joseph's compassion for his brother) and not to the seeking-clause itself; the seeking of a private place to weep is a consequence of, but not structurally bound to, the compassion term -- seeking here supplies the practical outworking (finding privacy) rather than being tightly fused with the emotion word.

5466.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in Exod 4:24 alongside the seeking-to-kill; the verse's other role tags are structural (T-codes) not M-codes.

5467.text: M13 (faithful, H0529) and M46 (heritage, H5159) are both present in 2 Sam 20:19 but describe the speaker's own self-identification and the city's status, not the act of seeking itself; the seeking-to-destroy stands as the threatening operation against which the faithful/heritage identity is asserted in appeal, rather than being definitionally fused with either.

5468.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in 1 Kgs 11:40 alongside Solomon's seeking to kill Jeroboam.

5469.text: M58 (wicked, H7563), M74 (watches, H6822 -- front-loaded below), and M12 (righteous, H6662) are present in Ps 37:32 but characterize the subject (the wicked one) and the object (the righteous), while the seeking-to-kill is the operation connecting them; seeking is the hostile verb bridging the wicked-pole and righteous-pole characteristics without itself being one of those qualities.

5471.text: In Gen 43:30 the operation-word 'hurried' (H4116A, role-T3) is initiated by Joseph and directed toward exiting to seek privacy; the seeking itself (H1245) is Joseph's own subsequent act, directed toward finding a place, with Joseph as sole initiating party.

5472.text: In Exod 4:24 the operation 'met' (H6298, role-T3) is initiated by the Lord toward him (Moses/his son, implied party); the seeking-to-kill (H1245) is likewise initiated by the Lord and directed at the same party -- both operations share the same initiator and target.

5473.text: In 2 Sam 20:19 the operation 'swallow up' (H1104, role-T3) is initiated by 'you' (Joab, addressed party) directed toward the heritage/city of the Lord; the seeking-to-destroy (H1245) shares the same initiator (you) directed at the same target (the city/heritage).

5474.text: In 1 Kgs 11:40 the seeking-to-kill (H1245) is initiated by Solomon (party) and directed toward Jeroboam (party); the subsequent operations 'arose' and 'fled' (role-T3) are initiated by Jeroboam in response, directed toward escape (to Egypt).

5475.text: In Ps 37:32 the operation 'watches' (H6822, role-T3 in cluster, though tagged M74 here) is initiated by the wicked party toward the righteous party; the seeking-to-put-to-death (H1245) is the same wicked party's escalated intent directed at the same righteous target.

5491.text: In 1 Chr 10:13 darash ('seeking guidance') again sits within the base sense of consulting a medium, paralleling Deut 18:11's usage with no additional divergence.

5492.text: In 2 Chr 15:13 darash carries its well-attested devotional sense 'seek the Lord' -- this is within the base gloss's own listed sub-sense (1a3, seeking deity in prayer/worship), not a divergence from it; contrast with the necromantic-object occurrences shows the same verb pivoting entirely on its object rather than on any special contextual nuance of the verb form itself.

5494.text: M57 (breach of faith, H4603/H4604) and M65 (command, H1697G) are present in 1 Chr 10:13 alongside the seeking; the seeking-of-a-medium is presented as the culminating instance/proof of the breach of faith and failure to keep the command -- the seeking characteristic supplies the concrete act that instantiates the abstract unfaithfulness named by the other M-codes.

5495.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in 2 Chr 15:13 alongside the seeking of the Lord; the other tagged items are structural/role tags only.

5497.text: In 1 Chr 10:13 the operation 'died' (H4191, role-T3) applies to Saul; the seeking (H1875, consulting the medium) is Saul's own initiating act directed toward the medium as the consulted party, which precipitates the death operation upon himself.

5498.text: In 2 Chr 15:13 the operation 'put to death' (H4191, role-T3) is directed by the covenant community against whoever fails to seek the Lord; the seeking itself (H1875) is the required act of the individual party directed toward the Lord/God of Israel, and its absence triggers the death-operation against that same individual.

5524.text: In Jer.2.33 'seek' applies the base sense 'to seek to secure' to the abstract object 'love', a natural extension already covered in the tree's own semantic range; no unusual divergence.

5525.text: In Exod.2.15 'sought' renders the base sense 'to seek to find/secure' applied to a hostile pursuit (Pharaoh seeking to kill Moses); within the base gloss's own range, no distinguishing nuance beyond ordinary usage.

5526.text: In 1Sam.23.25 'seek' applies the base sense of pursuit-to-find directly to Saul's manhunt for David; sits squarely within the base gloss.

5527.text: In 1Kgs.10.24 'sought' extends the base sense to seeking royal audience/presence (a social-diplomatic seeking), a well-attested figurative use already within the tree's own range (1a3 'to seek the face'); no unusual shift beyond the term's normal coverage.

5528.text: In 2Chr.9.23 'sought' repeats the same audience-seeking sense as the parallel 1Kgs.10.24 occurrence; no additional divergence.

5530.text: In Exod.2.15 the operation is initiated by Pharaoh and directed toward Moses (object of the seeking-to-kill); H1245 here functions as the governing intent-verb over the operation 'kill' (H2026, role-T3), with Pharaoh as initiator and Moses as target.

5531.text: In 1Sam.23.25 the seeking operation is initiated by Saul and his men, directed toward David as its object, paralleling the following pursuit operation (H7291 'pursued').

5532.text: In 1Kgs.10.24 the seeking operation is initiated by 'the whole earth' (collective party) and directed toward Solomon's presence, seeking access to his wisdom.

5533.text: In 2Chr.9.23 the seeking operation is initiated by 'all the kings of the earth' and directed toward Solomon's presence, identical relational structure to the 1Kgs.10.24 parallel.

5534.text: In Jer.2.33 the seeking operation is initiated by the addressed woman ('you') and directed toward the abstract object 'love', with the following operation 'taught' directed toward wicked women - two linked but distinct operations sharing the same initiating party.

5536.text: In Jer.2.33, H1245 (seek) co-occurs with M76 (course/ways), M51 (love), M24/M58 (wicked women), M05 (well/good); this characteristic's vantage: the seeking-operation is what channels 'course' (M76) toward its object 'love' (M51), showing the pursuit-verb as the active link between the moral-path vocabulary and the desired-object vocabulary, while M24/M58 marks the corrupting company taught along that same path.

5537.text: In 1Sam.23.25, no other M-code characteristic is present in the verse alongside H1245.

5538.text: In 1Kgs.10.24, H1245 (sought) co-occurs with M02/M50 (presence), M16 (wisdom), M47 (mind); this characteristic's vantage: the seeking-operation is the vehicle by which the collective party accesses Solomon's presence (M02/M50) in order to hear the wisdom (M16) that God placed in his mind (M47) - H1245 functions as the connecting act, not itself the content sought.

5539.text: In 2Chr.9.23, H1245 (sought) co-occurs with M72 (kings), M02/M50 (presence), M16 (wisdom), M47 (mind); same relational role as the 1Kgs.10.24 parallel - the seeking-act is the connecting operation between the royal parties and Solomon's wisdom.

5553.text: In Ps.119.155 'seek' (do not seek your statutes) applies the base sense 'to seek with application/study' (1a7) to the psalmist's contrast between the wicked and the diligent; sits squarely within the base gloss.

5555.text: In 2Chr.30.19 'seek' applies the base sense 'to seek deity in prayer and worship' (1a3a) directly and without divergence, describing hearts set to seek God despite ritual impurity.

5557.text: In Ps.119.155, no operation-tagged (role-T3) word co-occurs with H1875 in the role list provided (the verb 'do' negation carries T5, not T3); D7.7.1 is not applicable here.

5559.text: In 2Chr.30.19, the operation 'sets' (H3559H, role-T3, 'sets his heart') is initiated by the worshipper and directed toward seeking God (T7-tagged party); H1875 'seek' is the object-clause operation that this heart-setting act aims at.

5561.text: In Ps.119.155, H1875 (seek) co-occurs with M58 (wicked) and M79 (salvation); this characteristic's vantage: the negated seeking ('do not seek your statutes') is presented as the causal reason salvation (M79) remains far from the wicked (M58) - H1875 functions as the missing condition linking the negative moral state to the absent positive outcome.

5563.text: In 2Chr.30.19, H1875 (seek) co-occurs with M23 (sets/directs), M47 (heart), M61 (sanctuary's cleanness); this characteristic's vantage: 'seek' names the heart's (M47) devotional orientation that the directing-act (M23) establishes, functioning independently of and even despite the ritual-purity deficiency (M61) named alongside it.

5567.text: In Jer.2.33 'love' is used ironically/negatively - the object of the seeking is illicit or promiscuous love (paralleling harlotry imagery), diverging from the covenantal or affectionate senses (1a1, 2) toward the sexual-desire sense (1a4); this carries a condemnatory nuance distinct from the term's more common positive relational uses elsewhere.

5573.text: In 2Chr.30.19 'cleanness' (sanctuary's rules of cleanness) applies the base sense of ritual purification/purity directly to cultic regulation; sits squarely within the base gloss with no notable shift.

5590.text: In 2Chr.25.20 and Isa.19.3 the object of seeking is 'the gods of Edom' / idols and necromancers, a clearly negative-pole use of darash (illicit consultation) contrasting with its positive use toward God/heart-seeking in 2Chr.19.3.

5591.text: In 2Chr.19.3 darash is used positively of setting the heart to seek God, the devotional pole of the term contrasting with the idol-seeking senses elsewhere in this batch.

5592.text: In 2Chr.25.20 seeking (M83) co-occurs with M23/M72 (hand/power) tags on 'hand,' but these describe God's act of handing Amaziah over, not a direct semantic tie to the seeking itself; no prior relational context recorded.

5593.text: In 2Chr.19.3 seeking God (M83) is tightly bound to M05/M18 'good' and the M16-adjacent act of destroying the Asheroth: the setting of the heart to seek God is presented as the positive fruit alongside the removal of idolatry, showing M83 functioning as the culminating disposition of a reform sequence.

5595.text: In 2Chr.25.20, H1875 (sought) is an operation-tagged action with Amaziah/party (implicit 'they'=Israel) as initiator, directed toward 'the gods of Edom' as object -- the party seeks out a foreign deity.

5596.text: In 2Chr.19.3, H1875 (seek) is initiated by the addressed party (Jehoshaphat, 'you') and directed toward God, paired with the heart-setting act (M23/T3) as the internal preparation for the operation.

5611.text: In Prov.17.9, 'seeks love' is an idiomatic extension of baqash beyond literal searching -- it means to actively foster or promote love/goodwill (by covering an offense), not to search for an object; this figurative-relational sense diverges from the more literal 'seek to find' uses elsewhere (e.g. Eccl.12.10) and carries a constructive-relational nuance unique to this context.

5612.text: In Jer.19.7, 'those who seek their life' is an idiomatic hostile sense of baqash (seeking to kill/destroy), a negative-pole nuance sharply diverging from the devotional/benevolent senses in Isa.51.1 and 2Chr.19.3-type contexts; here the impact is to name mortal enemies pursuing destruction.

5613.text: In Isa.51.1, Eccl.12.10, Amos.8.12, and Dan.1.20, baqash carries its ordinary sense of active searching/inquiring with no notable divergence from the base gloss.

5614.text: In Isa.51.1, M12 (righteousness, 'pursue righteousness') co-occurs with M83 (seek the Lord) in synonymous parallelism -- both describe the same devoted pursuit posture, seeking functioning as the relational counterpart to pursuing righteousness, oriented toward the Lord as source.

5615.text: In Eccl.12.10, M65 (words) and M18 (delight) and M13 (truth) and M12 (uprightly) are present but describe the object and manner of the Preacher's writing rather than being directly tied to the seeking-act itself; seeking here is the means by which fitting words are pursued, not a disposition shared with these other M-codes.

5616.text: In Amos.8.12, M65 (word of the Lord) is the object sought but the frantic wandering context shows seeking here as futile and thwarted (they shall not find it) -- no positive relational tie to other M-codes, only an object-relation.

5617.text: In Prov.17.9, M83 (seeks) is tightly related to M51 (love) and M56 (offense/transgression): seeking love functions as the relational antidote to the offense, showing M83 in a restorative/reconciling role toward another M-code quality.

5619.text: In Jer.19.7, M02 (fall) and M47 (life) and M06 (enemies) surround M83 (seek their life) as a description of violent pursuit; seeking here functions instrumentally within a judgment scene rather than sharing a positive thematic tie with these other M-codes.

5620.text: In Isa.51.1, H1245 (seek) is an operation initiated by the addressed hearers/party ('you who pursue... you who seek') and directed toward the Lord as object of pursuit.

5621.text: In Eccl.12.10, H1245 (sought) is initiated by the Preacher (party) and directed toward finding words of delight -- an internal literary operation rather than an interpersonal one.

5622.text: In Amos.8.12, H1245 (seek) is initiated by the wandering people (party 'they') and directed toward the word of the Lord, but the operation fails ('shall not find it').

5624.text: In Jer.19.7, H1245 (seek) is initiated by hostile pursuers ('those who seek') and directed toward the life of the people of Judah/Jerusalem, a hostile operation.

5638.text: In Ps.63.1, 'earnestly I seek you' sits squarely within H7836's base gloss of diligent/early seeking, intensified by the surrounding thirst/faint imagery but not diverging from its core sense.

5639.text: In Ps.63.1, M83 (seek) is tightly bound to M47 (soul, flesh) and M18 (thirsts) and M24 (faints/weary): the earnest seeking of God is expressed through and intensified by bodily longing terms, showing M83 as the volitional counterpart to the physical/emotional longing conveyed by the other M-codes in the verse.

5640.text: In Ps.63.1, H7836 (seek) is an operation initiated by the psalmist ('I') and directed toward God ('you'), the addressed party of the entire psalm.

5674.text: Ezra.9.12's 'seek their peace' uses darash in its ordinary sense of pursuing/desiring welfare -- squarely within the base gloss, no divergence.

5675.text: 1Chr.26.31's 'search' (Niphal) shifts from the base sense of personal/religious inquiry to an administrative genealogical/military census-investigation -- a bureaucratic nuance distinct from darash's more common cultic 'seek God' usage seen elsewhere (e.g. 2Chr.15.12).

5676.text: 2Chr.15.12's 'seek the LORD' represents the term's paradigmatic cultic sense (1a3) -- no divergence from base gloss, this is the central religious usage.

5677.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with darash in Ezra.9.12; other tagged words (M19/M50/M56/M60/M70 on 'take') belong to a different lexeme (H5375U), not another M-code characteristic in relation to seeking here as a distinct thematic party.

5678.text: No other M-code characteristic is present in 1Chr.26.31 alongside darash; the verse's other tags (M24/M72 on 'chief', M23/M46 on 'ability') are administrative/status terms not thematically overlapping with seeking.

5679.text: 2Chr.15.12 pairs darash (seeking the LORD) with M44 (covenant) and M47 (heart/soul) -- from seeking's vantage, the covenant-act frames the seeking as its formal occasion, while heart/soul specify the wholehearted manner of the seeking; these are complementary but not synonymous with the seeking-action itself.

5693.text: Mal.2.15's 'seeking' (what was God seeking? Godly offspring) shifts the base gloss toward a purposive divine intent/design nuance -- not neutral searching but a stated relational goal for the covenant union, distinguishing it from hostile-seeking senses elsewhere (1Sam.20.16, Ps.4.2).

5695.text: Ps.4.2's 'seek after lies' pairs baqash with a negative object (H3577 lies), giving the seeking a morally negative, deceptive-pursuit nuance -- divergent from the neutral or godly-seeking senses in Mal.2.15 and 2Chr.15.12 (different strong).

5696.text: Mal.2.15 pairs baqash (seeking godly offspring) with M47 (spirit) present twice in the verse and M14 (faithless/treacherous dealing) and M74 (guarding). From seeking's vantage: the divine seeking-goal (godly offspring) stands as the positive aim that M14's faithlessness threatens to undo, and M74's self-guarding is the human response required to protect that sought outcome -- seeking here functions as the stated divine purpose against which the other characteristics are measured.

5698.text: Ps.4.2 pairs baqash (seek lies) with M22 (honor) and M07 (shame) and M51 (love). From seeking's vantage: the seeking-after-lies is the active pursuit that converts honor into shame -- it is the operative verb realizing the shame/honor-reversal the other terms describe statically.

5727.text: Rev.9.6's 'seek death' inverts the term's usual desirous-of-good connotation into an ironic, desperate seeking of one's own demise -- a stark contextual divergence carrying the nuance of unrelieved torment, contrasted against Mark.14.1/Acts.17.5's hostile-seeking-of-another and against the ordinary benign senses in Matt/Luke.

5728.text: Mark.14.1 and Acts.17.5 both use zeteo in the idiomatic Hebraic sense 'seek [someone] to kill/arrest' -- a lethal-hostile-pursuit nuance distinct from the base gloss of neutral searching, showing the term's capacity to carry murderous intent when its object is a targeted person.

5729.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with zeteo in Rev.9.6; the verse's other tagged terms (long/G1937 = M18) belongs to a different word not thematically overlapping as a distinct co-present characteristic beyond the shared death-longing motif.

5730.text: Acts.17.5 pairs zeteo (seeking to bring Jason's guests out) with M69 (jealous) and M58 (wicked). From seeking's vantage: the hostile seeking-action is the operational outworking of the mob's jealousy, using wicked men as instruments -- zeteo names the directed pursuit-act that jealousy motivates and wickedness executes.

5731.text: Mark.14.1 pairs zeteo (seeking to arrest/kill Jesus) with M14 (stealth/deceit). From seeking's vantage: the seeking-to-kill is the goal-directed pursuit for which stealth supplies the covert method -- seeking names the intent, stealth the concealed means.

5750.text: In Ezra.9.12 darash ('seek their peace') is the operation, initiated by the addressed Israelite party (2mp 'you') and directed toward the foreign peoples' peace/prosperity -- the command forbids this operation being directed outward toward the nations.

5751.text: In 1Chr.26.31 darash ('search was made') is the operation, initiated impersonally (Niphal, agentless) but functionally by David's administration, directed toward locating capable men (a party) at Jazer in Gilead.

5752.text: In 2Chr.15.12 darash ('seek') is the operation, initiated by the covenanting people, directed toward the LORD the God of their fathers -- a party-directed act of covenantal devotion.

5754.text: In Mal.2.15 baqash ('seeking') is the operation, initiated by God (the 'one'), directed toward the desired outcome of godly offspring from the marital union -- a divine-to-outcome directed act.

5756.text: In Ps.4.2 baqash ('seek') is the operation, initiated by the addressed 'men' (2mp), directed toward lies -- a human-to-deceptive-object directed act, paired with loving vain words.

5757.text: In Rev.9.6 zeteo ('seek') is the operation, initiated by the tormented people, directed toward death itself as the sought object -- a human-to-object (self-destructive) directed act.

5758.text: In Acts.17.5 zeteo ('seeking') is the operation, initiated by the jealous Jews and their mob, directed toward Jason's household guests (Paul and companions) whom they intend to bring out to the crowd.

5759.text: In Mark.14.1 zeteo ('seeking') is the operation, initiated by the chief priests and scribes, directed toward Jesus (arrest and kill him) using stealth as the method.

5772.text: In Ezra.2.62/Neh.7.64 'sought' registration matches the base gloss 'to seek to find' squarely -- a literal administrative search with no contextual nuance shift.

5773.text: In Lev.19.31 'seek' shifts from neutral searching to illicit spiritual consultation (seeking out mediums/necromancers); the divergence carries a strong negative moral charge absent from the base gloss, marking this as the prohibited-object pole of the term's range compared to its administrative or worship-directed uses elsewhere.

5774.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with H1245 in Ezra.2.62 (H1351 tagged M10c is the only other M-code term).

5775.text: M10c (uncleanness, via excluded/H1351) is present in Neh.7.64 but relates to ceremonial disqualification, not to the act of seeking itself; H1245's seeking is the failed cause (unproven lineage) that triggers the M10c uncleanness-exclusion outcome, but the two characteristics do not directly interact as co-present qualities.

5776.text: M10c (unclean, via H2930A) and M14 (lying, via H3049 mediums-adjacent context) appear in Lev.19.31 alongside H1245's seeking; the seeking of mediums is the very act that produces the uncleanness state -- H1245 here functions as the causal antecedent operation to the M10c defilement outcome, distinct from any earlier pass's framing.

5777.text: No role-T3 operation tag is present on H1245 itself in these verses (H1245's own tags are M83 without T3); the T3-tagged operation words present (e.g. H4672 'found', H1351 'excluded') are separate strongs, so D7.7.1 does not attach to H1245 directly in Ezra.2.62/Neh.7.64/Lev.19.31/Prov.21.6.

5793.text: In Isa.58.2, Ezra.6.21, and 1Chr.28.9 'seek/worship' sits squarely within the base cultic-consultation/devotion sense of H1875, with no further distinguishing nuance beyond ordinary devotional seeking of God.

5796.text: Numerous M-codes co-occur in Isa.58.2 (M18 delight, M15 know, M76 ways, M12 righteousness/judgment, M21 ask); H1875's own vantage is that 'seeking' functions as the umbrella act framing all these other qualities as its objects/means -- the people seek God's ways, delight, and righteousness together, with H1875 supplying the overarching pursuit-verb that the other M-codes qualify or specify.

5797.text: M15 (know), M36 (serve), M34 (whole/forever), M47 (heart/mind), M64 (plan), M06 (thought), M30/M59 (forsake), M18 (willing) all co-occur with H1875 in 1Chr.28.9; H1875's own vantage is that the verse pairs two mirrored uses of darash -- human seeking of God and divine searching of the heart -- forming the verse's relational spine that the other M-codes (serving, willing heart, forsaking) orbit as conditions or consequences of that mutual seeking.

5813.text: In Mark.14.11 'sought' carries the hostile-intent nuance (seeking an opportunity to betray) rather than the neutral 'look for' base gloss; the divergence casts the seeking as premeditated treachery, contrasting with the term's more common neutral or devotional uses (e.g. seeking God's kingdom, Mt.6.33) and aligning instead with the idiomatic 'seek to kill' pattern (Mt.2.20).

5814.text: M04 (glad, G5463) and M46 (money, G0694) co-occur with G2212's 'sought' in Mark.14.11; G2212's own vantage is that the seeking is the pivotal operative act converting the chief priests' gladness and promised money into concrete plotting -- seeking supplies the causal hinge between the emotional/financial motive (M04/M46) and the coming betrayal.

5815.text: G2212 'sought' is not itself tagged role-T3 in Mark.14.11 (its tag is M83); the T3-tagged operation words present are G0191 (heard), G1861 (promised), G1325 (give), G3860 (betray) -- performed by 'he'/Judas toward 'him' (Jesus) as target, with G2212 functioning as the deliberative act preceding the T3-tagged betrayal operation rather than being the T3 tag itself.

5847.text: In Prov.31.13 'seeks' (wool/flax) sits within the base sense of active diligent pursuit of material goods for domestic industry -- no notable divergence from the general gloss.

5849.text: In Lam.3.25 'seeks him' (the Lord) matches the devotional-inquiry base sense; no shift beyond the general gloss.

5850.text: In Prov.11.27 'searches for' evil parallels the base sense of diligent pursuit, applied here to a negative object (evil) rather than a positive one -- the divergence is in the object sought, not in the verb's own semantic shift, so treated as within-gloss usage.

5851.text: In Prov.31.13, the operation 'seeks' (H1875, role-T3-adjacent seeking act) is initiated by the woman (subject, implicit party) directed toward wool and flax as objects -- domestic industrious acquisition.

5853.text: In Lam.3.25, the operation 'seeks' is initiated by 'the soul' (the afflicted party) directed toward the Lord (divine party), an act of devotional pursuit amid suffering.

5854.text: In Prov.11.27, the operation 'searches for' (evil) is initiated by an unnamed agent ('him who searches') directed toward evil, contrasted with the one who seeks good -- an adversarial/negative-object variant of the seeking-operation.

5855.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Prov.31.13 beyond H1875's own tag alongside non-M role tags.

5857.text: In Lam.3.25, H1875 co-occurs with M05/M18 (good) M16/M68 (waiting) and M47 (soul): the seeking-characteristic here is the active counterpart to the more passive 'waiting' (M16/M68) -- both directed at the same divine object, seeking supplying the volitional/effortful dimension alongside patient endurance.

5858.text: Prov.11.27 also carries M05/M18 (good), M18 (favor), M24/M58 (evil) -- but the H1875 occurrence ('searches for it', referring to evil) is a synonym-pairing with H1245 (see below) rather than a substantive relation to the good/evil terms themselves beyond being their grammatical object.

5871.text: In Jer.4.30, 22.25, 34.20, and 34.21, 'seek your/their life/lives' is an idiom meaning to pursue someone with murderous intent, a significant narrowing from the base gloss's broader 'seek, desire, request' -- the divergence is that the general seeking-sense sharpens into lethal hostility, distinct from Prov.11.27's benign 'seeks good/favor' or Lam.1.11's survival-seeking; this formulaic idiom recurs four times in this batch alone, showing it as a standard prophetic/narrative death-threat expression rather than an isolated nuance.

5872.text: In Prov.11.27, 'seeks good' and 'seeks favor' sit within the base gloss's benign sense of pursuing a desirable object; no unusual nuance beyond ordinary usage.

5873.text: In Jer.4.30, the operation 'seek' is initiated by 'your lovers' (party) directed toward 'your life' (the addressed woman as party/object) -- a hostile pursuit following prior scorn/despising.

5874.text: In Jer.22.25, 'seek' is initiated by unnamed pursuers directed toward 'your life' (addressed king/party), functioning alongside 'give into hand of' as parallel hostile operations toward the same victim.

5875.text: In Jer.34.20, 'seek' is initiated by 'their enemies' (explicit party) directed toward 'their lives' (the condemned party) -- paired with 'give into the hand of' as the sentencing operation.

5876.text: In Jer.34.21, 'seek' is initiated by 'their enemies' directed toward 'their lives' (Zedekiah and his officials, named parties) -- same formulaic hostile-pursuit pairing with 'give into hand.'

5877.text: In Prov.11.27, 'seeks' (good/favor) is initiated by an unnamed diligent agent (party) directed toward good/favor as an abstract object -- a benign, self-directed benefit-seeking operation, contrasted with 'searches for' evil in the same verse.

5878.text: In Jer.4.30, H1245 co-occurs with M55 (desolate one), M28 (lovers), M30 (despise), M47 (life): the seeking-of-life here is the culminating hostile act following the sequence of adornment-turned-worthless and the lovers' despising -- seeking supplies the violent endpoint of the relational betrayal already signaled by M28/M30.

5879.text: In Jer.22.25, H1245 co-occurs with M23/M72 (hand), M01 (afraid), M02/M50 (afraid-face), M72 (king): seeking-life here is the operative threat that the 'hand' imagery delivers, with fear (M01/M02) as the resulting emotional state in the victim -- seeking is the cause, fear the effect.

5880.text: In Jer.34.20, H1245 co-occurs with M23/M72 (hand) and M06 (enemies): seeking-life here specifies WHAT the enemies (M06) do with the 'hand' they are given power over -- seeking supplies the active verb completing the enemies' threat.

5881.text: In Jer.34.21, H1245 co-occurs with M23/M72 (hand), M06 (enemies), M46 (army): parallels Jer.34.20's pattern -- seeking-life is the enemies' operative act, now specified as executed via the army (M46) of Babylon's king.

5882.text: In Prov.11.27, H1245 co-occurs with M05/M18 (good), M18 (favor), M24/M58 (evil), and its own cluster-sibling H1875 (searches): H1245's 'seeks good/favor' stands as the positive counterpart to H1875's 'searches for' evil in the same verse -- a direct antithetical parallelism internal to the cluster's own two members, distinct from any relation to M24/M58 as such.

5895.text: In Prov.11.27, 'diligently seeks good' sits squarely within H7836's base gloss of earnest/diligent seeking; no divergence noted.

5896.text: In Prov.11.27, the operation 'diligently seeks' is initiated by 'whoever' (generic party/agent) directed toward 'good' (abstract object) -- the positive-pole opening operation of the verse's antithetical structure.
