5897.text: In Prov.11.27, H7836 co-occurs with M05/M18 (good), M18 (favor), M24/M58 (evil), and its cluster-siblings H1245/H1875: H7836's 'diligently seeks good' opens the verse's chiastic structure, intensifying (via its 'early/earnest' root sense) the plainer H1245 'seeks favor' that follows -- the three cluster members together frame the verse's positive-versus-negative seeking contrast, with H7836 supplying the heightened-diligence register at the outset.

5923.text: In Neh.12.27 'sought' (Piel perfect) sits squarely within the base sense of active physical search -- the officials seeking out Levites in their locations -- with no distinctive nuance beyond ordinary usage.

5924.text: In Prov.18.1 'seeks' carries a negative nuance: the isolated man 'seeks his own desire' (ta'awah), shifting the verb toward self-willed, antisocial pursuit rather than neutral search -- the object sought (his own desire) colors the act as selfish, distinguishing this occurrence from the neutral-search sense seen elsewhere (e.g. Neh.12.27).

5925.text: In Neh.12.27, H1245 (seeking the Levites) is the operative act that brings about the celebration described by the prior M49/M22/M04 finding (thanksgivings/singing/gladness); however, seeking itself is a preparatory logistical act distinct from and not thematically merged with the emotional/musical cluster -- it enables the occasion but does not share its semantic domain.

5926.text: In Prov.18.1, no other M-code characteristic co-occurs alongside H1245 (M18 desire and M16 sound judgment are M-codes but not tagged as home-cluster here in the given prior context; treating strictly per this verse's M-code presence, H1245 stands as the only cluster-flagged term with an established relational thread).

5927.text: In Neh.12.27, the operation word H0935P ('bring', role-T3) is directed by the officials (implicit party) toward the Levites (party) to bring them to Jerusalem; H1245 'sought' itself is the initiating operation, with the officials as initiator seeking out the Levites as its object/target, functionally preceding and motivating the 'bring' operation.

5928.text: In Prov.18.1, the operation word H1566 'breaks out' (role-T3) is directed by the isolated man (implicit party, same subject as H1245 'seeks') against 'all sound judgment' -- H1245 itself functions as a parallel self-directed operation, the man seeking his own desire, initiator and object both centered on the isolated self.

5942.text: In Matt.7.7, Matt.7.8, and Luke.11.10, 'seek/seeks' sits squarely within the base gloss of active seeking/pursuing in the parallelism of ask-seek-knock; no distinctive nuance beyond ordinary usage.

5944.text: In 1Cor.1.22 'seek' (Greeks seek wisdom) sits within the base sense of striving-to-obtain, paralleling 'demand' (Jews demand signs) as a rhetorical contrast; no unusual divergence beyond the ordinary pursuit-of-wisdom sense.

5945.text: In Matt.7.7, Matt.7.8, and Luke.11.10, no other M-code characteristic is tagged in the role list alongside G2212 -- it stands as the sole M-coded term in these verses.

5947.text: In 1Cor.1.22, M43 (signs) and M16 (wisdom) are the objects sought/demanded but no other M-code characteristic-word co-occurs in relation to G2212 itself as a distinct characteristic; G2212 stands as the operative seeking-verb governing the wisdom-object, first pass over this verse.

5948.text: In Matt.7.7/Matt.7.8/Luke.11.10, 'seek' is directed by the disciple/petitioner (party, 2nd person addressed) toward an unnamed sought object, paralleling 'ask' toward God and 'knock' toward a door -- the seeking party initiates, the implied divine giver receives the action's aim.

5950.text: In 1Cor.1.22, 'seek' is initiated by the Greeks (party) directed toward wisdom (object), paralleling 'demand' initiated by Jews toward signs -- two parallel operation-party pairings contrasted rhetorically in the same verse.

5964.text: In Matt.6.32 and Luke.12.30, 'seek(after)' carries the nuance of anxious, worry-driven pursuit of material necessities by the Gentiles/nations, contrasted with trusting reliance on the Father -- a divergence from the base gloss's neutral 'earnest seeking' toward a critiqued, faith-lacking mode of striving; the impact is to frame such seeking negatively relative to kingdom-seeking (implied contrast in the wider Matt.6/Luke.12 context).

5965.text: In Matt.16.4, 'seeks' carries the nuance of faithless demand/testing (an evil generation demanding a sign) rather than neutral search -- this divergence impacts the verse by framing the seeking as spiritually culpable, contrasting with the anxious-but-not-malicious sense in Matt.6.32/Luke.12.30.

5966.text: In Matt.6.32, no other M-code characteristic co-occurs alongside G1934 in the given role list; it is the sole home-cluster term establishing the relational chain for this verse.

5967.text: In Matt.16.4, M58 (evil) and M57 (adulterous) qualify the 'generation' that seeks a sign (M43, sign), while M83's own G1934 names the seeking-act itself; the seeking here is enabled/colored by the generation's evil/adulterous character but the seeking-characteristic remains a distinct operational category from those moral-quality tags rather than merging with them.

5969.text: In Matt.6.32, 'seek' is initiated by the Gentiles (party) directed toward 'all these things' (material provisions, object), contrasted with the Father's prior knowledge -- the operation runs from the anxious party toward the sought object rather than toward the Father.

5970.text: In Matt.16.4, 'seeks' is initiated by the evil/adulterous generation (party) directed toward Jesus, demanding a sign from him -- the operation runs from the demanding party toward the party who is asked to supply the sign.

6004.text: In Acts.19.39 the sense shifts from physical searching to a formal/legal 'seeking a further matter to be settled' -- a procedural-demand nuance distinct from the literal-search occurrences elsewhere (e.g. Acts.12.19), reflecting the term's administrative/legal register.

6005.text: In Rom.11.7 the sense moves to an abstract theological seeking -- Israel's pursuit of righteousness/status which it failed to obtain -- contrasted with the elect who did obtain it; this is a more figurative, salvation-historical nuance compared to the concrete search of Acts.12.19.

6007.text: The addressed party ('you', the Ephesian assembly members) is directed to initiate the seeking-operation toward 'anything further' as an object requiring formal resolution in the lawful assembly.

6008.text: Israel (party, G2474) initiates the seeking-operation directed toward the sought status/righteousness ('what it was seeking'), but the operation fails while the elect subgroup succeeds in obtaining it.

6010.text: M44 ('assembly', G1577) is present as the venue in which the seeking(demand) of G1934 is to be resolved; the seeking-characteristic here is procedurally subordinated to the assembly as the proper structural forum, showing M83 operates in service of, not competition with, the community-institution characteristic M44.

6011.text: M75 (hardening, G4456) is present in the same verse: Israel's failed seeking (M83) stands in direct causal/contrastive relation to the hardening (M75) that befell 'the rest' -- the unattained object of seeking correlates with the onset of hardness, marking M83 here as the precursor condition to the M75 outcome.

6025.text: In Matt.6.33 'seek' functions as an imperative of prioritized spiritual pursuit ('seek first the kingdom') -- a moral-directive nuance elevating the term beyond simple literal search, impacting the verse as a call to reorder priorities; contrasts with the more neutral/literal 'search' senses elsewhere (e.g. Matt.13.45, Matt.18.12).

6026.text: In Matt.12.43 'seeking' rest sits within the base gloss of restless literal searching, describing the unclean spirit's wandering -- no notable divergence beyond the ordinary sense of seeking.

6028.text: In Matt.13.45 'search' functions within the base gloss of literal, purposeful searching (a merchant seeking pearls) -- a straightforward mercantile application with no notable divergence.

6029.text: In Matt.18.12 'search' sits within the base gloss of literal seeking (a shepherd seeking the lost sheep), extended metaphorically to pastoral care but not diverging structurally from the base sense of searching for something lost.

6030.text: In Matt.21.46 zeteo carries a hostile-intent nuance ('seeking to arrest him') -- shifting from neutral/benevolent search to malicious plotting, impacting the verse by casting the religious leaders as adversarial agents; this contrasts with the benevolent-search sense in Matt.18.12.

6031.text: In Matt.26.16 zeteo again carries the hostile-intent nuance ('sought an opportunity to betray'), paralleling Matt.21.46's malicious sense -- here directed specifically at securing a strategic occasion for betrayal, showing this is a recurring dark-application pattern of the term within the same narrative arc rather than an isolated occurrence.

6032.text: The addressee ('you', imperative subject) initiates the seeking-operation directed toward 'the kingdom of God and his righteousness' as the object of pursuit, with God as the ultimate relational referent.

6033.text: The unclean spirit (party) initiates the seeking-operation, directed toward 'rest' as the sought object, wandering through waterless places.

6035.text: The merchant (party) initiates the seeking-operation directed toward fine pearls as the sought object.

6036.text: The man/shepherd (party) initiates the seeking-operation directed toward the one sheep that went astray.

6037.text: The religious leaders (implied party) initiate the seeking-operation, directed toward Jesus (him) with hostile intent to arrest him, though restrained by fear of the crowds.

6038.text: Judas (he, implied party) initiates the seeking-operation directed toward an opportunity to betray Jesus (him).

6039.text: M72 (kingdom, G0932) and M12 (righteousness, G1343) are both present and are the direct objects of the M83 seeking-operation; this seeking-characteristic functions here as the active means by which the kingdom and righteousness characteristics are to be pursued and prioritized, subordinating M83 as instrumental to attaining M72/M12.

6040.text: M10c (unclean, G0169), M47 (spirit, G4151G) and M33 (rest, G0372) are present; the seeking-characteristic (M83) here is the restless activity of the unclean-spirit characteristic in pursuit of the rest-characteristic (M33), which it fails to attain -- M83 mediates between the unclean agent and its unmet goal of rest.

6042.text: M72 (kingdom, G0932) and M05 (fine/goodness, G2570G) are present; the seeking-characteristic (M83) is the merchant's operative pursuit that connects the kingdom-parable frame to the valued/fine-quality characteristic of the pearls sought, illustrating M83 as the active vehicle realizing the kingdom's worth.

6043.text: M59/M60 (leave/abandon, G0863G) is present; the seeking-characteristic (M83, going in search of the lost sheep) stands in direct sequential/causal relation to the leaving-characteristic (the shepherd leaves the ninety-nine in order to seek) -- M83 is the purposeful continuation of the M59/M60 act.

6044.text: M01 (fear, G5399) and M43 (prophet, G4396) are present; the seeking-characteristic (M83, seeking to arrest Jesus) is restrained/checked by the fear-characteristic (M01) toward the crowds, who regard Jesus per the prophet-characteristic (M43) -- M83's hostile pursuit is here directly limited by M01.

6045.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in Matt.26.16 beyond this cluster's own M83 word.

6069.text: Matt.26.59 'seeking false testimony' sits within the base gloss ('to require, demand') -- the imperfect tense marks ongoing effort by the council, no unusual nuance beyond stated sense.

6070.text: Mark.8.11 'seeking from him a sign' matches the specific sense 'to require, demand, ask for' explicitly attributed to this verse by the meaning tree itself, showing hostile/testing demand rather than neutral search -- a contextual narrowing worth flagging as the tree's own cited sense for this exact verse.

6071.text: Mark.11.18 'seeking a way to destroy him' is explicitly cited in the meaning tree as an instance of the sense 'to deliberate,' distinct from ordinary physical search -- the idiom 'seeking + means-noun' shifts the verb toward plotting/scheming, a notable divergence from the base 'search for an object' gloss.

6072.text: Mark.14.55 'seeking testimony against Jesus' parallels Matt.26.59 within the base 'require/demand' sense, no additional divergence.

6073.text: Luke.2.45 'searching for him' sits squarely within the base 'to seek, look for' sense (explicitly cited by the tree for Luke's usage of Jesus being sought), a plain physical search with no notable shift.

6074.text: Luke.4.42 'the people sought him' sits within the base sense of seeking/looking for a person, straightforward physical pursuit with no distinguishing nuance.

6075.text: Luke.5.18 'seeking to bring him in' shows zeteo governing an infinitive ('seek to do'), matching the well-attested classical pattern (LSJ II.2) of desiring/attempting an action -- within base range, no special divergence.

6076.text: Luke.6.19 'sought to touch him' again shows zeteo + infinitive expressing desire/attempt, within the base gloss, no notable shift.

6077.text: Luke.11.16 'kept seeking...a sign' is explicitly cited by the meaning tree as an instance of 'to require, demand, ask for,' paralleling Mark.8.11 -- the demand-for-proof sense is a contextual narrowing from plain search.

6078.text: Luke.12.29 'do not seek what you are to eat...nor be worried' is explicitly cited by the meaning tree as an instance of 'to deliberate,' paired with anxious worry (G3349) -- shifting zeteo from active physical search to inward, anxious preoccupation over provision, a notable nuance distinct from most other occurrences in this batch.

6079.text: In Matt.26.59 the chief priests and whole council (party) initiate the seeking, directed against Jesus (party), aiming to secure false testimony that would justify his execution -- an operation of hostile investigative pursuit.

6080.text: In Mark.8.11 the Pharisees (party) initiate the seeking, directed toward Jesus (party, 'him'), demanding a sign from heaven as a test -- an operation of adversarial demand for proof.

6081.text: In Mark.11.18 the chief priests and scribes (party) initiate the seeking, directed toward finding a way to destroy Jesus (party) -- an operation of hostile plotting.

6082.text: In Mark.14.55 the chief priests and whole council (party) initiate the seeking, directed against Jesus (party), aiming for testimony to secure his death -- an operation of hostile pursuit, ultimately fruitless per the verse.

6083.text: In Luke.2.45 Joseph and Mary (implied party, 'they') initiate the searching, directed toward the boy Jesus (party, 'him') -- an operation of benevolent, anxious search for a lost family member.

6084.text: In Luke.4.42 the people/crowd (party) initiate the seeking, directed toward Jesus (party, 'him'), wanting to keep him from leaving them -- an operation of eager, dependent pursuit.

6085.text: In Luke.5.18 the men carrying the paralyzed man (party) initiate the seeking, directed toward bringing him in and laying him before Jesus (party) -- an operation of purposeful, compassionate effort to reach Jesus for healing.

6086.text: In Luke.6.19 the whole crowd (party) initiates the seeking, directed toward touching Jesus (party, 'him') for healing power -- an operation of eager, benevolent physical pursuit.

6087.text: In Luke.11.16 'others' (party) initiate the seeking, directed toward Jesus (party, 'him'), demanding a sign from heaven to test him -- an operation of adversarial demand, paralleling Mark.8.11.

6088.text: In Luke.12.29 Jesus (as speaker, implicit party) commands 'you' (addressed party, disciples) not to seek/deliberate over food and drink -- here the operation is prohibited rather than initiated, directed inwardly at one's own anxious concern for provision rather than toward another party.

6089.text: Matt.26.59: co-occurs with M54 (G5577 false testimony) as the seeking's direct object -- zeteo supplies the operational drive that produces the false-testimony noun; the two M-codes are tightly linked as verb-and-its-sought-object rather than independently overlapping characteristics.

6090.text: Mark.8.11: co-occurs with M43 (G4592 sign) and M35 (G3985H test) -- seeking here is the vehicle by which the Pharisees' testing (M35) is carried out, targeting a sign (M43); zeteo functions as the operational means connecting the other two characteristics rather than an independent theme.

6091.text: Mark.11.18: co-occurs with M10 (G0622 destroy), M01 (G5399 feared), M48 (G1605 astonished) -- seeking a way is the deliberative operation preceding the M10 destruction-intent; the fear (M01) and astonishment (M48) are separate crowd/authority reactions not directly caused by the seeking itself but part of the same causal chain motivating it.

6092.text: Mark.14.55: no other M-code characteristic is present in this verse alongside zeteo's seeking of testimony.

6093.text: Luke.2.45: no other M-code characteristic co-occurs with the searching for the lost Jesus in this verse.

6094.text: Luke.4.42: no other M-code characteristic co-occurs; the crowd's seeking of Jesus stands alone as the verse's characteristic content.

6095.text: Luke.5.18: co-occurs with M70 (G5342 bringing) -- the men's bringing of the paralyzed man and their seeking to bring him in/lay him before Jesus are two facets of a single compound effort; seeking supplies the persistence/intent behind the physical carrying action.

6096.text: Luke.6.19: co-occurs with M23 (G1411 power) -- the crowd's seeking to touch Jesus is answered by the power (M23) going out from him; seeking is the human-side operation while power is the divine-source characteristic it draws upon.

6097.text: Luke.11.16: co-occurs with M43 (G4592 sign) and M35 (G3985H test) -- structurally identical to Mark.8.11: seeking is the operational means by which the testing targets the sign.

6098.text: Luke.12.29: co-occurs with M20 (G3349 worried/anxious) -- the prohibition against seeking food/drink is paired with a prohibition against being anxious; the two M-codes here name closely related but distinct responses (active pursuit vs. inward agitation) to the same concern over provision, both forbidden in parallel clauses.

6112.text: Luke.12.29's rendering 'be worried' reflects a rare, possibly late-developing passive sense ('to be anxious') that LSJ marks as only weakly attested (one 3rd c. AD papyrus) against the verb's much more common base sense of physically 'raising up' or 'buoying with false hope' -- this occurrence's psychological sense is a significant narrowing/specialization from the verb's dominant classical range.

6126.text: Both Mark.8.11 and Luke.11.16 use peirazo in the well-attested adversarial 'testing/tempting' sense explicitly noted in the meaning tree and mounce source for these very passages -- no additional divergence beyond the base gloss.

6140.text: Luke.5.18's use of phero for men physically carrying a paralyzed man on a bed sits squarely within the verb's most basic, most frequently attested sense ('bear, carry a load'), no notable divergence from the base gloss.

6154.text: Matt.26.59's use of pseudomartyria as the object sought by the council sits within the term's core NT-attested sense (the meaning tree cites this very verse), no additional divergence beyond the base gloss.

6168.text: In Luke.12.31 'seek his kingdom' sits squarely within the base gloss 'to seek, strive for' -- a straightforward imperative use with no notable surface divergence from zēteō's general sense.

6169.text: In Luke.15.8 'seek diligently' (with adverbial modifier) sits within the base gloss 'search after' -- the diligence is carried by the adverb, not by a shift in zēteō's own sense.

6170.text: In Luke.17.33 'seeks to preserve his life' reflects the specific NT idiomatic extension noted in the meaning tree (Hebraism 'zētein tēn psychēn') applied here to self-preservation rather than the more common 'seek to kill' sense -- the impact is a paradox (seeking to save life leads to losing it) distinct from the verb's ordinary neutral search-sense; compare Luke.19.47/Luke.22.2 where the same idiom-pattern is used with hostile intent (seeking to kill).

6171.text: In Luke.19.3 'was seeking to see who Jesus was' sits within the base gloss 'to seek, look for' -- an ordinary conative/intentional use (seeking-to-do-X), matching the well-attested infinitive-complement pattern.

6172.text: In Luke.19.10 'came to seek and to save the lost' pairs zēteō with sōzō in a programmatic mission statement; the sense is the base 'seek' sense, though the pairing itself (seek+save) is theologically loaded -- the verb's own gloss is unshifted.

6173.text: In Luke.19.47 and Luke.22.2 'were seeking to destroy/kill him' instantiates the NT Hebraism 'seek the life of' = seek to kill, a specific idiomatic narrowing of the general 'search/desire' sense toward lethal intent -- a notable divergence from the neutral base gloss, carrying the impact of marking the religious authorities' murderous resolve; contrast with the benign 'seeking to see/save' uses elsewhere in this same cluster.

6174.text: In Luke.22.6 'sought an opportunity to betray him' uses the base 'search after, look for' sense applied to an abstract object (opportunity) rather than a person -- consistent with the verb's general range, no unusual divergence.

6175.text: In John.5.44 'do not seek the glory that comes from God' sits within the base gloss 'seek, strive for' applied to an abstract prized object (glory), contrasted with receiving glory from men -- the verb's sense itself is unshifted, the contrast is carried by the surrounding clause.

6176.text: In John.6.24 'seeking Jesus' is a plain physical/personal search sense, matching the base gloss 'to seek, look for' with no special nuance.

6177.text: In Luke.12.31, M72 (kingdom) co-occurs but no prior relational context is recorded for this verse. From seeking's own vantage: seeking functions as the required disposition that orients the disciple toward the kingdom as object -- the kingdom's presence/growth is made contingent on this prior act of seeking, establishing seeking as logically and temporally prior to receiving the kingdom-benefits.

6178.text: In Luke.15.8, M10 (losing, G0622) co-occurs. Seeking here functions as the direct response to loss -- the woman's seeking is causally triggered by and directed at reversing the prior loss-event; seeking and losing form a loss-then-search sequence rather than being unrelated abstractions.

6179.text: In Luke.17.33, M45 (preserve/save) and M47 (life) and M10 (lose) co-occur. Seeking here is the initiating verb of the paradox: the act of seeking-to-preserve is what paradoxically produces loss, while its absence (implied) produces preservation -- seeking functions as the pivot-condition on which the preserve/lose outcome turns.

6180.text: In Luke.19.3, M15 (seeing) co-occurs. Seeking here is the enabling desire behind the attempted act of seeing -- seeking-to-see names Zacchaeus's intent, while seeing (M15) names the not-yet-achieved perceptual goal; the two are linked as intent-and-object rather than independent themes.

6181.text: In Luke.19.10, M45 (save) and M10 (lost) co-occur. Seeking is paired coordinately with saving as the Son of Man's twofold mission-activity, with 'the lost' (M10) as the shared object of both verbs -- seeking here supplies the searching-out phase that logically precedes and enables the saving-act.

6182.text: In Luke.19.47, M15 (teaching) and M10 (destroy) co-occur. Seeking here directs hostile intent (destroy) against the very person engaged in the teaching-activity -- seeking functions as the connective hinge turning Jesus's public teaching-ministry into the trigger for the authorities' lethal plotting.

6183.text: In Luke.22.2, M01 (fear, G5399) co-occurs. Seeking (how to kill) and fearing (the people) are both attributed to the chief priests/scribes but describe distinct psychological postures -- seeking names their active hostile intent while fear names the constraint that shapes HOW that intent may be executed (covertly), so the two are related as motive-and-constraint rather than the same activity.

6184.text: In Luke.22.6, M44 (G1843, consent/agree) co-occurs. Seeking follows consenting in sequence: Judas first consents to the plot, then seeks the opportunity to execute it -- seeking names the practical follow-through stage after the prior agreement, not a duplicate of the consent itself.

6185.text: In John.5.44, M19 (believe) and M22 (glory, both occurrences) co-occur. Seeking-glory-from-God is presented as the necessary condition for believing being possible at all -- the verse structures seeking (its object being glory) as logically prior to and determinative of belief's own possibility, with the contrastive object (glory from men vs from God) marking two competing orientations of the same seeking-capacity.

6186.text: In John.6.24, M15 (saw, G1492H) co-occurs. Seeing (that Jesus was absent) is the triggering perception that produces the crowd's subsequent seeking; seeking here is the resultant action responding to a prior negative perception, not the same event as the perceiving.

6187.text: Seeking is not itself tagged role-T3 in these verses' role lists (the operation tags fall on other verbs like 'added', 'light', 'sweep', 'finds', 'keep', 'came', 'destroy', 'betray', 'receive', 'got', 'went'); where an M83 occurrence carries T3 status is not indicated here, so D7.7.1 is recorded via the co-occurring T3-tagged operation words and their directed relation to parties present.

6188.text: In Luke.15.8, the T3-tagged operations ('having', 'light', 'sweep', 'finds') are initiated by the woman (party) and directed at objects (lamp, house, the lost coin) -- these surrounding operations frame the woman's own seeking, but seeking itself is not the tagged T3 word here.

6189.text: In Luke.19.47, the T3-tagged word 'destroy' (G0622) is initiated by the chief priests/scribes/principal men (party) and directed at 'him' (Jesus, party) -- an operation of hostile intent between two identified parties, co-occurring with the seeking-verb that governs it.

6190.text: In Luke.22.6, the T3-tagged word 'betray' (G3860) is initiated by the subject (Judas, implied party) and directed at 'him' (Jesus) 'to them' (chief priests/scribes, party) -- a three-party operation of betrayal framed by the seeking of opportunity.

6191.text: In John.6.24, the T3-tagged word 'saw' (G1492H) is initiated by the crowd (party) with Jesus (party) as its object of perception, and 'got'/'went' (T3) describe the crowd's own movement toward Capernaum -- these operations set up the subsequent seeking of Jesus by the same party.

6198.text: In Luke.22.6 'consented' reflects the later-developed active-voice sense 'agree, consent' (LSJ notes this as a later usage, exemplified specifically by this verse), diverging from the more common middle-voice NT sense of 'confess/openly acknowledge' (as in Mt.3.6, Phil.2.11). The impact is that Judas's act is framed as a simple bare agreement to betray, without the connotation of public confession/praise carried by the middle-voice occurrences elsewhere in the NT.

6212.text: In John.7.1, zeteo appears in its well-attested hostile idiomatic sense 'seek to kill' -- squarely within the base gloss's range ('to be on the watch for,' 'seek the life of'); no additional nuance beyond the term's ordinary semantic range is carried here.

6213.text: In John.7.18, zeteo is used twice in contrast: seeking one's OWN glory (self-serving pursuit) versus seeking the glory of the one who sent him (self-effacing, other-directed pursuit). The base gloss 'to seek/desire' doesn't itself carry this moral contrast; the divergence lies entirely in the object (own glory vs. sender's glory), giving the same verb opposite ethical colorings within one verse -- a sharper contrast than most of this word's other occurrences, which are uniformly hostile (seek to kill) or neutral (seek/find).

6214.text: In John.7.19, the hostile 'seek to kill' idiom recurs exactly as in John 7:1 and elsewhere -- no divergence from the established base sense.

6215.text: In John.7.30, zeteo governs 'to arrest' rather than 'to kill' directly, but remains within the same hostile-pursuit sense-range attested elsewhere for this word; no distinct nuance beyond ordinary usage.

6216.text: In John.7.34, zeteo is paired with heurisko ('you will seek me and not find me') in a context of eschatological/existential futility rather than physical pursuit or hostility -- the seeking here is temporally bounded and doomed to fail, a nuance (futile seeking after Jesus' departure) distinct from the hostile-pursuit sense dominant elsewhere in this cluster's John occurrences.

6217.text: In John.8.40, the hostile 'seek to kill' idiom recurs identically to other Johannine occurrences in this batch; no distinguishing nuance.

6218.text: In John.10.39, zeteo again governs 'to arrest' in the same hostile-pursuit pattern as John 7:30; no divergence from established sense.

6219.text: In Acts.17.27, zeteo takes God as its object in a groping, tentative sense ('perhaps feel their way toward him and find him') -- a religious/existential-seeking nuance distinct from both the hostile-pursuit and self-interest senses seen elsewhere in this batch; here the seeking is uncertain, exploratory, and universal (all humanity), showing the term's capacity to describe humanity's diffuse reaching toward the divine rather than a targeted pursuit of a specific known object.

6220.text: In Acts.21.31, the hostile 'seek to kill' idiom recurs exactly as in the Johannine occurrences; no divergence.

6221.text: In Acts.27.30, zeteo governs 'to escape' -- a self-preservation sense (sailors seeking to save themselves by abandoning ship under pretense) rather than hostility toward another or desire for glory/God; this self-interested survival nuance is distinct from the dominant 'seek to kill' pattern elsewhere in the batch, aligning instead with the self-serving 'seek own glory' sense of John 7:18.

6222.text: The Jews (party, T11) are the initiators of the seeking; it is directed toward Jesus (via 'him,' the party being sought) with the further-embedded operation 'kill' (G0615) as its goal. Seeking here functions as the preparatory/pursuit operation leading to the lethal operation.

6223.text: The subject 'the one who speaks on his own authority' initiates the seeking, directed toward 'his own glory' (an abstract object, not a party); the contrasting clause has 'the one who seeks' (Jesus, implied) directing his seeking toward 'the glory of him who sent him' (God, a party). Two initiators, two distinct objects of the same operation.

6224.text: The addressed 'you' (the crowd/interlocutors) initiate the seeking, directed toward 'me' (Jesus, the party), with the goal of killing him -- same hostile pursuit pattern as John 7:1.

6225.text: 'They' (unnamed opponents) initiate the seeking, directed toward 'him' (Jesus, the party), with the goal of arresting him; the operation is thwarted because 'no one laid a hand on him.'

6226.text: The addressed 'you' (Jesus' hearers, second person plural) are cast as future initiators of seeking, directed toward 'me' (Jesus, the party), with the futile outcome of not finding him.

6227.text: The addressed 'you' initiate the seeking, directed toward 'me' (Jesus, the party), with the goal of killing him -- the same hostile-pursuit pattern recurring across this cluster's Johannine occurrences.

6228.text: 'They' initiate the seeking, directed toward 'him' (Jesus, the party), with the goal of arresting him, though he escapes.

6229.text: Humanity generally ('they,' implied all nations) is called to initiate the seeking, directed toward God (party, T7), with the tentative goal of finding him -- a universal, exploratory rather than hostile operation.

6230.text: 'They' (unnamed opponents) initiate the seeking, directed toward 'him' (Paul, the party), with the goal of killing him -- reported to the Roman tribune.

6231.text: The sailors (party, T2) initiate the seeking, directed toward the object 'to escape from the ship' -- a self-directed operation of self-preservation rather than toward another party.

6232.text: M22 (glory) is present twice in this verse as the direct object of seeking, and M58 (falsehood, G0093) and M13 (truth/true, G0227) also appear. Seeking here is the operative verb that channels the character's orientation toward glory (M22) -- self-glory versus the sender's glory -- establishing the moral fork on which truthfulness (M13) versus falsehood (M58) is then predicated: one who seeks self-glory is implicitly capable of falsehood, one who seeks the sender's glory 'is true, and in him there is no falsehood.' Seeking is thus the pivot-operation determining which pole (true/false) the subject lands on.

6233.text: M54 (law, G3551) appears twice in this verse referring to the Mosaic law given and (unkept) by the hearers, but it is not the object of the seeking here -- the seeking targets Jesus' life, not the law itself; the two M-codes co-occur without direct semantic interaction.

6234.text: M13 (truth, G0225) is present in this verse as the content Jesus has told them, but the seeking is directed toward killing him, not toward or against the truth itself; the two M-codes co-occur in the same sentence structure without the seeking operation acting directly upon the truth characteristic.

6235.text: M72 (God, G2962G/theos-referent) is the direct object of the seeking in this verse, and M18 (far/distance-related term, G3117) qualifies the outcome of that seeking ('not far from each one of us'). Seeking's own vantage: it names the human-initiated operation of reaching toward the divine, while the M18 qualifier reassures that the objective distance to be closed by seeking is in fact minimal -- seeking is framed as an achievable, not hopeless, pursuit.

6236.text: M82 (word/report, G5334, 'word came') co-occurs with seeking in this verse: the hostile seeking-to-kill operation against Paul is what generates the report (M82) that reaches the tribune. Seeking is thus the causal antecedent event that the reporting characteristic subsequently transmits.

6298.text: Here zeteo carries a negative nuance not present in its base gloss: 'seeking to establish' their own righteousness is a misdirected, self-reliant striving contrasted with submission; this diverges from the neutral/positive 'seek' sense (as in Rom.2.7's seeking glory) by casting the pursuit as spiritually futile and opposed to God's righteousness -- a rare negative-object use of the term.

6299.text: The operation zeteo is initiated by 'they' (unbelieving Israel, ignorant of God's righteousness) and is directed toward establishing 'their own' righteousness, in implicit contrast to God as the party whose righteousness they fail to submit to.

6300.text: Seeking here is entangled with ignorance (M63) of God's righteousness (M12) and failure to submit (M23): the seeking is the misapplied energy that substitutes for submission, showing this characteristic can function destructively when its object is self rather than God -- first relational pass for this verse.

6302.text: This occurrence uses the idiom 'seek [my] life/soul' (zeteo + psyche), a specific Hebrew-derived sense meaning 'seek to kill' rather than the base gloss's neutral 'look for/desire' -- a hostile, lethal nuance distinct from the pursuit-of-good sense seen in Rom.2.7 and 1Pet.3.11.

6303.text: The operation zeteo is initiated by the hostile 'they' (Israel's persecutors of the prophets) and directed toward Elijah ('my life'), marking him as sole surviving target of lethal pursuit.

6304.text: Seeking here (to kill) sits amid killing prophets (T3 action), demolished altars (M55), and Elijah being left alone (M59); from seeking's own vantage, this is the negative/hostile pole of the seeking-verb, illustrating that the same lexical operation can serve destructive persecution as readily as devout pursuit -- first relational pass for this verse.

6316.text: Zeteo in 1Pet.3.11 ('let him seek peace') sits squarely within its base sense of purposeful pursuit of a good, matching its use for seeking glory/life elsewhere -- no notable divergence.

6317.text: The operation zeteo ('seek') is initiated by the imperative subject ('him') and directed toward peace (M33) as its object, paired with turning from evil (M58) and doing good (M05).

6318.text: Seeking peace stands as the positive pursuit-verb flanked by turning from evil (M58) and doing good (M05); from seeking's vantage it is the active complement to avoidance -- not merely refraining from evil but actively pursuing the good of peace (M33) -- first relational pass for this verse.

6320.text: Here zeteo takes on a menacing, predatory nuance ('seeking someone to devour') rather than the neutral or virtuous seeking of glory/peace elsewhere in this batch; it aligns lexically with the hostile 'seek my life' sense in Rom.11.3, showing this occurrence sits at the negative end of the term's range.

6321.text: The operation zeteo ('seeking') is initiated by the adversary/devil (the party M06/M14) and directed toward 'someone' (an unspecified victim among believers) to devour -- a predator-to-prey directed action.

6322.text: Seeking here is the devil's (M06/M14) predatory operation, framed by sober-mindedness (M69) and watchfulness (M74) as the believer's counter-disposition, and roaring (M84) as its accompanying menace; from seeking's vantage, it is the active threat that the other characteristics (sobriety, watchfulness) exist to guard against -- first relational pass for this verse.

6336.text: In Heb.12.17 ekzeteo carries the specific nuance of desperate, too-late seeking of repentance/restoration (with tears) after a blessing has been forfeited; this contrasts with its other NT occurrence (Acts 15.17, Rom.3.11, Heb.10.6) where it denotes seeking God or righteousness proactively -- here the seeking is retrospective and ultimately unsuccessful, carrying pathos absent from those other uses.

6337.text: The operation ekzeteo ('sought') is initiated by Esau (the party) and directed toward recovering/regaining the blessing (M22) and a chance to repent (M11), though the object is closed to him -- his effort is directed toward reversing his own prior loss.

6338.text: Ekzeteo here is entangled with rejection (M30), repentance (M11), and blessing (M22): Esau's intensive seeking comes after rejection and finds no avenue for repentance despite tears; from ekzeteo's vantage, it is the desperate, failed pursuit that follows -- rather than precedes -- disqualification, distinguishing it from zeteo's more open-ended seeking seen in Rom.2.7 or 1Pet.3.11 -- first relational pass for this verse.

6352.text: In Prov.8.17 shachar sits within its base gloss of diligent/earnest seeking, matching its ordinary wisdom-literature use; no notable divergence from the term's general sense.

6353.text: The operation shachar ('seek diligently') is initiated by 'those who' (human seekers, the party) and directed toward Wisdom personified ('me'), paralleling the reciprocal 'love' verbs framing the verse.

6354.text: Shachar (diligent seeking) here operates alongside love (M51, ahav) as the twin verbs binding the human party to Wisdom; from shachar's vantage, it supplies the effortful, persistent dimension of the relationship that complements love's affective dimension, together yielding the promised finding -- first relational pass for this verse.

6368.text: In Song 3.1 the surface 'sought' sits squarely within the base gloss of seeking to find a beloved person; no notable divergence from the general stepGloss.

6369.text: In 1 Sam 24.2 and 26.2, 'seek' carries a hostile-pursuit nuance (seeking to kill/capture David) rather than the neutral/benign 'seek to find' sense; this militarised sense diverges from the more affectionate or petitionary uses elsewhere (e.g. Song 3.1, Exod 10.11), showing the verb's flexibility to carry either amicable or adversarial intent depending on context.

6371.text: In Num 16.10 'seek' carries a negative nuance of illegitimate aspiration to office/status (the priesthood), diverging from neutral seeking toward censured ambition -- a distinctly negative-pole use compared to petitionary or affectionate uses elsewhere.

6374.text: The speaker ('I', the bride) initiates the seeking-operation, directed toward 'him whom my soul loves' (the beloved); no other party is present as a distinct co-agent, only the sought object.

6375.text: Saul (party) initiates the seek-operation, directed toward David and his men (party), moving into the wilderness terrain to locate them -- a hostile pursuit operation.

6376.text: M64 (chosen, of the men) is present but concerns selection/election rather than seeking; seeking here targets a person (David) not a quality, so no direct conceptual overlap with the co-present M-code.

6377.text: Saul (party) initiates the seek-operation, directed toward David (party), in the wilderness of Ziph -- again a hostile-pursuit direction of the operation.

6378.text: M64 (chosen) is present but pertains to the selection of Saul's soldiers, not conceptually tied to the seeking-of-David action itself.

6387.text: Korah's group ('you', party, addressed by Moses) is the initiator of the seeking-operation, directed toward the priesthood (an office/status, not a party) -- an illegitimate aspiration to religious office.

6400.text: Here 'sought' applies darash's normally God-directed worship/consultation sense to the host of heaven, an idolatrous inversion of its most frequent devotional use; this ironic redirection carries strong condemnatory nuance, since the same verb elsewhere describes proper seeking of Yahweh -- the impact is to underscore apostasy by borrowing the vocabulary of true devotion for false worship.

6401.text: The people (implied party, 'they') initiate the seeking-operation, directed toward the host of heaven (sun, moon, stars -- treated as quasi-party/object of worship), alongside parallel operations of loving, serving, following, and worshiping the same object.

6402.text: M51 (loved) and M36 (served) co-occur, forming a cluster of devotional-response characteristics all directed at the same false object; seeking here functions as one strand within this bundle of misdirected worship-responses, distinguished from M51/M36 by its investigative/consultative nuance (treating the host of heaven as an oracle to be consulted, not merely loved or served).

6429.text: In Deut.4.29 'seek' sits squarely within the base gloss of active pursuit/desire toward God, matching the general Piel sense with no unusual nuance shift.

6431.text: In 1Sam.19.10, 1Sam.23.15, and 1Sam.25.26 'sought/seek' carries the ordinary hostile-pursuit sense (seeking to kill/harm), consistent with the verb's attested range and not a special divergence from the base gloss.

6432.text: In Deut.4.29 the seeking is initiated by 'you' (Israel, second person plural) and directed toward 'the Lord your God' (party-tagged T7/T10); the operation is a covenantal approach from worshiper toward deity.

6433.text: In Josh.2.22 the pursuers (role-T3 operation agents) are the initiators of the searching, directed along 'the way' toward the fleeing spies, though the search fails (they find nothing).

6435.text: In Judg.14.4 Samson (implicit 'he') is the initiator of seeking, directed toward an 'opportunity' against the Philistines (T10/T11 party).

6436.text: In Judg.18.1 the tribe of Dan (party T11) is the initiator of seeking, directed toward an inheritance/land for themselves.

6437.text: In 1Sam.10.21 the collective 'they' (Israel) initiate seeking, directed toward Saul (T8 party) who is missing.

6439.text: In 1Sam.19.10 Saul (T8 party) is the initiator of seeking, directed hostilely toward David (T8 party) to kill him.

6440.text: In 1Sam.23.15 Saul (T8 party) is the initiator of seeking, directed toward David's life (T8 party as object).

6441.text: In 1Sam.25.26 unnamed 'enemies' (agentive party) are the initiators of seeking, directed toward doing evil to 'my lord' (David, T7/T8 party).

6442.text: In Deut.4.29 the only other M-code present is M47 (heart/soul), which functions as the instrument/totality-qualifier of the seeking rather than a separate characteristic in relation to baqash; no prior cluster pass recorded for this verse, so baqash here is effectively the sole substantive M-code characteristic, with M47 acting as an intensifying qualifier of the manner of seeking.

6443.text: In Josh.2.22 the M-codes M11/M81 (returned) tag the pursuers' movement, distinct from and prior to the seeking/searching act; the return and the search are sequential actions by the same party but not characteristically intertwined -- no relational dependency between baqash and the return-characteristic here.

6445.text: In Judg.14.4 baqash co-occurs with M15 (know) and M72 (ruled); Samson's secret seeking of an opportunity is contrasted with his parents' lack of knowledge (M15) and framed against Philistine political dominion (M72), but baqash does not characteristically depend on either -- it operates independently as the hidden divine-providential motive.

6446.text: In Judg.18.1 baqash co-occurs with M72 (king, in 'no king') and M46 (inheritance) and M02 (fallen); the seeking of inheritance is thematically linked to the absence of a king (a governance vacuum) but baqash itself remains the driving action distinct from these state-describing M-codes.

6447.text: In 1Sam.10.21 no other M-code characteristic is present in the verse; baqash (sought) stands as the sole M-code, describing Israel's failed search for the hidden Saul.

6449.text: In 1Sam.19.10 baqash co-occurs with M02/M50 (face, in 'eluded'); Saul's hostile seeking to kill David is thwarted by David eluding him (literally slipping from Saul's 'face') -- the two M-codes describe opposing movements of the same encounter but are not intrinsically linked characteristics.

6450.text: In 1Sam.23.15 the only other M-code present is M47 (life/soul), which functions as the object of the seeking rather than an independent characteristic; baqash effectively stands as the sole substantive characteristic in this verse.

6451.text: In 1Sam.25.26 baqash co-occurs with M25/M44 (lives, oath formula), M47 (soul), M45 (saving), M06 (enemies), M24/M58 (evil); the seeking-to-do-evil is characterized by the enmity (M06) and evil (M24/M58) terms, while the oath-formula and saving/restraining language belong to a separate part of the blessing/curse structure -- baqash relates most directly to M06/M24 as the hostile party's action, but not to the oath or saving terms.

6465.text: In Deut.4.29 'search' (darash, paired with baqash 'seek') sits within the base gloss sense of consulting/seeking God in worship, with no unusual divergence from the term's general stepGloss.

6466.text: In Deut.4.29 the operation is initiated by 'you' (Israel, second person) and directed toward 'him' (the Lord your God, T7/T10 party) -- darash names the intensive seeking-after that parallels baqash in the same verse.

6467.text: In Deut.4.29 the only other M-code present is M47 (heart/soul) functioning as an intensifying instrument-qualifier of the seeking, not a separate characteristic; darash pairs directly with baqash (its home-cluster twin) in this verse to intensify the same covenantal-seeking act, with no other distinct M-code characteristic present to relate to.

6485.text: In 1Sam.25.29 baqash carries its base sense of hostile pursuit of a life; the surface form 'seek' sits within the general stepGloss with no additional nuance beyond the standard hunting-for-life sense also seen in 1Sam.26.20.

6486.text: 1Sam.26.20 uses baqash in the same hostile-pursuit sense as 1Sam.25.29 (David's life sought by Saul), reinforced by the flea/partridge-hunt simile; no divergence from the base gloss, simply an intensified figurative restatement of the same sense.

6487.text: 1Sam.27.4 uses baqash negated ('no longer sought') to mark cessation of the hostile pursuit found in the prior two verses; the verb itself carries its base sense, the nuance lies in the negation particle rather than in baqash's own semantic shift.

6488.text: 2Sam.12.16 shifts baqash's object from a person to God ('sought God on behalf of the child'), carrying a devotional/petitionary nuance (seeking divine favor through fasting and mourning) distinct from the hostile-pursuit sense dominant in 1Sam.25/26/27; here the impact is intercessory, contrasting sharply with the predatory sense elsewhere in this batch.

6489.text: 2Sam.17.3 returns to the hostile-pursuit sense (seeking one man's life) paralleling 1Sam.25.29/26.20; no divergence from the base gloss.

6490.text: 1Kgs.1.3 uses baqash for a practical search for a suitable person (Abishag); this sits within the base 'seek to find' sense with no notable divergence, comparable to seeking pasture in 1Chr.4.39.

6491.text: 1Chr.4.39 uses baqash for seeking pasture, a mundane material-search sense within the base gloss, paralleling the search-to-find sense of 1Kgs.1.3.

6492.text: 2Chr.11.16 pairs baqash with 'setting the heart' toward seeking the Lord -- a devotional/covenantal nuance (idiom 'seek the face/God') distinct from the hostile-pursuit and material-search senses seen elsewhere in this batch; here the impact is one of loyal devotion drawing people to Jerusalem.

6493.text: 2Chr.20.4 uses baqash twice for a collective national seeking of the Lord's help during crisis (assembly and pilgrimage) -- the same devotional nuance as 2Chr.11.16 but at communal/national scale rather than individual, showing an added corporate dimension not present in the individual devotional case.

6495.text: M47 (life/soul) co-occurs with baqash in 1Sam.25.29 as the object of hostile seeking; the seeking-characteristic here functions as the operative verb directing lethal pursuit toward the 'life' M-code term, but the relation is one of grammatical object, not thematic overlap between the two characteristics themselves.

6496.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with baqash's seeking in 1Sam.26.20; the verse's other tagged terms (blood, presence, king, flea, partridge) are role-T tags without an M-code.

6497.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with baqash's cessation-of-seeking in 1Sam.27.4.

6498.text: M20 (night/lodging, from H3885A) co-occurs with baqash in 2Sam.12.16 as part of David's mourning ritual (fasting, lying all night), but the seeking act itself is directed at God, not at the night-lodging term; the two characteristics co-occur in the same devotional scene without one qualifying the other.

6499.text: M33 (peace) co-occurs with baqash in 2Sam.17.3 as the outcome sought to follow if the seeking of one life succeeds; from the seeking-vantage, baqash is the causal act whose success is framed as producing the peace-state, a means-to-end relation rather than overlap in nature.

6500.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with baqash's search for pasture in 1Chr.4.39.

6501.text: M47 (heart) co-occurs with baqash in 2Chr.11.16 as the instrument/disposition by which the people direct their seeking toward the Lord; from the seeking-vantage the heart-term supplies the internal resolve preceding the outward act of seeking, a preparatory relation rather than thematic overlap.

6502.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs with baqash's national seeking of the Lord in 2Chr.20.4.

6504.text: In 1Sam.25.29 baqash (role-T3, seek) is directed by 'men' who rise to pursue toward the 'life' of the lord (David) -- the seeking is initiated by hostile pursuers and targets the party whose life is bound in God's care.

6505.text: In 1Sam.26.20 baqash (role-T3) is initiated by 'the king of Israel' (Saul) and directed toward David, likened to seeking a single flea -- the operation's initiator is the pursuing king, its target the fleeing party David.

6506.text: In 1Sam.27.4 baqash (role-T3, negated) is initiated by Saul and was formerly directed toward David; the verse records the cessation of that operation once Saul learns David fled to Gath.

6507.text: In 2Sam.12.16 baqash (role-T3) is initiated by David and directed toward God, on behalf of the sick child -- an intercessory operation with David as agent, God as recipient party, and the child as the beneficiary object.

6508.text: In 2Sam.17.3 baqash (role-T3) is initiated by the addressee ('You') and directed toward 'the life of only one man' -- the speaker (Hushai to Absalom) frames the operation as a targeted, limited pursuit distinct from harming the whole people.

6509.text: In 1Kgs.1.3 baqash (role-T3) is initiated by unnamed servants/searchers and directed toward finding 'a beautiful young woman' throughout Israel, ultimately locating Abishag -- initiators are the king's men, the object of the search is the sought party.

6510.text: In 1Chr.4.39 baqash (role-T3) is initiated by the journeying clans and directed toward 'pasture' for their flocks -- a material-search operation with the people as initiators and pasture as the sought object.

6511.text: In 2Chr.11.16 baqash (role-T3) is initiated by 'those who had set their hearts' and directed toward 'the Lord God of Israel' -- a devotional operation with worshippers as initiators and the Lord as the sought party.

6512.text: In 2Chr.20.4 baqash (role-T3, occurring twice) is initiated by Judah/the assembled people and directed toward the Lord, seeking help in national crisis -- initiator is the collective nation, target/recipient is the Lord.

6546.text: In Esth.3.6 'sought to destroy' uses baqash in its ordinary sense of active intent/purpose ('sought to do X'), squarely within the base gloss of seeking/desiring to accomplish something; no distinguishing nuance beyond normal usage.

6548.text: In Esth.6.2, Job.10.6, Ps.24.6, Ps.27.4, Ps.34.14, Ps.35.4, and Ps.37.36 baqash is used in its standard senses (hostile pursuit, investigative search, devotional seeking, seeking peace) with no notable divergence from the base gloss.

6549.text: In Job.10.6 and Ps.24.6 darash is used in its standard investigative/devotional senses (searching out sin; seeking God's face), with no notable divergence from the base gloss.

6551.text: Other M-codes present in Esth.3.6: M30 (disdained), M65 (made known), M10 (destroy). Baqash's own seeking here is the vehicle of Haman's destructive intent (M10) but is not itself a modifier or extension of the disdain (M30) or the disclosure (M65) — it stands as the volitional pivot converting Haman's contempt into a concrete destructive plan.

6552.text: Other M-code present in Esth.6.2: M72 (kingdom/king, via king's eunuchs/king). Baqash's seeking (the plot to lay hands on the king) targets the royal office marked by M72 but does not modify or extend that characteristic itself — the relation is one of object/target, not qualification.

6553.text: In Job.10.6, baqash (seek out iniquity) and darash (search for sin, also M83) operate together as a synonymous parallel pair intensifying the single act of divine scrutiny; the two home-cluster terms mutually reinforce rather than each modifying a distinct outside M-code (M56 iniquity/sin are the objects, not characteristics being related to).

6554.text: In Job.10.6, darash (search for sin) pairs with baqash (seek out iniquity, also M83) as parallel intensifying synonyms describing the same divine investigative act; both terms jointly characterize the scrutiny rather than one qualifying the other externally.

6555.text: In Ps.24.6, darash (seek) pairs with baqash (seek, also M83) in synonymous parallelism describing the same devotional act of seeking the face of God; the two home-cluster terms reinforce a single unified characteristic of devoted pursuit.

6556.text: In Ps.24.6, baqash (seek) pairs with darash (seek, also M83) in synonymous parallelism, both describing the devoted seeking of the face of the God of Jacob; the relation is mutual reinforcement of one unified action.

6557.text: Other M-codes present in Ps.27.4: M21 (asked), M18 (beauty). Baqash (seek) here names the psalmist's total posture toward the Lord's house, which is expressed concretely through asking (M21) and gazing on beauty (M18); baqash functions as the umbrella intention, not a modifier of either.

6558.text: Other M-codes present in Ps.34.14: M11 (turn away), M24/M58 (evil), M05/M18 (good), M33 (peace). Baqash (seek) here governs 'peace' as its direct object, standing in contrastive parallel with turning from evil and doing good, but does not itself modify those other characteristics — it names the pursuit-act applied to peace specifically.

6559.text: Other M-codes present in Ps.35.4: M07 (put to shame/dishonor/disappointed), M47 (life), M15/M64 (devise). Baqash (seek after my life) names the hostile pursuit that the psalmist prays will be met with shame (M07); it is the initiating act to which the shame-outcome responds, but does not modify the shame-terms themselves.

6561.text: Other M-codes present in Ps.37.36: M02/M08/M56 (passed away). Baqash (sought) here describes the psalmist's subsequent failed search for the wicked person after his passing (M56 territory); the seeking is temporally and causally downstream of that departure but does not modify it.

6563.text: In Esth.3.6, H1245 (sought) is an operation initiated by Haman, directed toward destroying all the Jews (the people of Mordecai) — Haman is the initiating party, the Jewish people the target.

6564.text: In Esth.6.2, H1245 (sought) is an operation initiated by the two eunuchs Bigthana and Teresh, directed toward laying hands on (harming) King Ahasuerus — the eunuchs are initiators, the king the target party.

6565.text: In Job.10.6, H1245 (seek) is an operation initiated by God ('you'), directed toward Job's iniquity as the object of scrutiny — God the initiator, Job's iniquity/sin the target.

6566.text: In Job.10.6, H1875 (search for) is an operation initiated by God, directed toward Job's sin — the same divine initiator/target pair as the parallel baqash clause.

6567.text: In Ps.24.6, H1245 (seek) is an operation initiated by 'those who seek him/the face of the God of Jacob' — worshippers as initiators, God as the party sought.

6568.text: In Ps.24.6, H1875 (seek) is an operation initiated by the same worshipping generation, directed toward God (Jacob's God) as the party sought — parallel to the baqash clause in the same verse.

6569.text: In Ps.27.4, H1245 (seek) is an operation initiated by the psalmist, directed toward the Lord — specifically toward dwelling in his house and gazing on his beauty, marking God as the object of pursuit.

6570.text: In Ps.34.14, H1245 (seek) is an operation initiated by the addressee (imperative 'you'), directed toward peace as its object — an exhortation to pursue peace actively.

6571.text: In Ps.35.4, H1245 (seek) is an operation initiated by the psalmist's enemies, directed toward the psalmist's life ('my life') as the target — hostile pursuit.

6573.text: In Ps.37.36, H1245 (sought) is an operation initiated by the psalmist ('I'), directed toward the wicked person who had passed away — the psalmist's search fails to find him, marking the target as absent.

6601.text: In Ps.63.9 'those who seek to destroy my life' uses baqash in its ordinary sense of purposeful pursuit (here of harm), squarely within the base gloss with no notable shift -- the malicious object (destruction) is carried by the following infinitive, not by baqash itself.

6602.text: In Eccl.3.15 'God seeks what has been driven away' extends baqash beyond ordinary search into a theological/legal idiom of requital or calling-to-account for what has passed -- a notable nuance shift from the concrete 'search for an object' sense seen elsewhere (e.g. Prov.2.4's search for treasure), carrying an impact of divine moral oversight of time/history rather than literal finding.

6603.text: In Ps.104.21 the lions 'seeking their food' uses baqash for straightforward predatory pursuit of sustenance, sitting squarely within the base gloss with no distinguishing nuance.

6604.text: In Prov.29.26 'seek the face of a ruler' invokes the idiomatic 'seek the face' sense (1a3) already native to the lexeme's own definitional range, so this counts as within-gloss usage rather than a divergence, though it is worth noting as the idiomatic sense rather than the plain 'search' sense.

6605.text: In Ps.63.9 the operation-tagged verb 'go down' (H0935G, role-T3) is directed by the enemies (the same party who 'seek to destroy') toward their own downfall into the depths of the earth -- an ironic self-directed movement following their hostile seeking.

6606.text: In Prov.2.4 the operation word 'search' (H2664, role-T3) is initiated by the addressed 'you' and directed toward hidden treasures, paralleling and reinforcing the seeking of H1245 in the same verse -- both verbs share the same subject and object orientation.

6607.text: In Prov.14.6 the operation word 'easy' functioning as a verbal Niphal (H7043, role-T3, 'is easy/comes without effort') is directed toward the man of understanding as recipient, contrasting with the scoffer's fruitless seeking of wisdom in the same verse -- two different parties, two different action outcomes.

6608.text: In Prov.18.15 the operation word 'acquires' (H7069, role-T3) is initiated by the intelligent heart and directed toward knowledge, running parallel to 'the ear of the wise seeks knowledge' -- both clauses show a party actively pursuing/obtaining knowledge as object.

6609.text: In Eccl.3.15 the operation word 'driven away' (H7291, role-T3, Niphal passive) marks what was previously pursued/chased; God (the party performing 'seeks', H1245) is directed toward this driven-away thing, recovering or calling it to account -- God is initiator, the driven-away entity is the object.

6610.text: In Ps.63.9 M55 (H7722B, destruction/ruin) is present as the object of hostile intent, but 'seeking' here targets destruction of life rather than any positive characteristic -- the two M-codes are co-present but not mutually reinforcing; this is the first relational pass over this verse.

6611.text: In Ps.69.6 seeking (M83) sits alongside M16/M68 (hope) and M07 (shame) and M72 (hosts) -- the seeker's pursuit of God is paralleled by those who 'hope' in him, both verbs describing dependent orientation toward God, while shame is the feared outcome if that seeking/hoping proves misplaced; this is the first relational pass over this verse.

6612.text: In Ps.104.21 seeking (M83) co-occurs with M84 (roar, H7580) describing the lions' cry that accompanies their seeking of food -- the roar is an expressive accompaniment to the act of seeking rather than a distinct characteristic in tension or cooperation with it; first relational pass over this verse.

6613.text: In Ps.122.9 seeking (M83) is directed toward M05/M18 (good, H2896B) for the sake of the Lord's house -- seeking functions here as the active means by which the psalmist pursues the good of Jerusalem; first relational pass over this verse.

6614.text: In Prov.2.4 no other M-code characteristic co-occurs alongside seeking (M83); the verse's other role-tags are structural (T-codes) only.

6615.text: In Prov.14.6 seeking (M83) is paired with M08 (scoffer), M16 (wisdom), and M15 (knowledge/understanding) -- the scoffer's seeking of wisdom fails ('in vain'), contrasting with the man of understanding for whom knowledge comes easily; seeking here is the differentiating action between the two character-types. First relational pass over this verse.

6616.text: In Prov.18.15 seeking (M83) co-occurs with M15 (understanding/knowledge, twice) and M47 (heart) -- seeking is the ear's characteristic action complementing the heart's acquisitive action, both converging on the same object (knowledge). First relational pass over this verse.

6617.text: In Prov.28.5 seeking (M83) is contrasted with M24/M58 (evil) and paired positively with M15 (understanding, twice) and M12/M26 (justice) -- seeking the Lord is presented as the cause enabling full understanding of justice, while evil men's failure to seek the Lord correlates with their failure to understand justice. First relational pass over this verse.

6618.text: In Prov.29.26 seeking (M83) is directed toward M02/M50 (face) of a M72 (ruler), contrasted with M12/M26 (justice) which comes from the Lord rather than from seeking human favor -- the verse sets seeking a ruler's favor in tension with receiving justice from God. First relational pass over this verse.

6619.text: In Eccl.3.15 no other M-code characteristic co-occurs alongside seeking (M83); the remaining role-tags in this verse are structural (T-codes) only, so God's seeking of the driven-away stands as the sole characteristic-bearing term.

6637.text: In Eccl.7.28 (Qoheleth's own searching for wisdom/a person) the Piel form sits squarely within the base sense of diligent seeking without distinguishing nuance beyond ordinary usage.

6638.text: In Eccl.7.29 the Piel form again denotes ordinary human seeking (schemes/devices), matching the base gloss without special divergence.

6639.text: In Song.6.1 the Pual/passive-toned cohortative 'that we may seek him' shifts the base active-seeking gloss toward a cooperative, relational seeking undertaken jointly by companions on behalf of the speaker -- an emotional/romantic nuance not carried by the term's more legal or cultic uses elsewhere (e.g. Isa.1.12, Jer.50.20).

6641.text: In Isa.41.12 the imperfect 'seek' sits within the base sense of futile searching for adversaries who will not be found, matching ordinary usage without special nuance.

6642.text: In Jer.5.1 both occurrences ('Search'/'seeks') carry the base sense of diligent searching -- one physical search of the city, one abstract seeking of truth -- without notable divergence from the general gloss.

6643.text: In Jer.29.13 'seek' functions in its paradigmatic theological sense (seeking God wholeheartedly), matching the base gloss with no special shift, though it is the clearest instance of the term's seek-God usage in this batch.

6644.text: In Jer.50.4 'seek the Lord' matches the base theological-seeking gloss, part of a promised future repentant return, without added nuance beyond ordinary usage.

6645.text: In Jer.50.20 'sought' takes an unusual passive-of-abstraction construction ('iniquity shall be sought... and there shall be none') where the verb's object is sin/iniquity rather than a person or God; the nuance here is forensic -- a legal search for guilt that turns up empty because of divine pardon -- distinct from the personal/relational seeking senses dominant elsewhere in the batch, with the impact of dramatizing total forgiveness.

6646.text: In Ezek.34.6 'seek' (paired with H1875 'search') describes shepherds' neglect of the sheep, sitting within the base sense of active caretaking-seeking without further divergence.

6660.text: In Jer.29.13 the Qal imperfect 'seek' (parallel to H1245 in the same verse) activates the deeper cultic/wholehearted-devotion sense of darash (seeking God 'with all your heart'), a stronger and more covenantal nuance than the term's plain resorting/enquiring base sense, distinguishing it from H1245's more general seeking in the same verse; this pairing is a key illustration of the term's devotional intensity compared to its use in other contexts (e.g. mere investigation).

6661.text: In Ezek.34.6 'search' activates the pastoral-care/diligent-tending sense of darash (caring for lost sheep) rather than the cultic consult-God sense, a shepherding-specific nuance with the impact of framing the shepherds' negligence as a failure of basic pastoral duty, not merely a failure of religious devotion; this differs markedly from its use of seeking God in Jer.29.13.

6668.text: In Eccl.7.28 the seeking (H1245) is initiated by 'my soul' (the speaker) and directed toward finding a person (man/woman) -- the party performing the operation is the speaker's own soul, the target is the sought-after human party.

6669.text: In Eccl.7.29 the seeking is initiated by 'they' (mankind generally) and directed toward 'many schemes' (H2810) -- humanity as agent, self-devised contrivances as the object sought out.

6670.text: In Song.6.1 the seeking is initiated by the female speaker together with the daughters of Jerusalem ('we') and directed toward 'him', the beloved -- a joint party seeking a single missing party.

6672.text: In Isa.41.12 the seeking is initiated by the addressee ('you') and directed toward 'those who contend with you' (adversaries) -- the operation targets hostile parties who will not be found.

6673.text: In Jer.5.1 the seeking/searching is initiated by the imperative addressees (implicitly Jeremiah or agents commanded) and directed toward finding 'a man' who does justice and seeks truth, within Jerusalem's squares.

6674.text: In Jer.29.13 the seeking is initiated by 'you' (the exiles addressed) and directed toward 'me' (the Lord) -- a covenant party seeking the divine party wholeheartedly.

6675.text: In Jer.50.4 the seeking is initiated by 'the people of Israel and the people of Judah' and directed toward 'the Lord their God' -- national parties in repentant return seeking their deity.

6676.text: In Jer.50.20 the operation is passive/impersonal ('iniquity shall be sought') with an implied divine or juridical searching party directed toward 'iniquity' and 'sin' in Israel/Judah as the object -- notably yielding a null result because of pardon.

6677.text: In Ezek.34.6 the seeking (paired with H1875) is negated -- 'none to search or seek' -- meaning the shepherds who should be the initiating party toward the scattered sheep (the target) are absent from performing the operation, itself the verse's core indictment.

6678.text: In Jer.29.13 the seeking (darash) is initiated by 'you' (the exiles) directed toward 'me' (the Lord), paralleling H1245 in the same verse to intensify the wholehearted seeking of the divine party.

6679.text: In Ezek.34.6 'search' (darash) is negated together with H1245 -- 'none to search or seek for them' -- the shepherds who should initiate the caring-search toward the scattered sheep are absent, the operation's non-performance is the point.

6680.text: M47 (soul/heart-type term) is present in this verse but denotes the seeking party's inner faculty rather than a co-characteristic relating to the seeking act itself; no meaningful cross-characteristic relation to develop beyond agent-identification.

6681.text: M12 (uprightness, on 'upright' describing man as God made him) and M14 (schemes/devices) frame this verse's contrast: seeking (M83) here is directed toward corrupt self-devised schemes rather than toward the uprightness God originally gave -- seeking functions as the corrupted response to a prior good given state.

6682.text: No other M-code characteristic co-occurs in this verse; H1245 (seeking) stands alone as the verse's characteristic-relevant term.

6684.text: M10 (contend/war -- strife-type terms) are present but describe the adversaries' character, not the seeking act's own quality; the seeking here is futile precisely because it targets these strife-characterized parties, but the two characteristics remain distinct rather than mutually defining.

6685.text: M15 (take note/discernment), M12 (justice), M13 (truth), and M60 (pardon) all co-occur: seeking here is the central verb linking discernment, justice, and truth as the qualities being sought in a person, with successful finding leading to the pardon outcome -- seeking functions as the connective operation between the sought virtues and the resulting mercy.

6686.text: M47 (heart) co-occurs: seeking (with H1875 as intensifying parallel) is qualified by 'with all your heart', making the heart-characteristic the qualifying condition for the seeking to succeed in finding.

6687.text: M42 (declares -- prophetic-speech term) and M03 (weeping) co-occur: the seeking of the Lord here is embedded within a prophetic declaration and accompanied by penitential weeping, so seeking functions as the culminating covenantal act within a broader repentance scene framed by prophetic speech and lament.

6688.text: M42 (declares), M56 (iniquity/sin) and M60 (pardon) co-occur: here seeking functions ironically as a search for guilt that returns nothing, because M60 (pardon) has already removed the M56 object being sought -- seeking's role is to demonstrate the totality of the pardon by finding no sin left to find.

6689.text: M76 (wandering/straying) and M22 (height, 'high hill') co-occur alongside H1875 (also home cluster): the negated seeking (paired with H1875) is presented as the direct remedy that ought to have addressed the sheep's wandering (M76) but did not -- seeking's absence is causally tied to the wandering's continuation.

6690.text: Building on H1245's note for this verse: M47 (heart) qualifies both seeking terms jointly here, but darash's own contribution is the intensifying, wholehearted-devotion register it adds on top of baqash's general seeking, together forming a doubled emphasis on total-hearted pursuit of God as the condition for finding.

6691.text: Building on H1245's note for this verse: darash's own vantage adds the specifically pastoral-care dimension to the negated search -- it is not just general seeking (H1245) but the diligent shepherding-inquiry (H1875) that is absent, doubling the indictment of the shepherds' neglect toward the wandering (M76) sheep.

6705.text: In Dan.8.15 'sought to understand' sits squarely within the base gloss of seeking-to-find/secure understanding; no notable divergence from the general sense.

6706.text: In Dan.9.3 'seeking him by prayer' matches the base sense of seeking God's face/favour devotionally; no divergent nuance.

6707.text: In Hos.5.6 'seek the Lord' with flocks/herds is the standard devotional-seeking sense, ironically undermined by the following clause (they will not find him); the divergence is contextual/theological, not lexical -- the base gloss itself holds.

6708.text: In Nah.3.11 'seek a refuge' is a concrete, physical-safety sense of seeking, within the base semantic range (seeking to secure); no unusual shift.

6709.text: In Zeph.1.6 'do not seek the Lord' is the standard devotional-negative sense; base gloss holds without special nuance.

6710.text: In Zech.8.22 'seek the Lord of hosts' is the standard devotional-pilgrimage sense; no divergence from base gloss.

6711.text: In Zech.12.9 'seek to destroy' shifts the verb toward a hostile, military-intent sense (paired with an infinitive of destruction) rather than the more common devotional or cognitive seeking; this idiomatic pairing ('seek to X') functions as an auxiliary of intent/resolve, a notable nuance compared to Dan.8.15's cognitive seeking or Zech.8.22's devotional seeking.

6712.text: In Mal.2.7 'people should seek instruction' is within the base sense of seeking to obtain/receive (here, teaching from a priest's mouth); no notable divergence.

6713.text: In Dan.8.15 the operation-tagged word 'stood' (H5975G, role-T3) is performed by the vision-figure ('one having the appearance of a man') and directed toward Daniel ('before me') -- Daniel is simultaneously the one seeking (H1245) understanding, so the seeking-party and the recipient-of-standing-presence are the same person, tightly linking the operation to the seeking party.

6714.text: In Dan.9.3 the operation 'turned' (H5414H, role-T3) is initiated by Daniel (the speaker) and directed toward 'the Lord God' -- this operation is the physical/postural counterpart of the seeking (H1245) named in the same clause; Daniel initiates both toward God.

6715.text: In Hos.5.6 the operation 'go' (H1980G, role-T3) is initiated by 'they' (Israel, with flocks/herds) and directed 'to' the Lord -- the same party who then performs the seeking (H1245); the movement operation and the seeking are enacted by the same initiator toward the same divine object, though the following clause states they will not find him.

6716.text: In Dan.8.15 the co-occurring M-code M15 ('understand', H0998) names the object of the seeking (H1245 sought to understand) -- seeking here functions as the operative pursuit whose target is understanding; the two M-codes are directly linked as verb-and-object of one cognitive act.

6717.text: In Dan.9.3 M42 (prayer, H8605) and M42 (pleas for mercy, H8469) co-occur as the means/instruments by which the seeking (H1245) of God is carried out -- seeking is the overarching disposition/act, prayer and supplication are its expressed vehicles.

6718.text: In Hos.5.6 M45 (withdrawn, H2502A) describes God's own action AFTER the seeking fails -- seeking (H1245) is the human approach that proves futile, and the other M-code marks the divine response of withdrawal; the two characteristics stand in ironic tension rather than mutual support.

6719.text: In Nah.3.11 M14 (hiding, H5956) and M19 (refuge, H4581) co-occur with seeking (H1245): the party first hides, then seeks a refuge from the enemy -- seeking here is the active pursuit of the safety that hiding only partially achieves; the M-codes form a sequence of self-preservation acts.

6720.text: In Zeph.1.6 H1245 co-occurs only with its own cluster-sibling H1875 (inquire) -- no other M-code characteristic besides the two home strongs of this cluster is present.

6721.text: In Zech.8.22 M23 (strong, H6099, qualifying 'nations'), M72 (hosts, H6635B), and M03/M21/M73 (entreat, H2470B) co-occur; seeking (H1245) is the overarching pilgrimage-act, while 'entreat the favor' names a parallel, intensified act of supplication toward the same divine object -- the two acts (seek / entreat favor) form a synonymous escalating pair rather than opposing forces.

6722.text: In Zech.12.9 M10 (destroy, H8045) co-occurs directly as the infinitive object of seeking (H1245 seek to destroy) -- here seeking functions as the volitional resolve driving a destructive act, a rare hostile-intent pairing for this characteristic.

6723.text: In Mal.2.7 M36 (priest, H3548), M74 (guard, H8104H), M15 (knowledge, H1847), M54 (instruction, H8451), and M65 (mouth, H6310G) co-occur; seeking (H1245) here names the people's proper act of obtaining instruction, complementing the priest's duty to guard knowledge -- the M-codes together depict a reciprocal teaching relationship (priest guards/gives, people seek/receive).

6737.text: In Zeph.1.6 'inquire of him' is squarely the devotional consult-God sense of darash; no notable divergence from base gloss.

6738.text: In Ps.109.10 'seeking food' applies darash to a base survival need (foraging among ruins) rather than its more common devotional/investigative sense (consulting God, studying) -- a notable contextual narrowing to literal physical foraging, distinct from Eccl.1.13's intellectual application of the same root.

6739.text: In Eccl.1.13 'to seek and to search out by wisdom' pairs darash with H8446 (search out) in an intensified, intellectual/philosophical sense -- applying the term to comprehensive investigation of 'all that is done under heaven' rather than a devotional or physical-need sense, a notable extension compared to Ps.109.10's foraging use.
