15529.text: G5293 hypotassō: Faces in batch 5: submit yourselves to God · be subject to the Father of spirits · do not submit to God's righteousness · the flesh cannot submit · subject to authorities, masters, husbands, leaders, one another · the spirits of prophets subject to prophets · demons subject in his name · creation subjected not willingly · all things subjected to Christ · the Son subjected to the Father · the boy Jesus submissive; What differs: who is under whom, and whether willingly. Freely and for a ground (to God, for the Lord's sake). By refusal (Rom 10:3). By inability (Rom 8:7). By power (demons, all things). Against its will (creation). And the Son, of his own accord, to his parents and finally to the Father.

15602.text: Points that follow from the scan, with no reading done: ʿānî (H6041) is the partner of ʿānāw and of "poor and needy". It shares 32 verses with M09. 15608.text: Verses that are a source in the claims register: Count: 4 (Luk 16:22, Psa 34:18, 2Ch 7:14, Phili 2:8).

15625.text: G4239 / G4235 praus, praos: Gloss: gentle; Tagged: M05; Verses: 4 / 1; Shared with M09: 0 / 1; Cited: 1 / 1; Surface that bears on M09: humble, meek (Mat 5:5; 11:29).

15644.text: In the NT the one who humbles himself is any person. What follows is named as: "justified" (Luk 18:14); "grace" (Jam 4:6); "exalt you … at the proper time" (1Pe 5:6); "rest for your souls" (Mat 11:29).

15649.text: In the NT a new ground is named: Christ, and Christ's own way: "Have this mind among yourselves, which is yours in Christ Jesus" (Phili 2:5); "Christ also suffered for you, leaving you an example" (1Pe 2:21); "out of reverence for Christ" (Eph 5:21); "by the meekness and gentleness of Christ" (2Cor 10:1); "learn from me, for I am gentle and lowly in heart" (Mat 11:29).

15653.text: He is the ground and the example for humility toward others. Phili 2:3–5 makes "in humility count others more significant" rest on "this mind … in Christ Jesus". Also 1Pe 2:21; Eph 5:21; 2Cor 10:1; Mat 11:29.

15658.text: In the Son: in the form of God, "emptied himself … humbled himself … obedient to the point of death" (Phili 2:6–8); "gentle and lowly in heart" (Mat 11:29); "made lower than the angels", crowned "because of the suffering of death" (Heb 2:9); "submissive to them" (Luk 2:51); "the Son himself will also be subjected" (1Cor 15:28); the humble king (Mat 21:5); his humiliation, silent (Act 8:32–33).

15660.text: 13.1 already holds Dan 4:17 and 4:37 (Willing), Psa 51:16–17 (Delight), Jam 4:4–6 (Jealousy) and Isa 58:3, 5 (Choosing). None is placed for God's lowering.

15669.text: A humbling God does not accept: OT: the fast with "your own pleasure": "Why have we humbled ourselves, and you take no knowledge of it?" (Isa 58:3); NT: "self-made religion and asceticism" that leaves one "puffed up" (Col 2:18, 23); the Pharisee's "I fast twice a week" (Luk 18:12).

15672.text: God lowering himself: OT: "who looks far down on the heavens and the earth? He raises the poor" (Psa 113:6–7); "though the Lord is high, he regards the lowly" (Psa 138:6); "I dwell … also with him who is of a contrite and lowly spirit" (Isa 57:15); "your gentleness made me great" (2Sa 22:36); NT: "who, though he was in the form of God … emptied himself … humbled himself" (Phili 2:6–8); "I am gentle and lowly in heart" (Mat 11:29).

15673.text: Mat 11:29: What it says of him: "I am gentle and lowly in heart", his own word on his heart.

15747.text: Dominating H6184's 15 verses, cruelty is the property of oppressors and adversaries named from the position of the sufferer asking to be delivered from them: redeem me from the hand of the ruthless (Job 6:23); a band of ruthless men seeks my life (Ps 86:14); redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless (Jer 15:21).

15817.text: In Psalm 34:4-6 and 69:29-33 the poor man cries, and is heard: this poor man cried, and the Lord heard him and saved him out of all his troubles (34:4, 6); I am afflicted and in pain, the Lord hears the needy (69:29, 33). The poor man is the one who speaks, and his fear is among what he is delivered from (34:4).

15842.text: Soul/life and fear: Fear *for* one's life: Jos 9:24; Eze 32:10; 1Sa 22:23; The right object of fear is defined by the soul: "do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather fear him who can destroy both soul and body" (Mat 10:28); "awe came upon every soul" (Act 2:43); "fearfully and wonderfully made … my soul knows it very well" (Psa 139:14)

15846.text: Inner vs outer: "our bodies had no rest … fighting without and fear within" (2Co 7:5).; Revisit 2026-09-28: in context (2Co 2:12–13 → 7:5–7, 13) this is one step in the spirit's rest through persons: restless at Titus's absence, comforted by his coming. See Batch F §9.4.

15870.text: Spirit [H]: "his spirit was troubled" — after dreams (Gen 41:8; Dan 2:1, 3). Dreams trouble the spirit; the brief §6 notes dream words sit in T2.; "Jesus was troubled in his spirit" (Joh 13:21); "deeply moved in his spirit and greatly troubled" at others' weeping (Joh 11:33); "he sighed deeply in his spirit" (Mar 8:12)

15915.text: God searching the anxious heart: "Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts [anxious thoughts]" (Psa 139:23) [lexical].

15920.text: Fainting across every component: heart: "the whole heart faint" // "the whole head is sick" (Isa 1:5); Lam 1:22; Psa 61:2; spirit [H]: Psa 142:3; 143:4; "When I remember God, I moan; when I meditate, my spirit faints" (Psa 77:3); soul: "hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted within them" (Psa 107:5); flesh: "my flesh faints for you" (Psa 63:1); life: "When my life was fainting away, I remembered the Lord, and my prayer came to you" (Jon 2:7) — fainting turns into remembering and prayer; Revisit 2026-09-28: In the same book, Jonah "was faint" under the east wind and asked to die (Jon 4:8). Fainting in ch. 2 turns to prayer; fainting in ch. 4 turns to a death-wish (Batch G §6).; For spirit-fainting in meditation (Psa 77:3), memory works either way: it deepens the fainting (Psa 77) or turns it (Psa 42:6). See Batch F §9.4.; bosom: "their life is poured out on their mothers' bosom" (Lam 2:12)

15922.text: Self-affliction of the nephesh (fasting, Day of Atonement): "you shall afflict yourselves" (Lev 16:29, 31; 23:27, 32; Num 29:7); "Why have we humbled ourselves?" (Isa 58:3, 5); "I afflicted myself with fasting" (Psa 35:13); a vow "to afflict herself" (Num 30:13).

15940.text: 1.2 Attention — setting the heart (see §0.1): "Consider your ways" = set your heart on your ways.; "set your heart to understand" (Dan 10:12); "apply my heart to know wisdom" (Ecc 1:17; 7:25; 8:16); "Take to heart all the words" (Deu 32:46); The failure case: "it burned him up, but he did not take it to heart" (Isa 42:25).

15944.text: 1.4 God knows, tests and searches the heart: "you, you only, know the hearts of all the children of mankind" (1Ki 8:39; 2Ch 6:30); "he knows the secrets of the heart" (Psa 44:21); "God knows your hearts" (Luk 16:15); "Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts!" (Psa 139:23); "he who searches mind and heart" (Rev 2:23); "testing you to know what was in your heart" (Deu 8:2; 2Ch 32:31; Deu 13:3 "with all your heart and with all your soul")

15947.text: 1.5 The soul in knowing: "my soul knows it very well" (Psa 139:14); "knowledge will be pleasant to your soul" (Pro 2:10); "wisdom is such to your soul" (Pro 24:14); "Whoever gets sense loves his own soul" (Pro 19:8); Revisit 2026-09-28: Pro 19:8 is the wisdom side of loving or hating one's own soul. In the Gospels the valuation reverses (Joh 12:25). See Batch F §3.; "take counsel in my soul" (Psa 13:2); In the NT, psychē is rendered "minds" (Act 14:2 "poisoned their minds"; 15:24 "unsettling your minds").; [Claude reading] The soul *receives* knowledge as something pleasant or nourishing, rather than being the one who investigates.

15954.text: Inner inquiry in sequence: "let me meditate in my heart.' Then my spirit made a diligent search" (Psa 77:6). The heart meditates, then the spirit searches.

15957.text: 1.7 God's Spirit as the source of knowledge [D]: "the Spirit of wisdom and understanding … of knowledge and the fear of the Lord" (Isa 11:2); "filled him with the Spirit of God, with ability and intelligence, with knowledge and all craftsmanship" (Exo 31:3; 35:31); "through the Spirit the utterance of wisdom … of knowledge" (1Co 12:8); "the Spirit searches everything … the natural person does not accept the things of the Spirit … they are spiritually discerned" (1Co 2:10–14); "the Holy Spirit will teach you" (Luk 12:12; Joh 14:26); "we do not know what to pray for … but the Spirit himself intercedes" (Rom 8:26); "he who searches hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit" (Rom 8:27)

15969.text: 2.4 Wisdom entering and staying: "wisdom will come into your heart" (Pro 2:10); "Wisdom rests in the heart of a man of understanding" (Pro 14:33); Revisit 2026-09-28: *nûaḥ* "rest" has three residents: wisdom in the heart of the understanding (Pro 14:33), anger in the heart of fools (Ecc 7:9), the Spirit upon the prophet (Num 11:25; Isa 11:2). See Batch F §9.5.; "teach us to number our days that we may get a heart of wisdom" (Psa 90:12); "I searched with my heart how to cheer my body with wine — my heart still guiding me with wisdom" (Ecc 2:3) — the heart guiding the body's experiment

15983.text: Collapse: "as soon as we heard it, our hearts melted, and there was no spirit left in any man" (Jos 2:11; 5:1) [H]; "I hear the sound of the trumpet … my heart is beating wildly" (Jer 4:19); "his wife told him these things, and his heart died within him" (1Sa 25:37); Revisit 2026-09-28: the verse before has "Nabal's heart was merry within him, for he was very drunk … she told him nothing … until the morning" (25:36). The news lands on a heart that was merry the night before. See the threshold pattern in Batch F §7, and Abigail's speech (25:29–31) in Batch G §9.3.; Revisit 2026-09-28: "our hearts melted … there was no spirit left in any man" (Jos 2:11) and "every heart will melt … every spirit will faint" (Eze 21:7) have their law-code counterpart in "lest he make the heart of his fellows melt like his own" (Deu 20:8). A heart's collapse spreads to other hearts (Batch F §6).; "Because of the news … every heart will melt … every spirit will faint" (Eze 21:7); "Let not your heart faint … at the report" (Jer 51:46)

15990.text: Inner speech unheard by people: "Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved, and her voice was not heard" (1Sa 1:13); Revisit 2026-09-28 (context 1Sa 1:7–18, Batch G §8.2): Before: she weeps and will not eat; "why is your heart sad?" (7–8). The prayer comes "after they had eaten and drunk" (9).; After: Eli takes her for drunk (14). She answers in exact inner vocabulary: "a woman troubled in spirit … pouring out my soul before the Lord" (15). Then "Go in peace", and "her face was no longer sad" (17–18).; [Claude reading] Unheard heart-speech is misread by a human hearer as drunkenness, the merry-heart state (Batch F §7), and is heard by God. It is the sad-heart counter-case to the merry heart at a feast.

16010.text: Remembering weighs on the soul: "My soul continually remembers it and is bowed down within me" (Lam 3:20); "I have forgotten what happiness is" (Lam 3:17); "These things I remember, as I pour out my soul" (Psa 42:4, 6).; Revisit 2026-09-28 (contexts Psa 42:4–7 and Psa 77:2–4, Batch F §9.4): memory works either way. In Psa 42 remembering is the turn ("My soul is cast down … therefore I remember you"). In Psa 77 remembering God deepens the fainting of the spirit. "Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not" (Psa 103:2) is one of the self-addresses to the soul, now found in five settings (Batch F §15; Batch G §3.2).

16012.text: Remembering and the spirit: "When I remember God, I moan; when I meditate, my spirit faints" (Psa 77:3); "Let me remember my song … meditate in my heart. Then my spirit made a diligent search" (Psa 77:6) [H].

16052.text: Psa 69:32 (filed under "you who seek God, let your hearts revive"): seeing God's help to the humble

16053.text: Psa 22:26 (filed under "The afflicted shall eat and be satisfied … May your hearts live forever"): eating before God

16059.text: How revival shifts [Claude reading]: what revives the spirit depends on what exhausted it: thirst → water; disbelief → words with evidence; lowliness → God's presence; grief → a comforter (in Lam 1:16, missing); The heart "lives" by eating before God (Psa 22:26). This is the positive face of the eating–heart link in Batch F §7.

16079.text: The formula: "as the Lord lives and as your soul lives" (1Sa 20:3; 25:26; 2Sa 11:11); "as the Lord lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you" (2Ki 2:2, 4, 6; 4:30); "As your soul lives, O king, I do not know" (1Sa 17:55); "As you live, my lord" (1Sa 1:26; 2Sa 14:19); "As the Lord lives, who has redeemed my soul out of every adversity" (1Ki 1:29; 2Sa 4:9); "As the Lord lives, who made our souls" (Jer 38:16); "As God lives, … who has made my soul bitter" (Job 27:2); [lexical; Claude reading] The oath sets the other person's *nephesh* beside the Lord's own life as the thing that guarantees the word. To swear by someone's soul is to stake one's word on their life. In the second form, the Lord is identified by what he has done to the soul: redeemed it, made it, made it bitter.

16084.text: Jer 38:14–24 | "hide nothing from me" (14); "will you not surely put me to death?" (15) | Zedekiah "swore secretly, 'As the Lord lives, who made our souls, I will not put you to death'" (16) | "your life shall be spared" if you surrender (17, 20); "I am afraid" (19); "Let no one know of these words, and you shall not die" (24)

16085.text: What the sequences show [Claude reading]: The oath marks adherence at a cost.; Elisha's triple oath is the price of the double spirit.; The Shunammite uses Elisha's own oath against him. Her bitterness of soul becomes a hold on the prophet that he cannot refuse.; Uriah's oath by David's soul is kept against David's wish. The wine that should have lowered his guard fails (a failed threshold — Batch F §7). He dies for keeping it.; The oath by the soul can guard a life while refusing a life. Zedekiah swears secretly by "who made our souls" to spare Jeremiah's life. He then declines the life offered to him (38:17, 20), from fear (38:19). The oath and the refusal are in one conversation.; 1Sa 17:55 stands on the threshold of 18:1. A formal oath by Saul's soul immediately precedes the knitting of Jonathan's soul to David's.; The oath misused: "As the Lord lives, I will run after him and get something from him" (Gehazi, 2Ki 5:20; §13.2).; Revisit (Batch H): God swears by his own soul: "The Lord God has sworn by himself [*his nephesh*]" (Amo 6:8; Jer 51:14; read in Batch D and E). The oath by a *nephesh* is used of God as well as of men.; The oath answers a claim of vengeance. The murderers of Ish-bosheth: "your enemy, who sought your life. The Lord has avenged my lord the king" (2Sa 4:8). David: "As the Lord lives, who has redeemed my life out of every adversity" → he has them killed (4:9–12). The oath on David's own redeemed soul refuses a vengeance done on his behalf (Batch H §1.4).; Revisit (delta) — the oath with death in view: The oath formula frames the nearness of death. "But truly, as the Lord lives and as your soul lives, there is but a step between me and death" (1Sa 20:3). The oath by Jonathan's soul carries David's own peril.; A life pledged for a life. Rahab asks: "swear to me by the Lord … deliver our lives from death" (Jos 2:12–13). The spies answer: "Our life for yours even to death!" (2:14). They do not swear by the Lord's life. They pledge their own *nephesh*.; An oath on a life, broken after a spirit comes (context 1Sa 19:4–12): Jonathan: "he took his life in his hand and struck down the Philistine … Why then will you sin against innocent blood?" (5); "Saul listened … Saul swore, 'As the Lord lives, he shall not be put to death'" (6); War again; David's victory (8); "a harmful spirit from the Lord came upon Saul" (9) [O]

16097.text: 5.5 The soul's life and its failure to be satisfied: "lives many years … but his soul is not satisfied with life's good things" (Ecc 6:3); "the life of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of the living in the care of the Lord" (1Sa 25:29) — see §9.3 for its sequel (25:31)

16174.text: 16.3 The heart and soul measured against death: "I find something more bitter than death: the woman whose heart is snares and nets" (Ecc 7:26). The context is the searcher's own heart: "I turned my heart to know … the foolishness that is madness" (7:25).; [Claude reading] One heart searching finds another heart as the trap. A heart set with snares is worse than death.; "His greed [*nephesh*] is as wide as Sheol; like death he has never enough" (Hab 2:5). It follows directly on "his soul is puffed up" (2:4; §5.5).; [Claude reading] Here the soul is compared with death as appetite. Both swallow and are never satisfied.

16184.text: The heart's condition as the cause of death — wisdom and sayings: "fools die for lack of sense [*heart*]" (Pro 10:21); "Whoever keeps the commandment keeps his life; he who despises his ways will die" (Pro 19:16); "he who fails to find me injures himself [*his soul*]; all who hate me love death" (Pro 8:36; Batch F §3.1); "The godless in heart cherish anger … They die in youth" (Job 36:13–14); "the hearts of the children of man are full of evil, and madness is in their hearts while they live, and after that they go to the dead" (Ecc 9:3) → "a living dog is better than a dead lion. For the living know that they will die" (9:4–5); "Discipline your son, for there is hope; do not set your heart on putting him to death" (Pro 19:18) [lexical: *nephesh*]; "Another dies in bitterness of soul, never having tasted of prosperity. They lie down alike in the dust" (Job 21:25–26). Here the soul's state at death makes no difference to the outcome. This is Job's counter to the wisdom sayings above.; "I will strike her children dead. And all the churches will know that I am he who searches mind and heart" (Rev 2:23). The death is the evidence that the heart is searched.

16211.text: 16.10 Life risked "to death" for others — the OT precedent: "Zebulun is a people who risked their lives to the death" (Judg 5:18). This is in the same song as "March on, my soul, with might!" (5:21; §3.2).; "Our life for yours even to death!" (Jos 2:14; §4 revisit); David "took his life in his hand" against the Philistine (1Sa 19:5); The men to David: "If half of us die, they will not care [*set heart*] about us. But you are worth ten thousand of us" (2Sa 18:3). The enemy's heart is indifferent to many deaths. One life is weighed at ten thousand.; "the men who were seeking your life are dead" (Exo 4:19) → Moses returns (4:20). The death of the hunters frees the hunted life.; "Why then are you laying a trap for my life to bring about my death?" (1Sa 28:9). This is the medium to the disguised Saul.; "we are about to bring great disaster upon ourselves [*our souls*]" (Jer 26:19). To put the prophet to death would harm the souls of those who kill him. It is set against Hezekiah, who "feared the Lord … and the Lord relented".; [Claude reading] Batch F §3.2 read "hating one's life" and "not loving one's life unto death" as NT discipleship. The OT already has the same shape in battle and in covenant pledges: the life risked "to the death" for a people, a household or a king. What the NT adds is the object, "for the name of the Lord Jesus" (Act 21:13), and the example, "poured out his soul to death" (Isa 53:12).

16214.text: A dead man honoured for his grandfather's heart: Ahaziah "was put to death. They buried him, for they said, 'He is the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord with all his heart'" (2Ch 22:9)

16258.text: 1.5 The Spirit prays, cries and intercedes — divine speech in the human seat: "God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, 'Abba! Father!'" (Gal 4:6) [D1] — the cry sounds in the heart; "the Spirit of adoption as sons, by whom we cry, 'Abba! Father!'" (Rom 8:15) [X+D1] — the same cry, now ours; "the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words" (Rom 8:26) [D1]; "he who searches hearts knows what is the mind of the Spirit, because the Spirit intercedes for the saints" (Rom 8:27) [D2]

16262.text: 1.5 The Spirit prays, cries and intercedes — divine speech in the human seat: [Claude reading] Gal 4:6 and Rom 8:15 describe one cry from two sides: the Spirit cries in our hearts, and we cry by the Spirit. Rom 8:26–27 then locates the Spirit's intercession within the heart that God "searches". This is the fullest statement of divine-human co-agency in the batch.

16272.text: The soul-life as prize: "I will give you your life as a prize of war" (Jer 45:5; 39:18, "because you have put your trust in me").

16282.text: Asking for the way; rest for souls: "ask for the ancient paths … and find rest for your souls" (Jer 6:16).

16318.text: 4.1 Serving with all the heart and all the soul: "to serve the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul" (Deu 10:12; 11:13; Jos 22:5); "serve him with a whole heart and with a willing mind [*soul*], for the Lord searches all hearts" (1Ch 28:9); "serve him faithfully with all your heart" (1Sa 12:24; 12:20); "direct your heart to the Lord and serve him only" (1Sa 7:3)

16321.text: Service carried out "with all his heart": "every work … in the service of the house of God … he did with all his heart" (2Ch 31:21)

16323.text: 4.2 Worship in spirit: "God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth" (Joh 4:24); "the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth" (Joh 4:23) [D1+H2]; "who worship by the Spirit of God … and put no confidence in the flesh" (Phili 3:3) [D1]; "God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit" (Rom 1:9) [H1]; "the ministry of the Spirit" (2Co 3:8); "written … with the Spirit of the living God … on tablets of human hearts" (2Co 3:3); "present your bodies as a living sacrifice … your spiritual worship" (Rom 12:1, d0)

16380.text: Made with heart and soul: "to keep his commandments … with all his heart and all his soul" (2Ki 23:3; 2Ch 34:31); "a covenant to seek the Lord … with all their heart and with all their soul" (2Ch 15:12); "Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the Lord" (2Ch 29:10)

16393.text: 7.3 Fellowship, assembly, sharing: "all the churches will know that I am he who searches mind and heart" (Rev 2:23); "the assembly of the firstborn … and to the spirits of the righteous made perfect" (Heb 12:23) [H2]; "the Spirit of the Lord came upon Jahaziel … in the midst of the assembly" (2Ch 20:14) [D1]; "I have not hidden your deliverance within my heart … from the great congregation" (Psa 40:10)

16397.text: 8.1 God tests the heart: "I know, my God, that you test the heart" (1Ch 29:17); "I the Lord search the heart and test the mind" (Jer 17:10); "the Lord tests hearts" — like crucible and furnace (Pro 17:3); "Search me, O God, and know my heart! Try me and know my thoughts!" (Psa 139:23); "Prove me, O Lord, and try me; test my heart and my mind" (Psa 26:2); "You have tried my heart … you will find nothing" (Psa 17:3); "you who test the minds and hearts" (Psa 7:9; Jer 11:20; 20:12); "you … test my heart toward you" (Jer 12:3); "God who tests our hearts" (1Th 2:4); "testing you to know what was in your heart" (Deu 8:2); "the Lord your God is testing you, to know whether you love … with all your heart and with all your soul" (Deu 13:3); "God left him to himself, in order to test him and to know all that was in his heart" (2Ch 32:31)

16419.text: Restless spirit, leaving: "my spirit was not at rest because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I took leave" (2Co 2:13) [H1].

16465.text: Saving and losing the soul: "whoever would save his life will lose it" (Mat 16:25; Mar 8:35; Luk 9:24; 17:33); "what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world and forfeits his soul? Or what shall a man give in return for his soul?" (Mat 16:26; Mar 8:36); "to save life or to destroy it?" (Luk 6:9; Mar 3:4); "receive … the implanted word, which is able to save your souls" (Jam 1:21)

16473.text: The soul satisfied: "My soul will be satisfied as with fat and rich food" (Psa 63:5); "he satisfies the longing soul" (Psa 107:9); "if you pour yourself out for the hungry and satisfy the desire [*nephesh*] of the afflicted" (Isa 58:10) — pouring out one's own nephesh to satisfy another's; "satisfy your desire in scorched places" (Isa 58:11); "Out of the anguish of his soul he shall see and be satisfied" (Isa 53:11); "I will feast the soul of the priests" (Jer 31:14); "The afflicted shall eat and be satisfied … May your hearts live forever!" (Psa 22:26)

16479.text: Comfort: "my soul refuses to be comforted" (Psa 77:2); "When the cares of my heart are many, your consolations cheer my soul" (Psa 94:19) — heart burdened, soul cheered; "a comforter is far from me, one to revive my spirit [*soul*]" (Lam 1:16); "Reproaches have broken my heart … for comforters, but I found none" (Psa 69:20); God's heart: "How can I give you up, O Ephraim? … My heart recoils within me; my compassion grows warm and tender" (Hos 11:8)

16486.text: Beatitudes of the inner seat: "Blessed are the poor in spirit" (Mat 5:3) [H1]; "Blessed are the pure in heart" (Mat 5:8); "Blessed is the man … in whose spirit there is no deceit" (Psa 32:2) [H1]; "Blessed are those … who seek him with their whole heart" (Psa 119:2); "Blessed are those whose strength is in you, in whose heart are the highways to Zion" (Psa 84:5) — the heart as a road; "Blessed is the one who fears the Lord always, but whoever hardens his heart will fall into calamity" (Pro 28:14); "Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah! For flesh and blood has not revealed this to you" (Mat 16:17)

16491.text: 13. Cross-cutting observations for Batch E [Claude reading]: Relating to God engages the whole inner seat, and the texts say so by formula.; "With all your heart and with all your soul" governs: serving (Deu 10:12; Jos 22:5); keeping the law and renewing the covenant (2Ki 23:3; 2Ch 34:31; Deu 30:10); loving after circumcision of heart (Deu 30:6); praying and returning (1Ki 8:48); being tested (Deu 13:3); "With my whole heart" governs thanks, praise, crying and seeking.; The formula also appears of God (Jer 32:41).; The heart is where the relation to God is located, examined and known.; It prays without voice (1Sa 1:13) and cries (Lam 2:18).; It holds the law (Psa 37:31) and trusts (Psa 28:7).; It believes (Rom 10:10) and is circumcised (Deu 30:6).; It is the organ God tests (§8.1). Knowing hearts is the ground of God's forgiveness (1Ki 8:39) and of his giving the Spirit (Act 15:8).; Where heart and lips diverge, the lips do not count (Hos 7:14; Isa 29:13).; The soul is the self in address. It is spoken to by its owner ("Bless the Lord, O my soul"; "Why are you cast down, O my soul"), and asked to be spoken to by God ("Say to my soul, 'I am your salvation'", Psa 35:3). It is also the life that is: asked for (Est 7:3; 1Ki 17:21); asked to die (1Ki 19:4; Jon 4:8); redeemed, ransomed and atoned for (§9.1, §11.1); delivered or lost (§11.3); The human spirit is most active in this batch.; It prays and sings apart from the mind (1Co 14:14–16).; It serves (Rom 1:9) and worships in spirit (Joh 4:23–24).; It rejoices in the Savior (Luk 1:47) and is renewed (Eze 36:26; Eph 4:23).; It receives the benediction "grace be with your spirit".; At death it is the part committed to God (Psa 31:5; Luk 23:46; Act 7:59; Mat 27:50).; Its complaint voices anguish (Job 7:11), and its brokenness blocks hearing (Exo 6:9).; The divine Spirit relates to God on the person's behalf.; It cries "Abba" in the heart (Gal 4:6) and intercedes within the searched heart (Rom 8:26–27).; It bears witness (Heb 10:15) and writes on hearts (2Co 3:3).; It circumcises the heart (Rom 2:29) and renews (Tit 3:5).; It gives faith and gifts (1Co 12:9; Gal 3:2) and speaks through the prophet (2Sa 23:2).; It can itself be tested (Act 5:9), resisted (Act 7:51) and outraged (Heb 10:29).; Other spirits relate to God too, and are judged by that relation.

16726.text: 11. Cross-cutting observations for Batch D [Claude reading]: Moral condition is predicated above all of the heart. The heart is: upright, whole, pure, clean or blameless (§1); evil, crooked, perverse, twisted, false or double (§2, §4, §5); proud / high or humbled / tender (§9, §10); It is also where sin is stored, engraved or hidden (§3.3). God tests and weighs it (Psa 7:9; Pro 21:2; Luk 16:15; Act 15:8). The heart is the organ that is morally evaluated.; The soul (*nephesh*) is the accountable person and the life at stake.; It sins, realises guilt, bears iniquity and is cut off (§3.1). It is the unfaithful party (§5).; It is the life that righteousness delivers (§1.7) and that sin injures (§3.2).; It is the innocent blood that is shed (§1.7). It is afflicted on holy days (§7.5).; At the limit it is the corpse that defiles (§8.2).; The soul is less often *evaluated* (righteous soul: 2Pe 2:8; puffed-up soul: Hab 2:4) than *answerable*.; The human spirit is evaluated chiefly on the pride–humility axis (§9.2, §10.2): haughty, proud, hardened, lowly, poor, contrite. Otherwise it is: without deceit (Psa 32:2); right / clean (Psa 51:10); faithful in marriage (Mal 2:15–16); trustworthy (Pro 11:13); holy or defiled with the body (1Co 7:34; 2Co 7:1); sanctified with soul and body (1Th 5:23); perfected in the righteous dead (Heb 12:23); weighed (Pro 16:2); broken by a perverse tongue (Pro 15:4); [observation, not a count]; Other spirits carry the negative moral adjectives. They are evil / harmful (§2.1, 15 verses), unclean (§8.1, 23 verses) and lying / deceitful (§4.1, 6 verses). They are the moral clusters' names turned into kinds of spirit.; In the OT some are sent by God (1Sa 16; Judg 9:23; 1Ki 22:22–23).; In the NT they indwell and are cast out.; The Holy Spirit is the positive counterpart, and the one against whom human sin is directed: blasphemed, lied to, grieved, resisted, outraged (§2.4, §4.2, §7.1).; Inner vs outer purity.; Ritual clean / unclean / holy vocabulary attaches to flesh, body and *nephesh*-as-person or corpse.; Moral purity attaches to heart, spirit, soul and conscience.; Several texts deliberately contrast the two: Psa 24:4; 2Ch 30:19; Mar 7:19–21; Heb 9:13–14; 10:22; Jam 4:8.

16729.text: Held and turned: "The king's heart is a stream of water in the hand of the Lord; he turns it wherever he will" (Pro 21:1); "the Lord … had turned the heart of the king of Assyria to them" (Ezr 6:22); "who put such a thing as this into the heart of the king" (Ezr 7:27); "God has put it into their hearts … handing over their royal power to the beast" (Rev 17:17); "his wisdom, which God had put into his mind" (2Ch 9:23)

16753.text: The formula "into the hand of those who seek their life" (Jer 19:7; 21:7; 22:25; 34:20–21; 38:16; 44:30; 46:26) → Batch G §5.3.

16754.text: A reward for murder refused: the murderers of Ish-bosheth: "your enemy, who sought your life. The Lord has avenged my lord the king" (2Sa 4:8) → David: "As the Lord lives, who has redeemed my life out of every adversity" → he has them killed (4:9–12). The claim of vengeance on David's behalf is answered by an oath on David's own redeemed soul.

16774.text: Life: "surrender … your life shall be spared" (Jer 38:17); "they seek my life, to take it away" (1Ki 19:10, 14); "Why do you commit this great evil against yourselves?" (Jer 44:7)

16776.text: 1.10 ◆ Fringe (M72): "Let her lie in your arms [*bosom*], that my lord the king may be warm" (1Ki 1:2) — the king's failing body (G §8); "everyone who was in distress … and everyone who was bitter in soul, gathered to him. And he became commander over them" (1Sa 22:2) — bitterness of soul as the recruiting ground of a future king; "With him is an arm of flesh, but with us is the Lord … And the people took confidence" (2Ch 32:8), spoken "encouragingly [*to their heart*]" (32:6); "fatter in flesh than all the youths who ate the king's food" (Dan 1:15) → §7.6; "the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh" (Dan 2:11); "Our flesh is as the flesh of our brothers … yet we are forcing our sons … to be slaves … it is not in our power to help it" (Neh 5:5) → §3; "the kings … their hearts melted and there was no longer any spirit in them" (Jos 5:1) [H2]; "the souls of those who had been beheaded … came to life and reigned with Christ" (Rev 20:4); "the king … had sackcloth beneath on his body" (2Ki 6:30) — hidden grief under royal clothes

16794.text: 3.2 The servant's inner sentence: "if that servant says to himself [*in his heart*], 'My master is delayed,' and begins to beat the … servants, and to eat and drink and get drunk" (Luk 12:45; Mat 24:48–49). Context read: Luk 12:42–46; Mat 24:49–51.; The faithful manager feeds the household "at the proper time" (Luk 12:42).; The unfaithful servant says in his heart that the master is delayed → beats → eats and drinks with drunkards → the master "will come on a day when he does not expect him" (46).; → Batch D §10 (inner speech). New here: the inner sentence is followed at once by eating and drinking, then the sudden arrival (§7.6).

16796.text: Moses' burden, then the Spirit shared. Context read: Num 11:10–17.; "why … you lay the burden of all this people on me?" (11); "Did I conceive all this people? … Carry them in your bosom" (12); "kill me at once … that I may not see my wretchedness" (15); "I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them, and they shall bear the burden … with you" (17) [D2]; [Claude reading] Despair under a burden (like Batch G §6) is answered by distributing the Spirit, not by removing the burden.

16816.text: 5.1 Guarding one's own inner seat: "Keep your heart with all vigilance, for from it flow the springs of life" (Pro 4:23). Context 4:20–27 — the guarding moves outward: words kept "within your heart" (21) → "life … and healing to all their flesh" (22); keep the heart (23); → the mouth: "put away … crooked speech" (24); → the eyes: "look directly forward" (25); → the feet: "Ponder the path of your feet" (26–27); "take care, and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget … lest they depart from your heart" (Deu 4:9) — guarding the soul means guarding memory; "guard yourselves in your spirit, and let none of you be faithless to the wife of your youth" (Mal 2:15–16) [U+H1; H1]; "watch yourselves lest your hearts be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness" (Luk 21:34) → §7.6; "restore him in a spirit of gentleness. Keep watch on yourself" (Gal 6:1) [X]; "Take care lest there be an unworthy thought in your heart" (Deu 15:9); "Take care lest your heart be deceived" (Deu 11:16); "Be very careful, therefore [*guard well your souls*], to love the Lord" (Jos 23:11) — distance 0: the "careful" word *is* the nephesh phrase

16837.text: Jeremiah's sequence — context read, Jer 20:7–14: "you have deceived me" (7); "there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones … I cannot [hold it in]" (9); "my close friends, watching for my fall … 'take our revenge on him'" (10); → "let me see your vengeance … to you have I committed my cause" (12); → "Sing to the Lord; praise the Lord! For he has delivered the life of the needy" (13); → "Cursed be the day on which I was born!" (14); Jer 11:18–21 has the same prayer, and names "the men of Anathoth, who seek your life" (21).; [Claude reading]; Vengeance changes value with the heart that holds it. In the Philistines' soul it is malice. In God's heart it stands in one line with redemption (Isa 63:4). To the anxious heart it is rescue (Isa 35:4).; The prophet's heart does not take vengeance; it hands vengeance over. The friends want "our revenge" (20:10). Jeremiah asks to *see* God's (20:12). The handing over ("to you have I committed my cause") is what makes the praise of 20:13 possible. Two verses later the heart falls to cursing its birth (20:14). The inner seat swings from fire, to entrusting, to praise, to despair in five verses (cf. the despairing soul, Batch G §6).; What follows the divine heart's vengeance is complaint (Isa 63:15–17): the people ask where God's compassion has gone and why he makes them wander (§4.2).

16845.text: Shared threat as shelter. Context read: 1Sa 22:20–23. "I have occasioned the death of all the persons of your father's house" (22) → "Stay with me … for he who seeks my life seeks your life. With me you shall be in safekeeping" (23). David's guilt becomes a pledge: the one threat to both lives becomes the ground of protection.

16848.text: 7. Cross-cutting observations for Batch H [Claude reading]: The warning: "watch yourselves lest your hearts be weighed down with dissipation and drunkenness" (Luk 21:34).; The counter-statement: "the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking but of … joy in the Holy Spirit" (Rom 14:17).; David's heart reads kings rightly. The second follows immediately on Saul's oath and confession (26:21–25) (§1.8).; Voices addressed to the soul — beyond self-address (for synthesis item 1): Others speak to my soul: "Flee like a bird" (Psa 11:1); God swears by his own soul (Amo 6:8; Jer 51:14); God's soul is burdened (Isa 1:14) and avenges itself (Jer 5:9); Fringe worth keeping: the king's heart read by Joab (2Sa 14:1); bitterness of soul as the recruiting ground of a king (1Sa 22:2); the queen of Sheba's mind filled and spirit emptied (1Ki 10:2, 5); Haman's riches "worth nothing" to a heart fixed on Mordecai (Est 5:13); the soul's "burden" as its desire (Eze 24:25); Moses' despair answered by distributing the Spirit (Num 11); the watchman who delivers his own soul (Eze 33:9); Eli killed by the word "ark" (1Sa 4:18); Mary keeping what she did not understand (Luk 2:50–51); the sons of Sceva mastered by the spirit (Act 19:16); Simon's money exposing his heart (Act 8:21); the good intention set aside overnight (2Sa 7:3–5); "he who seeks my life seeks your life" (1Sa 22:23); Balaam's soul wishing for the death of the upright (Num 23:10)
